# Originators



## The Emanators

When the al-ʿAql al-Awwal (First Intellect) attained perfection from the Creator and ten envelopes of joy were placed upon it, two ⟪ar:اشباح صوریہ⟫ proceeded forward together, unaffected by this state of intimacy. Both observed the First Intellect and understood that this condition arose because it had performed tawhīd (divine unification) toward the Almighty Creator, along with tajrīd (abstraction) and tanzīh (transcendence). Witnessing this, the same state of mind manifested in both of them as in the First Intellect, and they too became creators of tawhīd toward the Almighty. Both denied divinity for themselves and all other species, humbling themselves before the Creator and acknowledging that they ⟪ar:الہ⟫ were not in a state of perfection from the outset—divinity belongs solely to the Creator. After bearing witness to the Creator's monotheism, both also acknowledged the grace and precedence of the First Intellect. With this confession, the two sprang forward together and followed the First Intellect.[^cite-1] These two beings ⟪ar:منبعثین⟫ are called the Emanators—those who emerge together.

The manifest difference between the tawhīd of the First Intellect and that of the al-Munbaʿithūn (Emanators) lay in this: the Emanators performed tawhīd by observing and following the example of the First Intellect, whereas the First Intellect performed tawhīd without any exemplar or ⟪ar:مُلحِم⟫ guide, deriving it from its own nature. In this capacity, it was called the First Intellect because it transcended itself and became a model to be followed, while the Emanators were called al-Munbaʿithūn because they advanced after witnessing the First Intellect.[^cite-2]

| First Intellect | First Emanator |
| --- | --- |
| *Ibdāʿ* (Origination) | *Inbʿāth* (Emanation) |
| Self-initiated | Following the exemplar |

The letter Alif evokes both Lam and Fa when considered in relation to the principle of definition. When Alif is written alone, it represents the original and singular, indicating the station of unity; Lam and Fa are connected and indicate that they were created together.

| Alif | Lam |
| --- | --- |
| First Intellect | Emanators |



## Existence, Dormancy, and Emanation

For an object to emanate, it must first come into existence. Nothing can be perfected unless something has existed. The al-Munbaʿithūn first came into being in a state of primary perfection (kamāl awwal). From the moment of their initial creation until the attainment of kamāl awwal, they remained in a condition of durus (dormancy or latency). During this state, they observed the ⟪ar:نور شعشعانی⟫ radiant light of the First Intellect and understood that it had attained this rank because of performing tawhīd, with tajrīd and tanzīh, toward the Creator of the Almighty. Perceiving this, they transitioned from dormancy to ⟪ar:انبعاث⟫ emanation—following the First Intellect and acknowledging its tawhīd.[^cite-3]

| Existence | Dormancy | Emanation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First Perfection | Passive contemplation | Secondary Perfection |
| Active potential | Receptive state | Active manifestation |

## The Difference in the Perspectives of the Emanators

The First Intellect established the tawhīd of the Almighty through the dual path of negation and affirmation within the utterance of sincere devotion. Because the Shahāda—"*Lā ilāha illā ʾAllāh*" (There is no god but Allah)—contains only these two components, with no third way to approach the Creator's monotheism, the First Intellect made both paths luminously clear. When the veil of joy descended upon the First Intellect, the two emanating souls were startled and proceeded together in its footsteps. They are called al-Munbaʿithūn—the two who emerge together.

**Principles of Essence and Manifestation:**

Every thing possesses an essence, and the manifestation of that essence is like a noun with its attributes. Without essence there is no substance; without nouns, no attributes. Likewise, the essence of the First Intellect's development was the act of tawhīd toward its Originator, and because of this action, a veil of radiant light was placed upon it—the state of submission itself.[^cite-4]

### The Monotheism of the First Emanator

Witnessing the ⟪ar:نور شعشعانی⟫ radiant light of the First Intellect, the First Emanator understood that this illumination arose because the First Intellect had performed the ⟪ar:فعل توحید⟫ act of tawhīd for the Creator of the Almighty. He sought to discover the true cause of the happiness that had descended upon the Intellect and the lofty rank it had attained—perceiving the light shining with its own luminosity. He recognized that the First Intellect had attained this station by unifying with the Creator and executing its ordained function. After performing tawhīd toward the Originator, the First Emanator accepted the primacy of the First Intellect and glorified it as the First Intellect had glorified and sanctified the Creator. He acknowledged the forgiveness and grace of the First Intellect, as well as its greatness, nobility, and superiority over all other beings. Through this confession and the relationship established with the First Intellect, he received ⟪ar:تائیدات، لحظات و برکات⟫ confirmations, attentions, and blessings from the First Intellect, and through it he came into contact with the Qudsi knowledge—that sacred knowledge issuing from the Divine Presence and the Light of the Spirit as sent forth by the Creator of the Almighty. Thus he too attained perfection and became ⟪ar:عقل ثانی⟫ the Second Intellect. As the rank of the First Emanator was elevated, the station of the First Intellect—whether ⟪ar:مقام وحدت⟫ the station of unification or ⟪ar:مقام ھویت⟫ the station of identity—was exalted. Now he is not reckoned among the creation, for he has become *Al-ʿAddād* (the Reckoner), and all others have been obliterated in him. Allah says in the Qur'an:

> ⟪quran 3:2⟫
> ⟪ar:‏ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ ‎⟫
> *Allah! La ilaha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He), the Ever Living, the One Who sustains and protects all that exists.*

| Allah | Al-Ḥayy (the Living) · Al-Qayyūm (the Sustainer) |
| --- | --- |
| First Intellect | First Emanator |

**Principle of Lower and Higher Perspectives:**

The musta­wdaʿūn (those entrusted with lower knowledge) received ⟪ar:نظر ادون⟫ the lower perspective, while al-mustaqqarrūn (those established in higher knowledge) received ⟪ar:نظر اشرف⟫ the higher perspective. It became necessary for al-mustawdaʿūn to acquire the higher perspective so that they could progress from the ⟪ar:مستودع⟫ realm of the entrusted to the ⟪ar:مستقر⟫ realm of the established.

### The Tawhīd of the Second Emanator

Like the First Intellect, the Second Emanator perceived the veil of the joys surrounding the First Intellect and understood that the First Intellect had attained this rank through tawhīd toward the Creator of the Almighty. Yet he gave precedence to the light itself rather than to the act of tawhīd. Captivated by the radiant state of the First Intellect, he marveled: "What a light! What magnificence! What a sublime station!" He did not penetrate to the reason for the light; he saw only its outward splendor, and his vision did not reach the inner truth. Dazzled by this visible radiance, he was overwhelmed. He valued the external station of the First Intellect without seeking to understand why he had attained it or why happiness had inundated him. Because of this outward attachment, he fell behind and descended in the hierarchy of ranks. Yet because he and al-Munbaʿath al-Awwal (the First Emanator) had both advanced together toward tawhīd, he imagined they were equal in station. He became guilty and ignorant through his own action, holding the ⟪ar:وهم مساوات⟫ illusion of equivalence—believing that because they had emanated together, he and the First Emanator were of equal rank. This ⟪ar:وهم مساوات⟫ illusion of equivalence corrupted the form of his emanation, preventing him from attaining secondary perfection (kamāl thānī).[^cite-5]

Although the Second Emanator praised the tawhīd of the Creator and acknowledged the primacy and superiority of the First Intellect, he did not receive the sacred materials from the First Intellect. This was because he did not truly recognize the superiority of the First Emanator and his vision; instead, he equated himself with the First. Yet perfection requires that there be no defect or injustice in the self. The error lay in the ⟪ar:وهم مساوات⟫ illusion of equivalence, for equality is possible only in primary perfection, whereas in secondary perfection no two limits can be equal. Al-Munbaʿath al-Thānī (the Second Emanator) offered correct tawhīd to the Creator, yet by attaching importance to an erroneous perception of the First Intellect, he forfeited success.

## The Difference in the Testimonies of the First Two

The First Intellect moved first toward tawhīd of the Creator of the Almighty and attained secondary perfection. Although the First Emanator attained perfection after the First Intellect, he was first in his own ⟪ar:انبعاث⟫ emanation, and in this respect he also achieved an individual status. For this reason, the First Intellect and the First Emanator are called ⟪ar:أَوَّلَین⟫ the First Two. Although both of them performed ⟪ar:کلمۃ الشہادۃ⟫ the testimony of faith, as the Qur'an declares:

> ⟪quran 3:18⟫
> ⟪ar:‏شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَٱلْمَلَٓئِكَةُ وَأُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمِ قَآئِمًۢا بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۚ لَآ إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ‎⟫
> *Allah bears witness that La ilaha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He), and the angels, and those having knowledge (also give this witness); (He is always) maintaining His creation in Justice. La ilah illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He), the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.*

Yet their testimonies were directed toward different realities. The testimony of the First Intellect was to the divinity of the Almighty. As soon as he attained tawhīd, he received the divine and perfect materials from the Creator and was elevated to the station of unity. The Creator made the First Intellect his ⟪ar:حجاب⟫ veil and became himself ⟪ar:محتجب⟫ veiled. That is, the First Intellect received materials from the Creator, but now all other beings shall receive materials from the First Intellect. In this capacity, he himself became ⟪ar:الہ⟫ ilāh (a divine principle) for all else. Therefore, when the Second Emanator followed in the footsteps of the First Intellect and testified ⟪ar:الہیت⟫ to divinity through ⟪ar-quote:شھد اللہ انہ لا الہ الا ھو⟫ "Allah bears witness that there is no divinity except Him," his ⟪ar:الہیت⟫ testimony of divinity was not to the Creator but to the First Intellect. For the Second Emanator, the First Intellect took the place of ⟪ar:ھو⟫ the Divine "He."[^cite-6]

| Witness | *Lā ilāha* (no divinity) | *Illā* (except) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First Intellect | There is no divinity | Save the Creator of the Almighty |
| Second Emanator | There is no divinity | Save the First Intellect |

## The Holy Sanctuary of the First Emanator

The First Intellect established tawhīd without any ⟪ar:ملحم و معلم⟫ guide or teacher, and was established in the station of unity. Witnessing this, the al-Munbaʿithūn moved forward—the First Emanator attaining secondary perfection while the Second remained behind because of his ⟪ar:وهم مساوات⟫ illusion of equivalence. When the First Emanator performed tawhīd, twenty-seven others perceived his vision and performed tawhīd with him, attaining secondary perfection without needing explicit invitation. As the Qur'an suggests through the language of spiritual sight: ⟪ar-quote:نَظَرُ بِنَظَرِہِ ، بَصَرُ بِبَصَرِہِ⟫ "I have witnessed through his witnessing; I have perceived through his perception."[^cite-7] In this way, the First Emanator formed a circle of twenty-seven souls, which is called ⟪ar:حضیرۃ القدس⟫ the Holy Sanctuary—the gathering of the sacred assembly. The First Emanator stands at the center of this circle.

These twenty-eight beings are compared to the twenty-eight lights of the Kalimah (the Shahāda), and they became a model for all the learned. For this reason, the entire divine system is divided according to the numbers 28 (comprising 2+3+4+7+12). The First Intellect and the First Emanator are two fixed points that shall never change their position. All other intellects will eventually merge into the realm of the First Emanator as the Day of Perfection approaches. This same pattern has been maintained throughout all the creation cycles.

### The Map of Ḥaḍrat al-Quds in the Worlds

Allah declares in the Holy Qur'an:

> ⟪quran 53:13-15⟫
> ⟪ar:‏وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرَىٰ ‎ ‏عِندَ سِدْرَةِ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ ‎ ‏عِندَهَا جَنَّةُ ٱلْمَأْوَىٓ ‎⟫
> *And indeed he (Muhammad PBUH) saw him [Jibrael (Gabriel)] at a second descent. Near Sidrat-ul-Muntaha [the lote-tree of the utmost boundary], Near it is the Paradise of Abode.*

In Arabic, the Sidra (سِدْرَة—lote-tree) possesses a singular distinction: it always grows in solitude, with no other tree beside it. The ⟪ar:جنت الماوی⟫ Garden of Refuge (Jannāt al-Maʾwā) refers to a sanctuary wherein people may enter and find shelter.[^cite-8] The First Intellect is symbolized by ⟪ar:سدرۃ المنتہی⟫ the Sidra of the Boundary because it stands unique in its world, existing in the realm of unity where only it subsists in its sphere, with no other beside it or associated with it. It is the sole originator. The First Emanator is symbolized by ⟪ar:جنت الماوی⟫ the Garden of Refuge because, having advanced after witnessing the First Intellect, he gathered around him a circle of twenty-seven souls who came to shelter in his presence and find rest. As the days progress, all intellects shall merge into the realm of the First Emanator. Therefore, his circle is called ⟪ar:حضیرۃ القدس⟫ the Holy Sanctuary (Ḥaḍrat al-Quds). This same cosmic pattern was then replicated throughout all worlds and realms.

In the physical world (⟪ar:جثہ ابدائیہ⟫), the First Intellect abides in supreme sovereignty as the sole master of the entire physical cosmos, and its reflection appears in the physical realm through the First Emanator, who shall gather the whole creation. In the celestial world, the highest heaven corresponds to the First Intellect, where neither stars nor planets dwell in multiplicity. All stars and planets reside in the lower sphere, which corresponds to the First Emanator. In the same way, in the era before the last (⟪ar:عین آخرۃ⟫), the positions of the First Intellect and its reflections correspond to the First Emanator. All the Imāms (⟪ar:عین اولہ⟫—the highest forms) shall be gathered in their proper stations. In each age, the Imām corresponds to the First Intellect, and his ⟪ar:باب الابواب⟫ Gate of Gates corresponds to the First Emanator. The gathering of all the forms of believers takes place at this Gate of Gates. Similarly, in the household, the husband corresponds to the First Intellect—the sole custodian of his household—and the wife corresponds to the First Emanator, within whose womb children are nurtured.

When a row is formed in prayer, all worshippers shift their positions and take their proper place in the line. Only the Imām and his deputy (standing to the right of the Imām) maintain their stations without change. In this way, all the worshippers create a living image of the spiritual world. Just as in the spiritual realm only the First Intellect and the First Emanator shall remain unchanging, while all other lower beings shall evolve, change their positions, and eventually merge into the realm of the First Emanator, so too in the mosque—the image of the spiritual world—does this pattern manifest.[^cite-9]

| *Jannāt al-Maʾwā* | *Sidrat al-Muntahā* |
| --- | --- |
| First Emanator | First Intellect |
| Gate of Gates | The Imām |
| *ʿAyn Awlā* (Highest Forms) | *ʿAyn Ākhira* (Last Forms) |
| Lower Celestial Sphere | Highest Heaven |
| Wife (household) | Husband (household) |

## The Universal Intellect and the Universal Self

⟪ar:عقل اور نفس، روح (کمال اول)⟫ The Intellect and the Self are names of faculties. Allah the Almighty ⟪ar:ارواح⟫ created the universe from the Spirit, which is why this realm is called ⟪ar:عالم روحانی⟫ the Spiritual World. By harnessing the powers of this Spirit, ⟪ar:عقل⟫ the Intellect is produced—the more perfected form of the Spirit *bi-l-fiʿl* (in actuality)—while ⟪ar:نفس⟫ the Self is the name of the Spirit's form *bi-l-quwwa* (in potentiality). The Self is she who receives sustenance from the Intellect, obeys its commands, and responds to its signals.

[diagram: Hierarchy diagram. Top box (dark gray) contains الروح (Al-Rūḥ / the Spirit). Two arrows descend to two child boxes: bottom-left box contains نفس (Nafs / the Self) rendered in blue text, and bottom-right box contains عقل (ʿAql / the Intellect) rendered in red text. The diagram visualizes the doctrine that the Spirit (al-Rūḥ) bifurcates into its two manifest faculties: Intellect and Self.]
  (see ../images/001.png)
  *Arabic labels in image:* ⟪ar:الروح · نفس · عقل⟫

The First Intellect is called ⟪ar:عقل کلیۃ⟫ the Universal Intellect because it was the first to contemplate its own existence and advance toward the tawhīd of the Creator. The First Emanator is called ⟪ar:نفس کلیۃ⟫ the Universal Self because he became the most refined and noble self in this spiritual world following the First Intellect. The First Emanator became the wholeness for ⟪ar:کُل⟫ all creation, and all others became part of him. For this reason, the First Emanator is the end and culmination of all worlds. The First Intellect created his own self as an exemplar. Only the First Intellect is a self that does not possess a self apart from itself, for it is the creator of the self itself. Except for the First Intellect, all souls were born because they emanated from the call (daʿwa) of the First Emanator. For this reason, the order proceeds as follows: the first to serve is the Intellect, and the one who comes next in function is his Self:

| Intellect | Self |
| --- | --- |
| First Intellect | First Emanator |
| Muḥammad (upon him be peace) | ʿAlī |
| ʿAlī | Fāṭima |
| al-Ḥasan | al-Ḥusayn |

## The Sign of Definition: Alif and Lam

In Arabic, Alif and Lam are known as the symbols of *Maʿrifa* (definite knowledge) or the article of definition. Therefore, if a noun whose meaning is indefinite—for instance ⟪ar:رجل⟫ (a man)—is to become known, one adds Alif and Lam before it: ⟪ar:الرجل⟫ (the man). Thus in Arabic, every noun preceded by Alif and Lam becomes known and determinate. Alif is the first letter of the Arabic alphabet. Lam is kindred to Alif because Lam is composed of two lines while Alif consists of a single line. Through the alphabet's logic, Lam is generated from the doubling of Alif.

Alif is an argument for the First Intellect, for just as Alif is the first letter, so too was the First Intellect born without any ⟪ar:ملحم و معلم⟫ guide or teacher. Similarly, Lam is an argument for the Self, which was created by the Intellect and on account of it—just as Lam is constituted from the lines of two Alifs.[^cite-10]

[diagram: A calligram of the Arabic definite article الـ (al-, formed by the letters Alif and Lam) rendered in large yellow strokes. Annotated in small blue text: the word عقل (Intellect) is placed at the top against the Alif (ا), and the word نفس (Self) is placed inside the curve of the Lam (ل). The illustration teaches the doctrine that the two letters forming the Arabic definite article symbolically represent the two primary spiritual principles — Intellect (mapped to Alif, the upright letter) and Self (mapped to Lam, the descending letter).]
  (see ../images/002.png)
  *Arabic labels in image:* ⟪ar:الـ · عقل · نفس⟫

Just as Alif and Lam together render other words known and determinate, so too are all spiritual and physical limits defined and made manifest through the Intellect and the Self. There exist two similarities (ratios) of Alif within Lam, for Lam is the First Emanator and Alif is the First Intellect. The First Intellect transcended itself and went before, yet before the First Intellect there existed an exemplar of two ratios of itself. Therefore, within Lam there are two Alif-lines: one longer, indicating a higher ratio, and one shorter, indicating a lower line.

## The Inkwell, the Pen, and the Tablet

The Messenger of Allah (upon him be the peace and blessings of Allah) said: "First Allah created the Pen, and then He produced a stream from it—sweeter than honey, whiter than milk, and softer than musk. Then He commanded the Pen: 'Write!' The Pen asked, 'What shall I write?' He said, 'Write down all that shall occur until the Day of Resurrection!' And the Pen wrote everything upon the Tablet. This is why it is called ⟪ar:لوح محفوظ⟫ the Preserved Tablet. As Allah says (in the meaning):

> ⟪quran 85:21-22⟫
> ⟪ar:‏بَلْ هُوَ قُرْآنٌۭ مَّجِيدٌۭ ‎ ‏فِى لَوْحٍۢ مَّحْفُوظٍۭ ‎⟫
> *Nay! This is a Glorious Quran, (Inscribed) in Al-Lauh Al-Mahfuz (The Preserved Tablet)!*

The Qur'ān is the utterance of the First Intellect. With this utterance, whatever the Pen inscribed upon the first Tablet, the Tablet preserved within itself until the Day of Judgment. The Pen has fulfilled its function. Now all the worlds shall receive their sustenance from it.[^cite-11]

| Pen | Stream | Tablet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First Intellect | Sacred Materials / Continuous Knowledge | First Emanator |

In this ḥadīth, the Messenger of Allah (upon him be the peace and blessings of Allah) signifies by "Pen" the First Intellect, by "Tablet" the First Emanator, and by "stream" the continuous and unceasing knowledge. The First Intellect is the pen of creation itself, inscribing twenty-eight words upon the First Emanator with the ink of Qudsi materials. These twenty-eight are the ⟪ar:نور کلمہ لا الہ الا اللہ⟫ luminous gems of the Kalimah "There is no god but Allah." With this light, the First Intellect bestowed upon the First Emanator all the ⟪ar:علم ماکان سیکون⟫ knowledge of what was and what shall be—a bestowal to which the hadith refers when it says "the Pen wrote down all matters upon the Tablet until the Day of Judgment." This is the meaning of what Allah declares:

> ⟪quran 68:1⟫
> ⟪ar:‏نٓ ۚ وَٱلْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ ‎⟫
> *Nun. By the Pen and what the angels write (in the Records of men).*

The pen cannot develop the capacity to write until it is immersed in ink. In the same way, until the First Intellect acquired the sacred materials, it had not developed the capacity to sustain the First Emanator and all other intellects. It is by virtue of these materials that the First Intellect attained perfection, reaching the station of ⟪ar:صمد⟫ the Self-Sufficient—one on whom all else depends for existence—such that all other intellects became dependent upon him. ⟪ar:(نٓ)⟫ The letter Nun itself invokes the principle that says: ⟪ar-quote:بَینَ المُبدِعِ وَالمُبدَعِ کَلِمَۃ⟫ "Between the Creator and the created stands a Word."[^cite-12]

| *Nūn* | The Pen | What is inscribed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Summons (*Daʿwa*) | First Intellect | Knowledge of what was and shall be |
| Nūr al-Kalima (Qudsi Material) | First Intellect | Learning from Sacred Knowledge |

[diagram: Schematic illustration of the cosmological writing metaphor (Inkwell, Pen, and Tablet—*Dawāt al-Qalam wa-l-Lawḥ*). Upper right: an inkwell labeled مواد قدسی (sacred materials) in red. Upper left: a pen labeled قلم (عقل أول) — Pen (First Intellect) — in red. Center: a black tablet labeled لوح (منبعث أول) — Tablet (First Emanator) — with the Kalima لا اله الا الله (There is no god but Allah) inscribed on it in white calligraphy. Bottom: an arrow pointing downward to عقول (the Intellects), depicting the hierarchical descent from the divine source through the First Intellect and First Emanator down to the subordinate intellects.]
  (see ../images/003.png)
  *Arabic labels in image:* ⟪ar:مواد قدسی · قلم (عقل أول) · لوح (منبعث أول) · لا اله الا الله · عقول⟫

These twenty-eight limits are summaries and expressions of the ninety-nine ⟪ar:اسماء الحسنی⟫ Most Beautiful Names. They are distributed according to the numerical order (2, 3, 4, 7, 12). Among them, the first three categories (2, 3, 4) are administered by the First Intellect, while the synthesis of the latter two (7 and 12) unites with the First Emanator.

# Planned Resurrection



## Condemned Souls: The Reproaching and Commanding Self

Since the fallen beings are divided into categories based on their own remorse—⟪ar:نادمین⟫ the penitent, ⟪ar:شاک و متحیرین⟫ the doubters and the perplexed, and ⟪ar:مصر و مستکبرین⟫ the obstinate and arrogant—these three natures are found in every species and gender. Prayer that pleases Allah is virtuous; prayer that becomes wrapped around the worshipper's face and kills the soul is vicious. In the same way, there exist three categories of human beings, distinguished by the character of the ⟪ar:نفس حسیۃ⟫ sensible soul.

### The Nafs Ammarah Bi'l-Su' (The Soul Inciting to Evil)

Allah Almighty declares in the Qur'an:

> ⟪quran 12:53⟫
> ⟪ar:‏ وَمَآ أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِىٓ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌۢ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّىٓ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّى غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ ‎⟫
> 
> *"And I free not myself (from the blame). Verily, the (human) self is inclined to evil, except when my Lord bestows His Mercy (upon whom He wills). Verily, my Lord is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful."*

The ⟪ar:نفس امارۃ بالسوء⟫ commanding soul (nafs ammarah bi'l-su') leads one toward transgression. This is the ⟪ar:نفس⟫ self that, when it unfolds its wings and refuses obedience, flees from righteousness.[^cite-1] Just as Allah sends forth one possessed of a ⟪ar:نفس خیر⟫ virtuous soul through His messenger ⟪ar:رسول اللہ (ﷺ)⟫, so too does He send forth one corrupted in soul. The ⟪ar:سورۃ الشمس⟫ Chapter of the Sun bears witness:

> ⟪quran 91:12⟫
> ⟪ar:‏إِذِ ٱنۢبَعَثَ أَشْقَىٰهَا ‎⟫
> 
> *"When the most wicked man among them went forth (to kill the she-camel)."*

He who departs in such wretchedness is truly ⟪ar:شقی الأولین والأخرین⟫ the most unfortunate of all former and latter generations. Allah shall punish him by casting him into the depths of Hell, for he has come forth in utter stubbornness. Such is the destiny of ⟪ar:معاویۃ⟫ those who emulate the tyrant's path, unlike ⟪ar:مولانا علی ابن ابی طالب⟫ our Master ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, the Commander of the Faithful.

### The Nafs Lawwamah (The Reproaching Soul)

By contrast, another self is the ⟪ar:'نفس لوامۃ '⟫ reproaching soul—perpetually suspended between states of doubt and disturbance by suspicion. This self does not permit either side to reach a final verdict, but remains in restless vacillation. Allah swears an oath in its regard:

> ⟪quran 75:2⟫
> ⟪ar:‏وَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلنَّفْسِ ٱللَّوَّامَةِ ‎⟫
> 
> *"And I swear by the self-reproaching person (a believer)."*

---

## The Slaughter and Hamstringing of the Soul

Regarding the ⟪ar:سورۃ الشمس⟫ Chapter of the Sun, Allah declares:

> ⟪quran 91:10-14⟫
> ⟪ar:‏وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّىٰهَا ‎ ‏كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَىٰهَآ ‎ ‏إِذِ ٱنۢبَعَثَ أَشْقَىٰهَا ‎ ‏فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ نَاقَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَسُقْيَهَا ‎ ‏فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُم بِذَنۢبِهِمْ فَسَوَّىٰهَا ‎⟫
> 
> *"And indeed he fails who corrupts his ownself. Thamud (people) denied (their Prophet) through their transgression. When the most wicked man among them went forth (to kill the she-camel). But the Messenger of Allah said to them: 'Be cautious! Fear the evil end. That is the she-camel of Allah! (Do not harm it) and bar it not from having its drink!' Then they denied him and they killed it. So their Lord destroyed them because of their sin, and made them equal in destruction."*

The term ⟪ar:'عقر'⟫ to hamstring—literally means to slay. It is the appellation ⟪ar:'ذبیحت '⟫ of lawful slaughter, and also the name ⟪ar:عقر⟫ of unlawful killing. In this verse, although the apparent referent is the she-camel, in truth the conscience turns toward the souls of those who perpetrated this deed—those who committed such evil and ⟪ar:'ھا'⟫ corrupted their own ⟪ar:'ھا'⟫ souls, bestowing upon them a forbidden death.[^cite-2]

---



## The Death and Return of the Believing Defaulter

The transgressor is called the ⟪ar:'مؤمن مقاصر '⟫ believing defaulter—one who has committed grave offenses. There is a distinction between the death of one who has fulfilled faith and one who has fallen short. Though every human being bears guilt in some measure, the defaulting believer is one specifically who has perpetrated ⟪ar:'کبائر'⟫ major sins: shirk, falsehood, adultery, intoxication, and murder.

The first punishment of such a person differs markedly from that of the righteous believer. Unlike the latter, he must endure the torment of the grave. The ⟪ar:نفس حسیۃ⟫ sensible soul does not depart wholly; instead, depending upon the magnitude of his transgressions, sensation reverberates within his body. He is entombed in a state of semi-death, enduring for three days the severe chastisement of the grave. Thereafter his body undergoes punishment in human form, and ⟪ar:حسیۃ⟫ sensation and ⟪ar:رجس⟫ corruption accompany ⟪ar:نقس⟫ the torment of wrench and degradation. Yet Divine mercy tempers this: he is not required to don seventy garments, each with seventy clasp-rings. Rather, ⟪ar:جوہر نفس⟫ nature—which is the very essence of the soul—chastises him according to justice alone, then restores him to human stature.[^cite-3]

---

## The Middle Torments

These are the four corners of the earth where climate is not temperate, where extremes of weather prevail. Great and terrible calamities abound. Only one already punished with this torment arrives at ⟪ar:جہنم کبریٰ⟫ the Great Hell—these are the stations of the Nāṭiq and the Imams.

### The Northern Part (The Opposites of the Imams)

The north is dark, painful, terrifying—the realm where the number of Imams is kept. For six months there is no sunrise, causing the full effect of ⟪ar:کرۃ زمحریر⟫ the cold sphere. The animals kept here cannot move from their place due to bitter cold, remaining like stones. They endure the most painful, agonizing punishment from ⟪ar:برودت⟫ cold and ⟪ar:یبوست⟫ dryness. This is what Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq referred to as "the cold of iron" (⟪ar-quote:برد الحدید⟫).

### The Southern Part (The Opposites of the Prophets)

The south is in the heat zone where ⟪ar:کرہ اسیر⟫ the fire sphere effect peaks. There is scorching heat and toxic winds. Here the multitude of prophets and messengers are tormented, grouped as evil beasts of monstrous form—high as mountains. They possess no external senses, yet feel the torment completely.

### The Eastern Part (The Supports of the Prophets)

The east, where the sun rises, is where those who aided the prophets are punished—⟪ar:اضداد انبیاء و مرسلین⟫ the opposites of the prophets and messengers. Towering mountains press close due to their height. They are placed as if nooses encircle their necks, chained in severe suffering.

### The Western Part (The Supports of the Imams)

The west is dark and wavy, called ⟪ar:بحر⟫ the sea—⟪ar:'بحر جن '⟫ the jinn-sea. Its waves rise like mountains. This is the torment of the Imams' helpers, inferior to the northern doom. In this sea, the Zodiac's aides are cast as shapeless beasts, devouring and attacking one another.

| Quarter | Opposites |
| --- | --- |
| North | The Imams' Number |
| South | The Prophets' and Messengers' Number |
| East | The Imams' Supports |
| West | The Prophets' and Messengers' Supports |

When they complete punishment on one side, they are thrown to another's torment until all four are suffered. They are then taken to ⟪ar:'عذاب اکبر'⟫ the greater punishment.

⟪ar:سیدنا مؤید اعلی اللہ قدسہ⟫ Our Master al-Muʾayyad (may Allah elevate his station) declared: "Those whose feet slipped, separated from the grasp of Allah's saints, must traverse the heat of ⟪ar:مرکز نورانی⟫ the luminous center and the troubles of ⟪ar:کرہ زمحریر⟫ the cold sphere, enduring ⟪ar:برودت⟫ cold." They walk in darkness toward "three-split shadows" (⟪ar-quote:ثلاثہ شعب⟫), which are the torments of Darckat, Hafdār, and Saqqar. Nowhere do they find shelter, suffering ⟪ar:قائم القیامہ⟫ punishment until the Qāʾim appears.[^cite-13]

---

## Return from the Torments of the Sides

After the torments of the sides, they are led to the Path ⟪ar:ربع مسکون⟫ (the inhabited quarter of the earth) where they ⟪ar:مزاج و ممتزج⟫ appear in the Garden of the ʿAzāʾis. They are then presented before the Qāʾim, and ⟪ar:قامت الفیہ⟫ thereafter led to the Heaven of the Living. ⟪ar:عذاب اکبر⟫

Among those appearing are those who have turned from torment and others who have completed the torments of the sides. Upon turning, they ascend the climbing staircase. First, they come as beneficial minerals for humans; from there to lawful plants, then to lawful beasts. They are eaten by the walī (guardian) or the obstinate one—whichever becomes their conduit for appearance. If a person's punishments are fulfilled, he goes to the guardian; if remnants remain, he goes to the obstinate. All is under Allah Almighty's will. Then he ⟪ar:قامت الفیہ⟫ appears and is presented with the guardianship of him whom he had previously denied. If he accepts, he is saved from punishment and joins the people of truth; if he denies and is arrogant, he falls back to punishment. In this manner, the cycle of punishment and reward continues.

When ⟪ar:قائم القیامہ⟫ the advent of the Qāʾim of the Resurrection draws near, all manifestations of the six periods from Adam to his time appear. Their condition is the same as at the moment of their death—denial and arrogance. Similarly, all prophets, imams, and guardians also appear in person. All shall stand in the fields of the Day of Resurrection, and Allah shall judge between them in truth, wronging none. When the Qāʾim appears, these additions—also termed ⟪ar:یاجوج و ماجوج⟫ Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj—are drawn from the islands and presented before him. Their eyes shall gaze upon the Qāʾim in amazement. ⟪ar:'یاجوج '⟫ Yaʾjūj refers to the multiplication of places, and ⟪ar:'ماجوج '⟫ Maʾjūj to the helpers of their multiplication.[^cite-14]

## The Great Punishment

All the Hudoods (the Divine Limits), Prophets, and Imams will gather in the assembly ⟪ar:قائم علی ذکرہ السلام⟫, where they shall inform all creation of the deeds of their communities. Thereafter, the Qaim will put them all to death. A fire will descend upon them ⟪ar:عقدتین⟫, consuming their foul and lifeless bodies; as vapor, they will rise into it and be absorbed. When this fire descends to the depths of the earth in its rotation, Saqqara—⟪ar:سقرا⟫—receives a fever ⟪ar:عقدتین⟫ appropriate to its nature.

Saqqara lies at the bottom of the earth. The heat enters through the pores of the terrestrial crust; once within, it evaporates and returns to the state it occupied in time. By analogy: a ⟪ar:کبریتی⟫sulphorous pot with a depression at its center, containing stones, fashioned inverted like a clay vessel—its upper and lower rims sealed, its interior ⟪ar:'لاوا'⟫ forming what is truly hell. Lower apertures permit vapor to escape and ascend. Thus it resembles ⟪ar:بیت الخلا⟫ a sealed, intensely hot chamber ⟪ar:سقرا⟫. This accords with what the Qur'an designates as ⟪ar:'سجین '⟫; scholars have formulated their understanding of Saqqara from this reference. The incandescent fuel beneath it equals the sun's heat—the sun warming Saqqara from below as fire heats a pot from beneath—until the already-scorching material of Saqqara ignites.[^cite-13]

When these vapors become troublesome, those before them observe and relate why they were consigned there. Saqqara bears another name, ⟪ar:'بوطا '⟫, and some cry out: "Woe to us, for we were heedless, and we were indeed among the wrongdoers." They are told, "Those whom you worshipped besides Allah are themselves in Hell, serving as its fuel." Their deputies say to the Imams, "Had you been true guides, we would not be cast into this saqqarah." All remain here eternally ⟪ar:بیت الخلاء⟫.

> ⟪quran 98:6-7⟫
> ⟪ar:‏إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَبِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ فِى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَلِدِينَ فِيهَآ ۚ أُو۟لَٓئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ ‎ ‏إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّلِحَتِ أُو۟لَٓئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ ‎⟫
> *Verily, those who disbelieve (in the religion of Islam, the Quran and Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him)) from among the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and Al-Mushrikun will abide in the Fire of Hell. They are the worst of creatures. Verily, those who believe [in the Oneness of Allah, and in His Messenger Muhammad (Peace be upon him)) including all obligations ordered by Islam] and do righteous good deeds, they are the best of creatures.*

In this verse, the wicked are designated ⟪ar:'شر البریۃ '⟫ with the modifier ⟪ar:'خالدین فیھا '⟫; yet the righteous, termed ⟪ar:'خیر البریۃ '⟫, receive ⟪ar:'خالدین فیھا ابدا '⟫—abiding eternally. This signals a profound distinction: the duration of punishment for the wicked is finite, a temporal ordeal; the reward of Paradise is infinite and without end.[^cite-14]

In Saqqara, these people cry out, yet remain unheard. When ⟪ar:شمس⟫ the sun descends to the earth's interior, each night it heats Saqqara as fire heats a pot's lower surface. As the sun's rays heat this lower chamber, its stones ignite ⟪ar:ملاعین⟫; the interior boils. At that moment, they cry for succor—but none comes.

## The Inhabitants of Lesser and Greater Punishment

Three categories of torment are distinguished:

| The Lesser Punishment | The Intermediate Doom | The Great Punishment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Seven Gateways | The Punishment of the Extremities | The Punishment of Saqqara |

There are ⟪ar:'روع خننر'⟫ seven degrees of punishment, remembered by those in error. The seventh station ⟪ar:'معدن'⟫—which one who reaches it shall also traverse—corresponds to ⟪ar:عذاب اطراف⟫; what ⟪ar:عذاب اطراف⟫ one has attained shall also be cast upon them. And ⟪ar:عذاب اکبر⟫ are those of polytheism and the manifold Imams and Prophets described in the Qur'an as ⟪ar:'مغضوب علیھم'⟫—those upon whom wrath has descended.

**Stations of Transmigration and Punishment:**

| Category | Form | Principle |
|---|---|---|
| **Abomination** | Human stature | *Ḥassiyyah + Nāmiyyah* |
| **Waqf** | Monkeys and creatures | *Nāmiyyah operative* |
| **Aks** | Beasts | *Potential Names* |
| **Bear** | Earth insects | |
| **Impure** | Birds | |
| **Naqs** | Plants | |
| **Dance** | Minerals | |

⟪ar:عذاب ادنی⟫ Within each station are seventy chambers, and within each chamber, seventy bonds. Thus one transmigrates 4,900 times within a single category before advancing. While ⟪ar:شریر نفوس⟫ they remain in animal form, they are told each time of the crime for which they suffer; yet when they descend into plant and mineral realms, such knowledge is stripped away.

**The Intermediate and Greater Punishments:**

When these seven penalties conclude, one whose sentence is complete ⟪ar:قامت الفیۃ⟫ is restored; one destined for further torment proceeds to the punishment of the extremities. All sent there are also cast into Saqqara. From the extremities, these criminals are remolded into human shape to be judged by the Qaim's hand, then consigned to Saqqara. When ⟪ar:عذاب اکبر⟫ one ⟪ar:کور اعظم⟫—an immense age—concludes, they return to human stature. First they ⟪ar:'معدن'⟫ become what the plant absorbs; that plant is eaten by animals, which become food for their parents, and thus they are reborn.[^cite-15]

**On the Constituents of Food and Sustenance:**

The halal food we believers consume, though lawful, ⟪ar:شاک و متحیر⟫ contains ingredients of and ⟪ar:مصر ومستکبر⟫. All waste—urine, stool—comprises ⟪ar:مصر و مستکبرین⟫ constituents. Secretions from other orifices—earwax, eye matter, nasal discharge, saliva—are all ⟪ar:شاک و متحیر⟫ components. Blood, formed from nadmī elements, reaches the brain and generates its faculties. The lawful fragrances we apply require no digestion; they transmute instantly into the mind's powers.

## The Description of Saqqara

Our earth is ⟪ar:بیضوی⟫ oval and ⟪ar:مسطح⟫ flat, and on its far side lies ⟪ar:سقرا⟫, which is ⟪ar:سجین⟫ and ⟪ar:جہنم کبریٰ⟫—the Great Hell—⟪ar:مستوی⟫ on its level. The center of the earth's surface aligns with the ⟪ar:کعبۃ اللہ⟫; on the earth's opposite pole stands Saqqara in the form of a hollow, its lowest region ⟪ar:'اہل طاغوت '⟫ the abode of the rebellious. The earth has four corners, called its extremities, where extremity-punishment is inflicted upon the opponents and oppressors. These extremities border Saqqara, lying so cold that passage is impossible. Beyond these borders lie multiple apertures in the encircling land; in the Ruba Muskun (Uninhabited Region) stands the greatest ⟪ar:'دُردُور'⟫, located in the river between China and India, toward which all rivers flow—a passage from which manifold sounds issue. ⟪ar:نعوذ باللہ منھا⟫

When the sun revolves before the earth, it is day for earthly dwellers and night for ⟪ar:اہل سقرا⟫—the inhabitants of Saqqara. When the sun rises for them, there is day, and night for the earth's inhabitants. In such a day and night, the Day of Judgment passes. ⟪ar:اہل سقرا⟫ The people of Saqqara endure extreme day-heat and unbearable night-cold beyond reckoning. As these afflictions strike them continuously, punishment multiplies a hundredfold.

It is essential to recall that the Almighty created Saqqara before the earth. In His Word, He granted Saqqara a distinct identity, mentioning the earth, Saqqara, and the heavens separately in one verse. Nine planets and seven constellations orbit both earth and Saqqara.[^cite-16] The heavens, though superficial in aspect, rotate both planarly and circularly—their motion both orbital and axial.

A crucial observation made here is that the earth spreads like an inverted vessel beneath the surface. Yet where ⟪ar:کعبۃ اللہ⟫ exists, ⟪ar:مقام ابراھیم⟫ the Station of Abraham, and ⟪ar:روضہ اقدس⟫ the Sacred Garden, and ⟪ar:غدیر خم⟫ Ghadir Khum are situated, there is no Saqqara, but rather a spacious realm wherein dwell all ⟪ar:ارواح نورانیہ⟫ luminous spirits and all ⟪ar:ارواح حسنۃ⟫ virtuous souls. Conversely, where ⟪ar:امیال⟫, ⟪ar:وادی شیطان⟫ the Valley of Satan, and ⟪ar:جمرات ثلاثہ⟫ the Three Heaps are found, ⟪ar:ارواح خبیثہ⟫ foul spirits exercise dominion. The upper portion of these sacred sites, opposite to the heavens, resides in the heavens themselves. Pores exist in these places, yet their locus should not be understood in spatial terms; rather, they transcend all limits and are wholly spiritual and nonmaterial.

The center of the entire cosmos is the Sun, around which the Earth orbits. Only human development can manifest upon Earth. The earth derives its substance from the sun; all influences orient toward earth to facilitate ⟪ar:استخراج انسانیت⟫ the extraction of humanity. Thus it is said that human perfection emerges from the earth—humanity was created nowhere else.

The true land (the land of feast) holds only ⟪ar:سقرا⟫, ⟪ar:کعبۃ اللہ⟫, and ⟪ar:مقدس مقامات⟫ sacred precincts upon a platform. The lands scattered in the remainder are not festive. The true land is sustained by ⟪ar:کعبۃ اللہ⟫; it is enveloped in dust—a clay sphere—with Saqqara beneath. Saqqara was created before the earth; these ⟪ar:مصر ومستکبرین⟫ stubborn oppressors are its components—the most ⟪ar:مصر ومستکبر⟫ obstinate among them, the most vile occupants of ⟪ar:'مقام سجین '⟫ the Station of the Record, the vilest ⟪ar:'طاغوت'⟫ of the tyrants. ⟪ar:رسول اللہ صلی اللہ علیہ و آلہ وسلم⟫ The Messenger of Allah declared: ⟪ar-quote:مُعاَوِیَۃ مِنَ الطَّاغُوت⟫ "Mu'awiyah is of the tyrants."[^cite-17]

**Concerning Saturn and Mars:**

⟪ar:زحل و مریخ⟫ It was revealed that these are components of the original ⟪ar:'نادمین'⟫—the remorseful. Yet among those accompanying them lay elements of obstinacy; ⟪ar:نادمین⟫ some were remorseful, ⟪ar:تائبین⟫ others repentant. Because corruption befell them at the sight of these malignancies, they—⟪ar:نادمین⟫ the remorseful and ⟪ar:تائبین⟫ the penitent—⟪ar:زحل اور مریخ⟫ were commanded to remain with you, and your purification became theirs. Therefore, their influences deteriorate.

All such entities endure ⟪ar:کور اعظم⟫ vast epochs within Saqqara's cavity. Throughout, they wage ceaseless war within Saqqara; their quarrels and enmities persist forever. The slain dissolve and are immediately reborn in a yet more ⟪ar:قبیح⟫ hideous and debased state. Some possess two heads, some three; some have faces reversed, others with visages rightward or leftward. In such abject condition, they suffer and burn eternally in hellfire. ⟪ar:کور اعظم⟫ Thus shall it remain for them.

## Emergence from Saqqara

When the period of Saqqara's punishment concludes, they emerge from Saqqara's upper reaches through four apertures, exhaling as vapor into the earth's exterior. One of these four passages lies in a valley ⟪ar:'حضر موت '⟫—Hadramaut—containing a well named ⟪ar:'برہوت '⟫ or ⟪ar:'شفاہُ'⟫. The second sits in the ⟪ar:خراسان (ایران)⟫ Khurasan (Iran) region, called ⟪ar:'موکا '⟫ or ⟪ar:'حار'⟫. The third stands in ⟪ar:عربستان⟫ Arabia, termed ⟪ar:'سیدو'⟫ or ⟪ar:'جو'⟫ or ⟪ar:'خرقا '⟫. The fourth bears the name ⟪ar:'سبر'⟫ or ⟪ar:'سعیر'⟫.

| Direction | Saqqara's External Apertures |
|---|---|
| East | Barhut / Shifa |
| West | Mocha / Hot |
| North | Syed & Joe / Kharqa |
| South | Sabr / Sa'ir |

They rise from these valleys as dust toward mountain peaks; as they reach the earth's level, they transform. The virtuous minerals transfer to plants and animals until they ⟪ar:قامت الفیہ⟫ acquire human stature. They are invited to the truth, shown wilayat (divine guardianship), and called to join the people of truth. Those who accept find salvation; those who refuse and transgress cycle again according to their hostility.[^cite-18]

In Saqqara, evil imagination, the base soul, and the body dissolve, arriving at ⟪ar:کمال اول⟫ primary perfection. They are then revealed to the world anew, granted complete authority and freedom to choose their path.



## How the Adversaries of the Imams Shall Be Punished

First, their bodies are spread into ⟪ar:نفس حسیہ⟫ the sensate soul and ⟪ar:نامیہ⟫ the vegetative soul. After forty days, the evil imagination departs the body and disperses to six loci:

| First | Second | Third |
|---|---|---|
| Toilet | Deserted forest | Wasteland |
| Refuse heap | Crossroads | Slaughterhouse |

They are retained at each station for a period so that outstanding recompense from the world may be exacted. Then they ⟪ar:عقدتین⟫ are cast into ⟪ar:'راس وزنب'⟫—the head and tail—a confinement more severe than any prison. ⟪ar:زنب⟫ The tail portion represents the lowest imprisonment; ⟪ar:راس⟫ the head, the uppermost. Their bodies are dispatched to the Seven Realms, where they fall into successive forms, passing through the kingdoms of man, animal, plant, and mineral. They are then hurled into extremity-punishment. From there they are restored to human form for a time, whereupon the rulers calculate and ⟪ar:'مِنیٰ'⟫ slaughter them at the field of Mina. ⟪ar:راس و زنب⟫ Thereafter, their evil imaginations consume their corpses like fire, burning bodies to cinders, which are cast into Saqqara. Within Saqqara exist distinct classes—⟪ar:(ھاویہ، سعیر، طاغوت)⟫ the Pit, the Blaze, and Tyranny—each section containing seventy valleys with varying temperatures. The seventeenth valley bears the name ⟪ar:'طاغوت '⟫. By day, the moon's rays burn them; by night, the sun's rays. This punishment endures one ⟪ar:کور اعظم⟫—vast age. Moreover, they slay and are slain, yet do not die. They perish and fall, reviving instantly; thus are their accounts settled. Such punishment persists ⟪ar:کور اعظم⟫ through long epochs.[^cite-19]

## Do the Punished Know Their Past Human State?

They are aware. When passing through animal forms and changing their conditions, they are made conscious of the sin for which they suffer. Upon reaching the plant and mineral realms, this knowledge is withdrawn; when cast into Saqqara, they are informed of their offense and those who led them astray. They perpetually strike and slay one another; the moment they perish, they revive and resume their combat. This punishment endures ⟪ar:کور اعظم⟫ through long epochs. Remorse becomes useless. When their sentence expires, they ⟪ar:انسانی قامت⟫ are resurrected in human stature, the punishment they endured erased from memory. ⟪ar:انسانی قامت⟫ They are then invited anew: if they accept, ⟪ar:فبھا⟫ salvation is theirs; if not, they descend again to the extremities. Thus does the divine mill turn eternally.

## The Angels of Kindness and the Angels of Wrath

⟪ar:صاحب رسائل اخوان الصفاء⟫ The author of the Epistles of the Brethren of Purity and ⟪ar:مولانا امام احمد⟫ Mawlānā Imām Ahmad affirm: "⟪ar:صورات خبیثہ⟫ The foul forms—⟪ar:ملائکۃ الغضبان⟫ the Angels of Wrath—drive them forth at the command of ⟪ar:عالم قدس⟫ the Holy World." ⟪ar:عاشر علیہ السلام، عالم طبعیت⟫ The Tenth One upon him be peace, the World of Nature, delegates ⟪ar:'مدبر'⟫ the manager and these ⟪ar:'مالک'⟫ guardians; He arranges all things by their celestial trumpets in hierarchical rank. And just as there is a chapter for the holy world, so there is one for the natural world; just as every Imam has a religious chapter, so ⟪ar:'رضوان'⟫ Ridwān—the Treasurer of the Gardens—is designated. Every ⟪ar:نفس صالحہ⟫ virtuous soul has an attendant. ⟪ar:'رضوان'⟫ Ridwān is called the sun because he is the chapter of the cosmos and the magnet drawing all goodness toward ⟪ar:نفوس ریحیہ⟫ the luminous souls. The virtuous and chaste among the outward people also attain such souls.

The same ⟪ar:ملائکۃ الغضبان⟫ Angels of Wrath appear under the name ⟪ar:'زحل'⟫ Saturn because he is the custodian of casting down the foul soul into Saqqara through his rays and the rays of the faithful. Your statement that the darkness emptied of the body points to ⟪ar:وسط سقرا⟫ the center of Saqqara, where ⟪ar:نفوس خبیثہ⟫ foul souls reach darkness, and where they ⟪ar:عذاب ألیم⟫ burn in painful torment. There they are reminded of the lesser punishment and reminded of the old torments about them, before they ⟪ar:'عذاب اکبر'⟫ bear the great punishment.[^cite-20]

And ⟪ar:صاحب رسائل⟫ the author of the Epistles recounts that the waves of Hell sometimes lift them ⟪ar:برد زمحریر⟫ toward cold and frost, sometimes cast them downward ⟪ar:حرارت أسیر⟫ toward imprisoned heat—a description of how one who dwells at the center of ⟪ar:اطراف شمالی⟫ the northern extremity—⟪ar:اسیر⟫ in captive heat—endures torment, and then one at the center of ⟪ar:اطراف جنوبی⟫ the southern extremity—⟪ar:زمحریر⟫ in crushing cold—suffers severe affliction. When the devils fall with them, this refers to their scholars and leaders who share their torment. ⟪ar:عقول مجردۃ⟫ The unembodied intellects send punishment through these devils and ⟪ar:صورات خبیثہ⟫ foul forms—⟪ar:شہاب ثاقب⟫ piercing meteors—and when a believer or any ⟪ar:'حدود'⟫ limit-holder curses them, it affects them. ⟪ar:عقول مجردہ⟫ The unembodied intellects broadcast their faults, curse them mercilessly, and inflict severe punishment. When cursed, they are intensified by the rays of ⟪ar:کرہ اسیر⟫ the imprisoned sphere and by the rays of ⟪ar:کرہ زمحریر⟫ the frozen sphere, and such punishment reaches them. This ⟪ar:'شمس وقمر'⟫ (the sun and moon) by way of ⟪ar:ملائکہ بالقوۃ⟫ the angels in potentiality—the ⟪ar:'حدود'⟫ divine limits—is how ⟪ar:ملائکہ بالقوۃ⟫ they operate. When these forms dwell in this physical world, it is paradise for them rather than the ⟪ar:عذاب ادنی و عذاب اکبر⟫ lesser and greater punishments that await them.[^cite-21]

## How Forbidden Deeds Receive Their Recompense

When a person commits that which is forbidden—transgressing what has been enjoined by no authority—his own ⟪ar:جوہر نفس⟫ essence of soul darkens swiftly. His wicked deeds obstruct him from the path of guidance; they soil his soul and lead him astray, ensnaring him in sin's snare. These misdeeds then incite enmity toward the limits (ḥudūd) of truth and ultimately propel him toward Hell.

**A Principle of Divine Justice:** Allah forgives sins committed against Himself, yet He does not forgive sins against His servants, except through a means by which Allah reconciles the accounts between them, fulfilling retribution.[^cite-4]

When obscene acts—⟪ar:'زنا '⟫ adultery or like transgressions—are committed, retribution becomes obligatory, for such deeds darken the essence of the soul with terrible swiftness. First, he is clothed in ⟪ar:'رجس'⟫ filth—a punishment in human form wherein he completes his retribution. He is then garbed in ⟪ar:'رقص'⟫ the garment of shame through an act of marriage, whereby faces turn inward to breasts. Subsequently he is clothed in ⟪ar:'عکس'⟫ the garment of reversal, fulfilling retribution through matrimonial union. In each instance, the magnitude depends upon the abundance or scarcity of his sin in the world.

It often occurs that many have committed adultery with a single woman. Her retribution is fulfilled by dressing her in differing garments, in each of which she is married anew. It has been observed that the swine itself incites its female to copulate with other beasts; and at times even such unions transpire with mutual pleasure and will, because ⟪ar:قامت الفیہ⟫ they too perform this act willingly and with consent.[^cite-5]

## The Death and Return of the Righteous

Those who, though they take not the pledge of the Imam, follow the outward commandments of Islam—who do not oppress, who remain chaste, pious, benevolent, truthful, and faithful; who do not recognize the guardianship of the Prophet and his successor, yet harbor no rancor toward the Imams—such are called the ⟪ar:'صلحاء'⟫ righteous. When they depart this life, the spirituality of the sun and Venus stirs them; their soul expands through their bodies. Their temperatures cool and their blood congeals. The imagination they have created through their outward deeds leaves their bodies.

**A Divine Truth:** Allah wastes not the good of anyone. "Evil has no root in creation" (⟪ar-quote:اَلشَّرُّ لاَ اَصلُ لَہُ فِی اِلبدَاء⟫). Though a disbeliever performs a good deed, he receives its reward. Allah recompenses the righteous deeds of such people through elevation, even though they have not achieved ⟪ar:خاتمہ بالخیر⟫ a good end.

> ⟪quran 6:160⟫
> ⟪ar:‏مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا ۖ وَمَن جَآءَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجْزَىٰٓ إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ ‎⟫
> 
> *"Whoever brings a good deed shall have ten times the like thereof to his credit, and whoever brings an evil deed shall have only the recompense of the like thereof, and they will not be wronged."*

This noble conception first ascends to the moon; the moon then conveys it to the sun. Once the imagination reaches the solar realm, fermentation and purification occur. The concept remains in the sun until its appointed return. Gradually the body dissolves, rising through evaporation until it reaches the moon and the middle spheres. Thence it descends in rain and is absorbed into pure, wholesome substance. This nourishment is consumed by his parents, from which sperm is produced, and he appears anew in the world. Upon birth, he receives from the ⟪ar:نفس نامیہ⟫ vegetative soul; upon emergence from the womb, his formation derives from the sun through Venus and the moon, connecting with body and soul. That ⟪ar:نفس حسیہ⟫ sensible soul, together with the ⟪ar:نامیہ⟫ vegetative principle that had dispersed through his body after death, now converges. These three—body, soul, and imagination—unite and become ⟪ar:ممازج⟫ unified. His condition is now superior to before, more exalted, grand, and honorable. This is the recompense of his good deeds, which Allah bestows upon him.[^cite-6]

The example is that of a traveler who departs his home and family, living in poverty abroad until acquiring wealth, then returning in better estate than before. By contrast, one who departs and never returns—whose imagination, soul, and body are all lost—suffers a form of punishment.

## The Death and Return of the Disbeliever

Save for ⟪ar:مقاصرین⟫ the defaulting believers and ⟪ar:صلحا⟫ the righteous, all other people merit punishment and endure grievous torments at death. After death, they undergo the most severe afflictions. A slight difference exists between the death of a Muslim and a disbeliever—provided the Muslim harbors no rancor against ʿAlī and his descendants.

**A Parable:** ⟪ar:حضرت ضیا علی صاحب⟫ A certain master, citing an example, declared: "If a ladder stands and people of every sect climb it, he who falls from the top suffers greater hurt than he who falls from below." Since the Bohra community has approached nearest, they shall suffer most intensely after death.

When disbelievers and adversaries of the Imams and saints approach their final hour, the ⟪ar:جوزہر ظلمانی (عقدتین)⟫ dark essence (the two knots) stirs within them—for both are magnets drawing every wicked form. It pulls forth the sinister configuration of stubbornness. Since his lord possesses no narrator to attract his senses, his soul becomes ⟪ar:'شائع'⟫ dispersed throughout his body like mercury from a shattered thermometer. His self transforms into body-form, the two merging into one thing. From both emerges his ⟪ar:تصور خبیث⟫ evil imagination and ⟪ar:نفس ہوائیہ⟫ airy soul—that part remaining in his body—while his body is left with that which is termed in the language of the invitation ⟪ar:'حُصالات'⟫ (the vessels).

**An Origin and Duration:** The self confined within the body represents progress; the self dispersed into the body signifies degradation. Even if the body burns, its components remain, for what Allah has created cannot be annihilated—only its form changes; existence cannot become non-existent.

### How the Concept of Evil Arises

His evil imagination constitutes in fact his beliefs and misdeeds, created through obstinacy toward the Imams and saints or through separation from them. This concept is called ⟪ar:'نفس ظلمانیۃ ابلیسیۃ شیطانیۃ '⟫ a dark, Iblis-like, demonic soul. Sometimes it assumes ⟪ar:صورت شیطانیہ⟫ a fiery form—the fire that consumes the burned or their possessions. At times this concept lodges in the body and does not depart; that body is entombed with ⟪ar:نفس شیطانیہ⟫ the demonic soul, which then burns the body for a period, inflicting punishment. It has been witnessed that at night the grave of such a person blazes with pride; sometimes the grave itself appears afire, yet upon approach no flame is found. The man within, burned and tormented by his own imagination, is all the more wicked in deed and fierce in enmity.[^cite-7]

### Grave Punishment

He is buried in his grave alongside a non-believer ⟪ar:حسیہ⟫ sensible presence, his state resembling one buried alive. When he perceives his wicked form, terror grips him; he prays that a vast distance separate him from this evil figure—as Allah declares:

> ⟪quran 3:30⟫
> ⟪ar:‏يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ مَّا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍۢ مُّحْضَرًۭا وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِن سُوٓءٍۢ تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُۥٓ أَمَدًۢا بَعِيدًۭا ۗ وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسَهُۥ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفٌۢ بِٱلْعِبَادِ ‎⟫
> 
> *"On the Day when every person will be confronted with all the good he has done, and all the evil he has done, he will wish that there were a great distance between him and his evil. And Allah warns you against Himself (His Punishment) and Allah is full of Kindness to the (His) slaves."*

Thereafter he beholds the Divine Universe, which ⟪ar:علی ابن ابی طالب علیہ السلام⟫ the Imam grants him—a taste of Hell itself.

For forty days after burial, this figure circumambulates the sides of her grave, striving to escape the physical world and reach the realm of light, only to be drawn back by celestial rays. She attempts to reconnect with her body but cannot; she merely circles the corpse in anguished longing, a state of exquisite pain. As the grave-torment approaches its end, she grows maddened and shrieks and wails. This is why the sounds of lamentation are heard at night in cemeteries, and sometimes the words ⟪ar:'عنیم'⟫ of the anguished are audible. In her desperate attempt to enter the body, she strikes it with such force that severe pain radiates through it, for the entire sensation inheres in it.[^cite-8]

## The Wandering of Evil Forms

After forty days, when this evil form separates from the body, it shapes itself as it wishes and acts as it desires. Having departed the body's confinement, it has reached the extremity of its wickedness. While embodied, its powers were limited—it was ⟪ar:شیطان بالقوۃ⟫ a satan in potentiality; now separated, restraint vanishes and it becomes ⟪ar:شیطان بالفعل⟫ a satan in actuality. The body was its prison, from which it has now been freed. It is the justice of Allah that He does not prevent the wicked from fulfilling their retribution. Simultaneously, punishment accrues whether the wicked person acts willingly or unwillingly. Upon emerging from the grave, it moves between heaven and earth. Thus the Messenger of Allah ⟪ar:رسول اللہ صلعم⟫ declared: "The air is neither empty nor full" (neither devoid of such forms nor crowded with them).

This evil form, having left its body, works against the righteous, though only against those with whom accounts remain unsettled. It cannot trouble everyone. Some of these wicked forms sometimes speak truth, for though they were wicked in the flesh, they spoke truthfully alongside their wickedness. Nostradamus's predictions, for instance, held some accuracy because the spirits informing him conveyed truth; this reflects Allah's justice, for He does not destroy the good and evil of anyone.

According to ⟪ar:رسول اللہ صلعم⟫ the Messenger of Allah, the ⟪ar:صورات خبیثہ⟫ evil forms affect only the ignorant—men, women, and children. All actions spring from fear of their ⟪ar:صورات خبیثہ⟫ evil manifestations. Even in sleep, those who pray ⟪ar:صورات خبیثہ⟫ for protection from their influence do so because their ⟪ar:صورات خبیثہ⟫ machinations are released at night. These evil spirits enter the dreams of sleepers, relating events both true and false. When any come to pass, people deem them truthful and are thereby corrupted, their hatred intensified. Whoever opposes the Imam becomes a ⟪ar:جن مزموم⟫ condemned jinn, sustained in enmity and malice. For this reason, when passing through filthy places like desolate wastelands, we seek protection, for these are the abodes of such evil ones.

So long as the wise one does not will it, the evil state remains unchanged. It shelters only in desolate, dark dwellings; in foul-smelling locales; in deserts and wastes; along paths and crossroads; in horrific places; in slaughterhouses and toilets. Sometimes in the sleep of wicked people akin to it, it appears imaginatively and speaks according to their evil beliefs, further corrupting them and increasing enmity toward the righteous. Thus Allah declares:

> ⟪quran 6:112⟫
> ⟪ar:‏وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِىٍّ عَدُوًّۭا شَيَطِينَ ٱلْإِنسِ وَٱلْجِنِّ يُوحِى بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ زُخْرُفَ ٱلْقَوْلِ غُرُورًۭا ۚ وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ مَا فَعَلُوهُ ۖ فَذَرْهُمْ وَمَا يَفْتَرُونَ ‎⟫
> 
> *"And so We have appointed for every Prophet enemies—Shayatin (devils) among mankind and jinns, inspiring one another with adorned speech as a delusion. If your Lord had so willed, they would not have done it, so leave them alone with their fabrications."*

The ignorant—be they man or woman or child—to whom this form whispers are visited by this evil state, which common folk call "possession" (or the jinn). The evil form then speaks in the tongue of the man or woman, narrating coming events in their language. Yet even then, it tells both truth and falsehood, and commands the ignorant to sin. Sometimes it departs and seeks another vessel; sometimes it cleaves to him, refusing to leave until death. These are called ⟪ar:'جنات مزموم'⟫ condemned jinn—⟪ar:شیاطین⟫ demons and ⟪ar:أفاریط⟫ the most wicked—who flee in amazement when the Qur'an is recited.

Elsewhere, such forms are deployed to emphasize the evils of the wicked against the righteous, intensifying enmity and inclining hearts toward the adversary's words. They affirm and obey this form, committing what it commands. All occurs because of similarity between these people and the wicked. In the same manner, it whispers into the hearts of the righteous, leading them astray and drawing them toward ⟪ar:ابلیسیت⟫ Iblis-like states, plunging them into sin.

When such a person dies, they are left behind and ⟪ar:عقدتین⟫ absorbed into the two knots—their barzakh (intermediate realm)—joining the congregation of former wicked forms. In this state they are ⟪ar:'شیاطین بالقوۃ '⟫ satans in potentiality. Then they descend to earth, and ⟪ar:قامت الفیہ⟫ they reach ⟪ar:شیاطین بالفعل⟫ satans in actuality. Previously they accomplished wickedness through intermediaries; now they possess the power to act wickedly themselves. When the ⟪ar:حجاب امام⟫ Veil of the Imam—through whom retributions are fulfilled—appears, they too manifest in the world to accomplish their revenge. Of these, those whose ⟪ar:صورات خبیثہ⟫ evil forms become Muslim are termed ⟪ar:'جن محمود '⟫ commendable jinn, while those persisting in disobedience remain ⟪ar:'جن مزموم '⟫ condemned jinn. Many deny the existence of jinn through ignorance.

Beneath the moon are two stars shaped as a dragon. These two heavens fall not within circumferential circles—they are frozen in place, outside the celestial spheres. ⟪ar:اھبطو⟫ Those who descend continue sinning in their state and remain steadfast in stubbornness. Within the Saqqara that lies in the earth, the multitude are punished; ⟪ar:راس و زنب⟫ the head and the tail—along with ⟪ar:صورات خبیثہ⟫ their evil forms—are punished. These two stars have become magnets for wicked images. From there, these evils cast their maleficent effects upon this world, causing all misfortunes and sinful deeds. Their tactics oppose those of ⟪ar:امام علیہ السلام⟫ the Imam. Before being cast into Saqqara, these wicked figures are clothed. At solar and lunar eclipses, the machinations of these three knots commence. These evil conceptions remain in this world as long as the wise man permits, continuing to influence his likes and dislikes.

**A Fact:** In Ras reside the enemies of Noah; in Zanab, the enemies of the Awsiyyas and Imams. Therefore, Zanab is more evil than Ras. Ras is the principal and Zanab his minister, or Ras is the devil and Zanab the assistant-devil. On the Day of ʿĀshūrā, these wicked ones attached themselves to the hearts of ⟪ar:شمر زلجوشن⟫ Shimr (the cursed), causing them to perpetrate the evil of the martyrdom of ⟪ar:امام حسین⟫ Imam al-Ḥusayn. Likewise, this wicked form ⟪ar:ملعون ابن ملجم⟫ struck the accursed Ibn Muljam's blow against ⟪ar:امیر المومنین⟫ the Commander of the Faithful.

After traversing the seven realizations, when they reach the final stage of punishment, angels lead them to severe torment. The waves of Hell lift them to ⟪ar:اسیر⟫ the fire-sphere's heat, then cast them to ⟪ar:زمحریر⟫ the cold-sphere's depths. The angels strike them with ⟪ar:شہاب ساقب⟫ shooting stars (⟪ar:رجم⟫ lapidation). They remain thus as long as earth and sky rotate. When the appearance of ⟪ar:قائم علیہ السلام⟫ the Qāʾim draws near, those ⟪ar:خبیث نفوس⟫ evil souls appear in the world. Their trumpets, ⟪ar:جسم⟫ embodied in filthy form as fire, consume them to ash. This ash then enters ⟪ar:وسط سقرا⟫ the middle of Saqqara through the rays of Saturn and Mars, where they endure torment for ⟪ar:کور اعظم⟫ a very long time.[^cite-9]

## Evil Forms as the Opposites of the Sacred Stations

There is a gathering of wicked concepts—the ⟪ar:عقدتین⟫ two knots. They are granted respite so that the person with whom they are to be reckoned may appear in this world. When both are present and the hour of retribution comes, then the ⟪ar:صورات خبیثہ⟫ evil forms complete their ⟪ar:قصاصات⟫ retribution. By the will of the wise one, these verses fall from the Aqṭaʿīn to the earth and are absorbed into food and drink. Those foods reach the worthy—whether from among the saints or the elders. This is why ⟪ar:جناب آدم⟫ the lineage of Adam produces ⟪ar:قابیل⟫ Cain-like offspring and why the children of the Imams multiply; these wicked ingredients do not affect the righteous who consume them, but are rendered apparent through them. Similarly, the idols fashioned are composed of these same wicked ingredients.

When they are buried, their bodies rot and decompose in the grave; their components scatter into the four elements and the body dissolves into the Ummah. Vapors ascend to fire, breath to air, mucus to water, and sodium to the ground. These four vapors are then collected from the universe, forming clouds that rain upon the earth. They penetrate water, soil, and humans to retrieve their residual wicked components, becoming incorporated into the bodies of corrupt plants and animals—which are then consumed by the wicked similar to them. Thus do these forbidden ones gather their likes, either to lead them to ⟪ar:برازق جہنم⟫ the provisions of Hell or to bring forth their offspring. They remain as a ⟪ar:سلالہ⟫ heritage until the wise one wills their reappearance.

When his time comes, he appears as a child through his parents, ⟪ar:شیطان بالقوۃ⟫ a satan in potentiality, trained until he becomes ⟪ar:شیطان بالفعل⟫ a satan in actuality. He then claims the rank of truth whilst concealing its real status. Sometimes he becomes so obstinate, intending to kill the Imam as ⟪ar:حارث بن مرۃ⟫ Ḥārith ibn Murrah hid his inner treachery, and as ⟪ar:قابیل⟫ Cain slew ⟪ar:آدم علیہ السلام⟫ in his hatred of ⟪ar:ھابیل⟫ Abel, seeking to usurp his station.

Likewise, there existed one who was the opposite of the Prophet ⟪ar:نوح علیہ السلام⟫ Noah; one opposite to ⟪ar:سام⟫ Sham was ⟪ar:ہام⟫ Ham, who slew him; ⟪ar:نمرود⟫ Nimrod opposed ⟪ar:ابراھیم⟫ Abraham; ⟪ar:سحر بوتا⟫ sorcery-wielders opposed them. ⟪ar:ابی جہل⟫ Abū Jahl and ⟪ar:ولید بن مسعب⟫ al-Walīd ibn Mus'ab opposed ⟪ar:موسیٰ⟫ Moses and ⟪ar:عیسی⟫ Jesus. ⟪ar:ابی لہب⟫ Abū Lahab opposed the Prophet. For this reason, the Messenger of Allah declared: "There was a devil for every prophet, but two for me." Such likewise were the adversaries against ⟪ar:ابو بکر⟫ Abū Bakr and ⟪ar:عمر⟫ ʿUmar and ⟪ar:علی ابن ابی طالب⟫ ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and ⟪ar:ابن ملجم⟫ Ibn Muljam the cursed, who struck the fatal blow. ⟪ar:معاویہ امام حسن⟫ Muʿāwiyah was the stubbornness that poisoned and killed Imam al-Ḥasan through his wife ⟪ar:'جعدۃ بنت عشس'⟫ Jaʿdah. It was the same stubbornness that ⟪ar:یزید امام حسین⟫ Yazīd brought forth to cause the martyrdom of Imam al-Ḥusayn through ⟪ar:شمر لعین⟫ Shimr the cursed. Thus ⟪ar:مولانا مستنصر باللہ⟫ al-Mustanṣir poisoners, and ⟪ar:شمرۃ الخیبریۀ⟫ the poisoness of Khaybar killed ⟪ar:رسول اللہ صلی اللہ علیہ و آلہ وسلم⟫ the Messenger of Allah himself. Two people shared a meal with the Prophet; when one died, the Prophet prayed for the other, saving him from the poison's effects. Yet the poison remained with the Prophet until it led to his death—poison that came from the Aqṭaʿīn itself.

**A Fact:** ⟪ar:رسول اللہ (ﷺ)⟫ The Messenger mixed poison into meat with a plant. The moment she placed the herb in her mouth, she cried, "O Messenger of Allah, poison is mixed in me!" He immediately spat it out. The herb was indeed composed of plant and poison ingredients; because the herb's rank exceeded the poison's, it revealed its true condition to the Messenger.

Sometimes these evil forms dwelling in the Aqṭaʿīn become manifest in a plant, rendering it poisonous—causing the death of an Imam or a Nāṭiq (Speaker). Such poison reached the Prophet or Imam al-Ḥasan. When these wicked forms descend toward minerals, they take the form ⟪ar:برزق ظلمانی⟫ of dark provisions—knives and swords—used to attack and fulfill ⟪ar:مقامات شریفہ⟫ retribution against the sacred stations. Arrows fashioned from minerals become ⟪ar:نبل⟫ arrows that with the bow attack and slay the bearers of ⟪ar:مقامات شریفہ⟫ the sacred stations. The swords of ⟪ar:شمر اور ابن ملجم لعنت اللہ علیھم⟫ Shimr and Ibn Muljam—may Allah's curse be upon them—were collections of such wicked forms.

All is executed under the guidance of the wise one (ʿAlayhi ʾl-Salām) and according to Allah Almighty's balance of justice. The guardians of these evil forms are the three Aqids, protecting them until the one with whom they must reckon appears. If there are Imams ⟪ar:صاحب سیف⟫ (wielders of the sword), they set limits on the sinners, striking or slaying them. When such people die, their evil form differs from the ⟪ar:عقدتین⟫ two knots, appearing in the form of poison and sword to complete the reckoning with the Imam. This is Allah's mighty justice.

The person who delivers this poison to the sacred place is himself a combination of these accursed forms. First come the evil conceptions compounded into three beliefs. Apart from these, the curses inflicted upon them remain separate, lodged in the beliefs. When the most wicked person in the world appears, all these curses emanate from the Aqṭaʿīn and accumulate in that person. When such a one commits atrocities, he wreaks injustice upon the entire age—all are encompassed in his arms. The Universe cursed the people of Kūfah and Iraq because they abandoned him at the crucial hour and oppressed him. You cursed them, saying you would send upon them a man who would afflict them all most severely. These curses were gathered in the Aqṭaʿīn, then ⟪ar:حجاج بن یوسف السقفی⟫ al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf, a most cruel person, emerged from the Aqṭaʿīn, inflicting terrible atrocities upon the people of Iraq and Kūfah.[^cite-10]

## Munkar and Nakīr (The Evil Form)

⟪ar:آنحضرت صلعم⟫ According to the Messenger of Allah, it is well known that at the moment of death, two angels appear—⟪ar:'مبشروبشیر'⟫ bearers of glad tidings and bearers of tidings. The reality is that the Speaker and Guardian of every age is, for those who love him, a ⟪ar:مبشر و بشیر⟫ herald of good news, whilst for those who hate him he is a ⟪ar:منکر و نکیر⟫ denier and interrogator. In the same manner, the Imam of the age is for his contemporaries both a ⟪ar:مبشر و بشیر⟫ herald of glad tidings and a ⟪ar:منکر و نکیر⟫ denier to others. Therefore ⟪ar:مولانا امیر المومنین⟫ our Master, the Commander of the Faithful, declared: "O ⟪ar:حار ھمدان⟫ Ḥār of Hamadān, whoever dies shall see me, whether believer or hypocrite, shortly thereafter. I know him by his eyes; he knows me by my names, surnames, and deeds."

### Denial and Denial of Multiplication (The Evil Form)

By contrast, the obstinate one, through ignorance, becomes an enemy of his Lord and claims what he does not deserve. He becomes the leader of misguidance and ignorance. When his evil imagination departs his body, he becomes a devil; his soul does not leave his body but he ⟪ar:اسفل السافلین⟫ descends to the lowest of the low. Then He reveals to those like him, misleading them, frightening them in sleep and wakefulness, moving between earth and sky, making corrupt places his dwelling. Allah says to them: "We have made them leaders calling to the Fire; they shall find no help on the Day of Resurrection."

When he dies, he acts by the plan of Allah (upon him be peace), which differs from him—the ⟪ar:عقدتین⟫ two knots—a ⟪ar:ابلیسی علم⟫ demonic science and ⟪ar:خبیث افعال⟫ wicked deeds prepared through stubbornness and enmity toward the people of truth. The form he made in his lifetime becomes at death a ⟪ar:'شخص مظلم'⟫ dark figure, most terrifying. He dislikes to see her and becomes terrified. That evil form frightens and harms him, becoming terrible to him. Then he knows he is ⟪ar:'اہل شر'⟫ among the people of evil.

The Messenger of Allah told ⟪ar:قیس ابن آسم⟫ Qays ibn Āsim: "O Qays, you have a companion with whom you shall be buried, alive while you are dead. If you are good to him, he shall be merciful to you; if you are evil to him, he shall deliver you to torment. Your resurrection shall be with him, and you shall be questioned about this companion. Make this companion virtuous! If he is good, you shall take pleasure; if he is bad, you shall derive horror from him. He is your ⟪ar:'عمل '⟫ deed." ⟪ar:سیدنا حمید الدین⟫ Our Master Ḥamīd al-Dīn, pointing to the same, said to Azdā: "His evil deeds become beasts that frighten and hurt him."[^cite-11]

## The Lesser Torments

After death, the believer's body becomes the self—his development—while the disbeliever's soul disperses into the body so that torment upon the body reaches his feeling. Soul and body unite and merge with the soil, then rise like vapor and fall like rain. This rain produces lightning and thunder—deadly strikes—and floods that drown nations and destroy fields, producing a cold most painful. The ⟪ar:حصالات⟫ effects of these evil forms, when they trouble this world, are also included in this action. They are then escorted to the courtyard and led to the Bridges of Punishment, which possess seventy garments in each category and seventy rings in each garment. The person passes through all these garments in torment and testifies that he entered this realm through his denial of truth. At each turn, he is told what crime brings punishment. Without this knowledge, there is no punishment; but as he suffers, awareness may be withheld.

### Abomination

When their ⟪ar:حصالات⟫ rain falls to earth, plants grow from which animals feed. The beast then enters the food of one destined to manifest this wicked form as sperm—for the first is the ⟪ar:'بشری'⟫ human garment. These are nations with whom the righteous cannot speak. He passes through seventy species of this realm and seventy rings of each species.

### Simian Stage

When he leaves the first door, he enters the second—a form between human and monkey. He is then clothed with seventy garments of this type, each with seventy rings—a time of bestiality and monkey-nature. Those who committed adultery and drank wine are brought into this category. As the monkey is naturally inclined to adultery, so the wrench naturally inclines to eating and drinking intoxicants. The actions they performed happily in the world, nature now imposes as punishment. They commit adultery repeatedly, an itch never satisfied no matter how often sated.

**A Fact:** If believers commit similar sins, they too are brought to this torment and punished. Yet they need not pass through seventy garments and seventy rings in each. Nature punishes them according to justice, then restores them to human stature.

### Wild Beasts

The third category is that of wild ⟪ar:بری و بحری⟫ land and sea beasts: lions, leopards, foxes, and creatures with claws and fangs. They feel these torments fully, tearing and devouring one another, fulfilling their stories. After donning the seventy garments, they progress to the next door.

### Mute Beasts

This is the station of the dumb. Until now, beasts could vocalize; in this stage, they become ⟪ar:'⟫ mute ⟪ar:'⟫. These are ⟪ar:بر و بحر⟫ creatures moving by rubbing the ground—deer, snakes, rats, scorpions, etc.

### Birds

The bird realm. Predatory birds such as eagles, crows, and hawks.

### Vegetation

It ends in this realm—the stage of the vegetative. Thus Allah says: "You shall be returned to old age." It is ignorance after knowledge, where only ⟪ar:'نمو'⟫ growth remains. These are corrupt plants that destroy living beings.

### Minerals

The final strain—vile minerals: hard, filthy stones used in base construction.
