# Sat Minds



## Spiritual Invitation and the Seven Intellects

When both the al-ʿAql al-Awwal (the First Intellect) and the first emanator attained kamāl thānī (secondary perfection), they resolved that they should unite and summon all ⟪ar:اشباح نورانیہ⟫the luminous forms so that these beings, like themselves, might succeed in the tawhīd (monotheistic devotion) of the Creator and attain secondary perfection. For this purpose, the First Intellect appointed the first emanator as his wife and hijāb (veil), commanding him to invite all the remaining souls to the tawhīd of the Creator. Thus began the daʿwa (the summons), the spiritual invitation. Prior to this, no summons had been established in the realm of spirit.

The supplications allude subtly to this moment, saying, "When the two met, the applause began." Just as both hands clap and their sound resonates outward to affect others, so too did the First Intellect and the first source meet, issuing forth the daʿwa to all beings toward tawhīd.[^cite-1]

The sole purpose of every invitation is the submission of nature—the transformation from kamāl awwal (primary perfection) to kamāl thānī (secondary perfection), from jismāniyyat (corporeality) to rūḥāniyyat (spirituality). The first source established his daʿwa in the spiritual realm by command of the First Intellect, calling all toward the tawhīd of the Creator (may He be glorified and exalted). No obstacle or materiality existed in the spiritual world to prevent these luminous forms from accepting the invitation, for they were masters of all knowledge, life, and power, requiring no external summons. Yet because they did not exercise their authority spontaneously, the caller had to invoke them. All these unnumbered beings received the same feast of invitation equally—none was offered less, none more.

Although the daʿwa extended equally to all beings, its primary purpose was to remove the waywardness of the second source ⟪ar:'وحم مساوات'⟫. An analogy illuminates this: when one part of cloth becomes soiled, though the whole cloth is washed uniformly, the cleansing action concentrates at the point of dirt. Similarly, though the invitation reached all souls equally, the main aim concerned the correction of the second source. [^cite-2]

Responding to ⟪ar:أجابت⟫ the daʿwa of the first munbaʿith (the Emanator), each successive intellect began to answer and advance toward the tawhīd of the Creator of the Almighty, until seven intellects and their circles were established in correspondence to the seven letters of Sūrat al-Ikhlās. Each acknowledged the tawhīd of the Creator, recognized the majesty and prestige of the first and second intellects, and acknowledged the precedence of the intellect that preceded it within its horizon. This act bound these intellects through tawhīd to ⟪ar:مواد الٰہی⟫the divine substance, and through the First Intellect—itself the ⟪ar:ھیولی⟫primordial matter and ⟪ar:صورت⟫form—all attained perfection.[^cite-3]

## Circle and Its Center

The chiefs and members of the circle were all called ⟪ar:عقول⟫intellects, and among them a hierarchy of highest to lowest was established. Yet the last member of the sixth circle of intellect surpassed the chief of the seventh, though the former held membership while the latter held leadership. The First Intellect, having made no invitation, formed no circle; only the one who summons establishes a circle. For this reason, the circular form ranks as the noblest among all forms.

In the spiritual realm, all seven intellects arose because of the kalimah lā ilāha illā-Allāh ⟪ar:کلمہ لا الہ الا اللہ⟫—the utterance "There is no god but God." The first letter corresponds to the First Intellect, and the seven letters that follow correspond to the seven intellects. Just as these letters combine to form the word, so too shall these seven intellects be integrated into the realm of the first source on the Day of Resurrection. The verses shall join as the word; the First Source is the whole, and the seven intellects are its parts. This assemblage is called the 8 Aʿquls ⟪ar:'**ملائکۃ حملۃ العرش**'⟫—the angels who carry the Throne and have lifted up the First Intellect. These eight angels are, in truth, the eight gates of Paradise, of which the circle of the first angel is the highest heaven.

| Kalimah | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First Source | Third Mind | Fourth Mind | Fifth Mind | Sixth Mind | Seventh Mind | Intellect Eighth | Ninth Mind |
| *Lā ilāha illā-Allāh* | Lā | A | Lā | A | Lā | A | Llāh |

Each of these seven intellects came into being through the intellect of its predecessor. The First Intellect was commanded to invoke until the Second Intellect was established. Thereafter, the Second Intellect's last member was ordered to issue the daʿwa, thus forming the Third Intellect, and this process continued until all seven intellects and their circles were constituted. Each intellect was established through the daʿwa of its predecessor's final member.

In the word of tawhīd, seven stanzas arise when the pen lifts from the tablet and then descends again upon it. The pen's rise signals the completion of an intellect's feast; its fall signifies that the last member of that circle now issues the daʿwa. That is, when the feast of lā ⟪ar:' لا '⟫ was completed, the last member received command to feast. At his daʿwa, the circle began forming from those who ⟪ar:لب بیک⟫answered the call. Then, at the invitation of that last member, one was born at ⟪ar:' لہ'⟫. This process continued until the word of tawhīd was complete and the seven intellects established.

Each circle pointed toward its center, for without center, no circle could exist. Each circle stood amazed at the greatness of its center, circumambulating it in wonder and seeking knowledge, much as one circles the Kaʿba. The First Intellect marvels at the Creator of the Almighty, since the Creator is the center of the First Intellect, which revolves around Him in wonder and knowledge. In like manner, the First Intellect is the center of the Second Intellect, and the Second revolves around it in amazement at its majesty. God fashions each center for its own sphere. Whosoever is astonished at His greatness is called to Him; thus we call Him Allāh ⟪ar:'اللہ'⟫, because the First Intellect was the first to be astonished at Him, and having declared tawhīd, pointed toward Him. So too did all intellects marvel at the greatness and knowledge of the First Intellect, leading to the appellation ⟪ar:'اللہ'⟫"First Intellect."

In another sense, the center signifies quiescence and the circle signifies motion. Tranquility surpasses motion, for the center's stillness derives from its constancy, while the circle's motion arises from its wonder. The final tranquility of every motion is the essence of the First Intellect. Motion within the realm of the First Intellect is exceedingly subtle. Were it not for this slightest gesture, it would rest in the peace of the Almighty. This motion is a gesture of praise to His Creator, which ⟪ar:سورۃ الفاتحۃ⟫the opening sūra of the Qurʾān ⟪ar:'الحمد'⟫—"The Praise"—signifies.

When this motion and quiescence entered the temporal world, the imprint reversed itself. Tranquility became a symbol of death; motion became a symbol of life. Since we have not heeded the invitation of the intellect in the spiritual world, we must fulfill this action through the daʿwa of the Imāms, so that we may attain the peace of the Hereafter. All our deeds are for the sake of God's tranquility.

## The Circles of the Intellects

When the people of tawhīd advanced toward the Creator of tawhīd, they were joined by their circles, whom they called the Raʾīs (chief). When the first emanator moved toward the tawhīd of the Creator, a number of souls came forward, met his gaze, and became monotheistic in his monotheism. For this state he prays: ⟪ar-quote:النَّظَرُ بِنَظَرِہِ و اَلبَصَرُ بِبَصَرِہِ⟫"Seeing by his seeing and perceiving by his perceiving." These souls became the realm of the Second Intellect, and he became their chief or leader. When the circle's number reached twenty-seven—and some texts say one hundred—the last member of the circle was commanded to issue the daʿwa. An analogy: when the Imām steps forward to lead prayer, the people rise and join him upon seeing him. He is called their chief or imām, and all others become his followers. The entire congregation prays, yet the precedence of the one who stood first is established.[^cite-4]

The master Sayyidnā ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān (may God sanctify his spirit) ⟪ar:سیدنا علی بن سلیمان اعلی اﷲ قدسہ⟫ mentions twelve chiefs in the circle of the first source. One hundred years later, Sayyidnā Ḥasan ibn Hibat Allāh (may God sanctify his spirit) ⟪ar:سیدنا حسن بن ھبۃ اللہ صاحب⟫ mentioned twenty-eight chiefs in the same circle. When Sayyidnā ʿAlī ibn ʿAlī (may God raise his rank) ⟪ar:سیدنا علی بن علی اعلی اللہ قدسہ⟫ inquired of this discrepancy, he explained that the difference arose because Sayyidnā ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān ⟪ar:سیدنا علی بن سلیمان⟫ spoke of the parts, while Sayyidnā Ḥasan ⟪ar:سیدنا حسن⟫ spoke of the whole. A comparison: two persons viewing the same book—one looking from a distance sees only pages, while one looking closely sees both pages and words. Both accounts are thus correct. The first source encompasses a grouping of twenty-eight, a group of one hundred, and a group of twelve.

When the last member of the circle of the first source called all to tawhīd, at his daʿwa an intellect advanced beyond itself. With the awakening of this intellect, a great multitude stepped forth—the al-Munbaʿithūn ⟪ar:'انبعاثی عقول'⟫(the Emanators). It took the precise form of that of the first source. Then the last member of this circle of Emanators issued the daʿwa, at which another vast group came forward, called the Third Circle of Wisdom.

The one who advanced beyond himself at the daʿwa of the last member of the first source's circle became chief of all by virtue of precedence. The nobles became the center and chief of the entire circle, and all the rest were called his circle or followers. All intellects of the circle equaled the Third Intellect in intensity, but by precedence, order was established among them. This occurred in all intellects and circles alike.

We also name the noble and the last member of his circle the "first," for every member of the circle equals his noble in perfection. Only the order of precedence distinguishes them.

To form a circle, the compass is rotated by placing it at the center, and the circle closes where it began. When the circle's last point meets its first point, the circle is complete. Thus the Third Intellect served as the center upon which the circle was placed. Its first point became its chapter; then successive degrees were established until the last point. It was then commanded: "Now you must issue the daʿwa!" From this point's invitation the next intellect advanced and formed its circle.

### Setting of Boundaries in Rationale

The seven intellects and all souls in their circles were so interconnected that the foot of the one above was joined to the head of the one below. The foot of the Third Intellect was attached to the head of the first member of its circle, becoming thereby his ḥadd ʿālī (upper limit). Similarly, the foot of the last member of the Third Intellect's circle was connected to the head of the chief of the Fourth Intellect. This chain of upper and lower limits was established according to their precedence. The current of the Creator's bounty that began from the First Intellect reached its limits through all exalted means.

The first source contained only twenty-seven souls; but from the Third Intellect ⟪ar:عقل ثالث⟫ onward, the souls were countless. The number of souls in the circles of these seven intellects was so vast that enumeration itself could not contain them.

## The Essence of the Word in Monotheism

The actions (movements) that occurred in the spiritual world correspond to the letters—alif, lām, and hāʾ—in the word "God" ⟪ar:'الہ'⟫. First, the intellect advanced from its own self toward the self without any external summons. This is the state of alif ⟪ar:' ا '⟫. Observing this, and without any daʿwa, another proceeded toward it—this is the state of lām ⟪ar:'ل'⟫. Then, by command of the First Intellect, the first source began the daʿwa, upon which seven intellects advanced. This is the state of hāʾ ⟪ar:' ھ '⟫. Thus three states were established in the spiritual realm, corresponding to three essences within the Word ⟪ar:لا الہ الا اللہ⟫.[^cite-5]

| Alif | Lām | Hāʾ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First Intellect | First Source | Seven Intellects |
| Advance from Self | Advance by Witnessing | Proceed to Invitation |

The same pattern arose in all intellective realms. When the first member began the daʿwa, an intellect advanced beyond itself at his daʿwa and accepted the invitation—this is the state of alif ⟪ar:' ا '⟫. This being became noble and chief of its circle. Witnessing this act, a vast multitude revolted and joined the noble, coming to understanding. The multitude required no daʿwa; they accepted the invitation simply by seeing their chief. If the example be drawn from the circle, then the noble became the center of the multitude, for without his advance, the multitude would not have moved forward seeing him. This is the state of lām ⟪ar:' ل '⟫. Then the last member of the assembly (lām) was commanded by his chief to issue the daʿwa. At his daʿwa, a vast multitude joined him, called the members of the intellect's circle. As soon as the last member received the command to summon, he became the center for the next, for without his daʿwa, the congregation accepting the invitation would not have advanced. This is the state of hāʾ ⟪ar:' ھ '⟫.

The noble of the Third Intellect and all people within his constituents, the al-Munbaʿithūn ⟪ar:'انبعاثی عقول'⟫(the Emanators), dwelled all in the same heaven and attained perfection equally. Through knowledge of the Second Intellect and tawhīd, they all achieved the same perfection. Only the distinction of sābiqiyyat ⟪ar:سباقیت⟫(precedence) remained among them.

Alif moved from itself. Witnessing alif, lām stepped forward. At the daʿwa of lām, hāʾ proceeded forward.

The Raʾīs al-ʿAql (chief of intellect) is the Imām for his group, and the members of his group are his followers. He became the intellect ⟪ar:حَد⟫(the limit) and his group became the muḥaddidīn ⟪ar:مُحَدِّدِین⟫(those who define the limit). He became the wise ⟪ar:رئیس⟫(chief) and all others became his marʾūsūn ⟪ar:مرؤسین⟫(those under him). The circles are attributed to their nobles, just as the circle is connected to its center. Therefore, when we speak of the Third Intellect, we mean the Third noble and all the people within his circle.

All those ⟪ar:عین عظیمہ⟫who advanced toward knowledge of the Divine Beings became Imāms. Those who advanced after witnessing the Imāms became the bāb al-inbiʿāth ⟪ar:باب انبعاثی⟫(the gate of emanation), and those who advanced at the daʿwa became the bāb al-bāṭin ⟪ar:باب باطن⟫(the inner gate).

## "God Bears Witness That There Is No God But He"

When the seven intellects were established, the First Intellect manifested as ⟪ar:نور شعشعانی⟫radiant luminescence. Witnessing this ⟪ar:نور شعشعانی⟫radiant light, all the intellects were astonished and astounded, seeing His greatness and exaltation. At that moment, all these intellects acknowledged the First Intellect and conferred upon Him the Name ⟪ar:أسم اللہ⟫"Allah." For this reason, Allāh says in the Holy Qurʾān:

> ⟪quran 3:18⟫
> ⟪ar:‏شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَٱلْمَلَٓئِكَةُ وَأُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمِ قَآئِمًۢا بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۚ لَآ إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ‎⟫
> *Allah bears witness that none has the right to be worshipped but He, and the angels, and those endowed with knowledge (also bear witness to this). He is always maintaining His creation in Justice. There is no god but He, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.*

That is, the First ⟪ar:اللہ⟫Intellect testified that there is no god but the Creator ⟪ar:ھو⟫, as did the First Source and the seven intellects ⟪ar:الملائکۃ⟫(the Angels), and ⟪ar:جثہ ابدائیۃ⟫the primordial community (ūlū al-ʿilm, those endowed with knowledge) testified in the same manner and were thereby justified.[^cite-6]

# Formation of the world of life



## Their Slip: A Momentary Lapse

Along with Asher's repentance, a group offered their repentance, which ⟪ar:تاَبُو بِتَوبَتِہِ⟫ was called. This was followed by the feast of Asher—⟪ar:تابو بتوبتہ⟫ the last person in the circle—which led to another group called ⟪ar:لب النداہ⟫ the Brotherhood. All three ⟪ar:عاشر، تابو بتوبتہ، لبو النداہ⟫ of them achieved perfection. He invited the disobedient group and called them to the truth, forbidding them from disobeying Allah. Yet all of them denied it and were arrogant, which caused their souls to become distressed.[^cite-1]

When the ten intellects had attained perfection with their circles, the First Intellect (al-ʿAql al-Awwal) knew through its omniscience that these disobedient groups would no longer emerge from their stubbornness. Therefore, the First Intellect decided to remove this disobedient group from the spiritual realm and ordered their descent: ⟪ar:اھبطو⟫

> ⟪quran 7:24⟫
> ⟪ar:‏قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّۭ ۖ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّۭ وَمَتَعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ ‎⟫
> *(Allah) said: "Get down, one of you an enemy to the other. On earth will be a dwelling-place for you and an enjoyment, for a time."*
> — **Quran 7:24**

This command proceeded from the First Intellect and passed through all ⟪ar:دوائر عقلیۃ⟫ the intellective circles to Ashir—⟪ar:لب الندا⟫ the last person in this order. It became incumbent upon him to instruct this disobedient group toward perfection once more. Although the second source had not misled anyone from the summons, if he ⟪ar:وحم مساوات⟫ had not acted thus, the whole group would have been corrupted. By the justice of Allah, Asher was commanded to release them, for he had become their chief by virtue of having caused them to stray. The position of the First Intellect in the world of *Abdāʾ* (the primordial realm) corresponds to the position that Ashir holds for those in the world of density—that group whose rectification had been ordained.[^cite-2]

In truth, Asher ⟪ar:ابلیس روحانی⟫—the spiritual Satan—was entrusted with the work of reform, which belongs to his station. ⟪ar:وحم مساوات⟫ As soon as the command ⟪ar:اھبطو⟫ was issued by the First Intellect and reached Asher through all the ⟪ar:دوائر عقلیۃ⟫ intellective circles, a sect accepted Asher's invitation with longing. That is, they hesitated for a moment and then confessed. This moment of hesitation, and their momentary denial, became their fault. That group ⟪ar:'خطائھم کلمَّم'⟫ was thus named—their mistake was but a fleeting delay. In Arabic, this is called ⟪ar:' لمم'⟫—the blink of an eyelid, a most slight transgression. And ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ means "error like the blink of an eye," or "a particle of error."[^cite-3]

## The Formation of the World of Life

The group ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ hesitated to accept Asher's invitation and refused acceptance, yet they repented before his order could be executed. Here came a delicate moment for Asher—⟪ar:لب النداہ⟫ the last person in his circle—to determine what would become of the group: whether they would be punished or pardoned. He looked upward with longing and beseeched those above him for aid and assistance, as the Quran declares:

> ⟪quran 1:5⟫
> ⟪ar:‏إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ ‎⟫
> *You (Alone) we worship, and You (Alone) we ask for help (for each and everything).*
> — **Quran 1:5**

All the intellects above him offered their counsel and favor upon Ashir, suggesting that the group should neither remain in the spiritual world nor be cast into the physical world. Rather, a place should be created for them between the spiritual realm and the material realm, situated at an intermediate station. The Prophet's tradition (peace be upon him) points to this principle in its deepest sense: "The best of all matters is their middle course."[^cite-4]

Thus the ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ group was not overwhelmed entirely, nor were they permitted to fall into the material world. Since ⟪ar:لب انداہ⟫ they had heeded the invitation yet sinned, they could no longer dwell in the spiritual realm—that place of spiritual perfection where neither imperfection nor sin can exist. Therefore the ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ people were thrust out from there and placed between the spiritual world and the material world, which ⟪ar:عالم حیات⟫ is called the World of Life. This realm has also been designated by several other names: ⟪ar:تامور⟫, ⟪ar:کعبۃ الروحانی⟫, ⟪ar:مرکز⟫, ⟪ar:باب عالم قدس⟫, ⟪ar:قلب روحانی⟫, and ⟪ar:عالم محتجبین⟫.[^cite-5]

All members of his ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ group were genuinely repentant, and there was no fault in their repentance itself. Yet they did not attain perfection. Although it would have been possible for them to be counted among the realm of Intellect by virtue of the perfection of their remorse, what occurred was that when they denied for a moment, some among them gazed upon him, accepted his influence, and deteriorated. It was solely because of this that they did not achieve perfection. The same principle was applied to them as to the intellect of Ashir: ⟪ar:من کسر عظم فعلیہ جبر⟫ "Whoever breaks a bone must set it right." Now it became incumbent upon this ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ people to reform those who had been corrupted by their example.

### Adam of the Beginning

As soon as the command ⟪ar:اھبطو⟫ came, one from the ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ tribe, ⟪ar:انحدار⟫ descending in repentance, became monotheistic after profound shame and became what is called ⟪ar:آدم ابدائیۃ⟫—Adam of the Beginning. Beholding this, twelve persons separated themselves, they who had gazed upon him and repented together with his repentance. Then twenty-seven others split away through the invitation of the last member of the group. All ⟪ar:'مدبرین'⟫ these are called the Governors, and all attained perfection. All developed within the Asheric realms, while the remainder became the fallen realm of ⟪ar:مدبرین⟫ nature. The strategy of salvation for the whole world was entrusted to them.

Now Asher truly refers to ⟪ar:آدم بدایۃ⟫—Adam of Inception—the last person of the circle, who is the leader of the World of Life and who shall dwell in this natural realm. He holds the same station in the material world as the First Intellect (al-ʿAql al-Awwal) holds in the world of origin. He became the place where the rays of the First Intellect fell, and in every age of the natural world, he became the radiant light shining upon the Prophet, the Imam, and their supporter. The entire material world is established through his command.[^cite-6]

He is called the highest point ⟪ar:'محدد'⟫ in the realm where ⟪ar:آدم ابدائیۃ⟫ was established as ⟪ar:مور اول⟫ the first matter. ⟪ar:آدم ابدائیۃ⟫ He appeared in this world as a veil through a ⟪ar:جثہ ابدائیہ⟫ primordial form. ⟪ar:جثہ أبدائیۃ⟫ He is the one who, ⟪ar:آدم أبدایۃ⟫ when beheld, was perceived as complete—and thus had to appear in the world veiled.

**Statement:** On the model of the World of Life's limitation, the physical Kaaba likewise holds the position of limitation—the highest and most noble. This position is not reflected in physicality owing to its subtlety.

### The Imams Settled and the Imams Entrusted

The rest of the ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ group divided into two sects. Those who repented and attained monotheism, reaching the highest rank in their monotheistic station, are called ⟪ar:مستقرین⟫—the Settled Ones. All of them ⟪ar:جثث، قوائم، ائمۃ، اوصیا⟫—bodies, pillars, Imams (imāma, the spiritual authority), and Successors—are included therein. Those who repented and attained monotheism while reaching the lowest level in their monotheistic station are called ⟪ar:مستودعین⟫—the Entrusted Ones—and include all the messengers, prophets, chapters (divisions of the hierarchy), and high supplicants.

### The Astronomical Congregation

⟪ar:تنجوم⟫ It was the name of Adam's father when the celestial arrangement took form. At that time, three congregations were established. The ⟪ar:امام ھنید⟫ crowd approached ⟪ar:مستقرین⟫ the Settled Ones. ⟪ar:مستودین⟫ Adam received a congregation, and Adam's father received a congregation, which is called ⟪ar:تنجومی مجمع⟫ the Astronomical Assembly. This congregation stands at a rank higher than ⟪ar:مستودعین⟫ the Entrusted Ones, yet ⟪ar:مستقرین⟫ lower than the Settled Ones. ⟪ar:تنجومی مجمع⟫ From the last circles of the Hujjat (the Proof) to the final circles of the Gate of Gates, there extends a gathering that ⟪ar:مستودع⟫ cannot be encompassed.

### The Kaaba and the Pillar of Light

⟪ar:عالم حیات⟫ The World of Life—also called ⟪ar:تامور⟫ by another name—or ⟪ar:کعبہ روحانی⟫ the Spiritual Kaaba, has another designation. ⟪ar:عمود نور⟫ The map of the physical Kaaba was kept in perfect correspondence with the Spiritual Kaaba of the same spiritual world. Every place that exists in the physical Kaaba is also present in the spiritual Kaaba. The points of noble relation were situated in the inner recesses ⟪ar:تجاویف⟫ of the Kaaba, while points bearing the lowest relation were located at the periphery ⟪ar:(بطائخ)⟫. All believers ⟪ar:خمیرۃ الندامۃ⟫ gathered in the coordinates ⟪ar:عمود نور⟫ of the Pillar of Light.

When ⟪ar:عالم حیات⟫ the World of Life was formed, ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ the *Kalmam* were ordered to invite all who ⟪ar:مستودع و مستقر ائمہ⟫ were settled and entrusted as Imams. There existed a crucial difference between their invitations and those of the intellects:

| 1 | Until now, only the last person of the circle had been invited (individual invitation); but all members of the *Kalmam* were now ordered to invite as a collective (collective invitation). |

| 2 | Until now, there had been only a positive invitation—to believe in the Creator Most High and to attain monotheism. But the *Kalmam* people now called with both positive and negative invitation: Believe in the Creator! Yet also: Do not believe in Satan! |

⟪ar:عالم حیات⟫ Not only were all members of the ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ *Kalmam* group inviting together; they also called with both positive and negative summons—to believe in the Creator Most High and to attain monotheism, and to reject the words of ⟪ar:ابلیس روحانی⟫ the spiritual Satan. The ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ *Kalmam* began learning from one another on this foundation. On the basis of their mutual perception ⟪ar:افادۃ و استفادۃ⟫—giving and receiving—the ranks and hierarchies were established among them.[^cite-7]

## The Classification of the *Kalmam*

### Sight and Vision

The noblest sight is that which is born through struggle and effort in Asher's summons. In the same way that the caste accepted Ashir's invitation, their eyes were fixed upon him. The people of noble sight continue to receive the light of God. Those who attained the highest rank had their sight established through the attention of ⟪ar:'حدت و قوت'⟫ strength and power in Ashraf's intention-world. ⟪ar:صاحبان اموار⟫ Those of the Waters and ⟪ar:آدم بدایۃ⟫ Adam of Inception accepted the invitation and repented with full heart, so their sight was raised to the highest level. Then came the sight of ⟪ar:صاحبان کور⟫ diminishing vision, and then again ⟪ar:صاحبان دور (عین آخرۃ)⟫—those of the circle—with renewed nobility and ⟪ar:عین عظیمۃ⟫ the Great Eye.[^cite-8]

### The Station of the Settled Ones

The gaze of all ⟪ar:مستقرین ائمۃ⟫ settled Imams was upon those who had achieved the noblest state—all ⟪ar:عین عظیمۃ⟫ concentrated upon Ali ⟪ar:محتجب⟫ the Veiled. Everyone was learning from you and feeling the warmth of your summons and benefiting from you. And it was upon the visible presence ⟪ar:قائم علی ذکرہ السلام⟫ of the Standing One that your station—⟪ar:صاحب دور⟫ the Master of the Circle—came to rest. After ⟪ar:عین عظیمۃ⟫ you, their rank was established. All ⟪ar:مستقر آئمہ⟫ settled Imams are those who, having proceeded forward from ⟪ar:عین عظیمۃ⟫ the Great Eye and submitted to it, became subservient to themselves and ⟪ar:توحید، تجرید اور تنزیہ⟫ to unification, abstraction, and transcendence—becoming as ⟪ar:قائم الدور (عین آخرۃ)⟫ the Standing One of the Circle (the Last Eye).

### The Ranks of the Entrusted

The gaze of all ⟪ar:مستودعین⟫ the entrusted ones, who had received the station of Adum, was directed toward their invocation. And their eyes ⟪ar:میم مریمیۃ⟫ of the Marian *mīm*—that of ⟪ar:ذات أحمدیۃ (محمد مصطفی صلی اللہ علیہ و آلہ وسلم⟫—the Ahmadian Essence (Muhammad the Chosen, peace be upon him and his family)—looked ⟪ar:محتجب)⟫ veiled. That is, they were influenced by the summons of all the Prophets and Messengers ⟪ar:حضرت ابراھیم⟫ such as Abraham ⟪ar:حضرت ابراھیم⟫ and were benefiting from the summons of themselves. ⟪ar:مولانا أحمد علیہ السلام⟫ Mawlānā Ahmad, peace be upon him, thus stood highest in the rank of ⟪ar:میم مریمیۃ⟫ the Marian *mīm*, the lowest, followed by the rank of the other Prophets and Messengers. ⟪ar:حضرت ابراھیم خلیل اللہ⟫

During ⟪ar:مستقرین ومستودعین⟫ these feasts of the settled and entrusted, when ⟪ar:عین عظیمۃ⟫ the Great Eye began to witness the feast of the lower rank, the gaze fell upon the assembly, and it was observed that ⟪ar:میم علیہ السلام⟫ the *mīm*, peace be upon him/her, possessed a feast of such intensity, and their method of utilization was so exalted. So far her gaze ⟪ar:مستقرین⟫ had been upon the Settled Ones, and ⟪ar:مستودعین⟫ her gaze had been upon the Entrusted Ones. ⟪ar:عین عظیمہ⟫ Since she was of superior rank and had become the leader of all ⟪ar:مستقر ائمۃ⟫ settled Imams, as soon as ⟪ar:میم⟫ the *mīm* beheld those who were the people of Adum, the eyes ⟪ar:میم⟫ of all the Imams were likewise drawn to her, and all ⟪ar:میم مریمیہ⟫ the Imams began to draw benefit from her. The Kaaba became the center of the gaze of all these Imams. That is why all these Imams are called in ⟪ar:ائمہ دور محمدی علیہم السلام⟫ this world the Imams of the Muhammadan Circle, peace be upon them all![^cite-9]

**Statement:** The perfection of ⟪ar:مستودعین⟫ the entrusted ones is to become ⟪ar:مستقرین⟫ the settled ones. That is, to ascend to the highest relation from Adum, and to enter the Spiritual Kaaba from the sides of the Kaaba.

### The *Mīm's* Ascent from the Entrusted:

When Asher witnessed this state in the World of Life—that a person of higher proportion had become the head of the lower—he elevated the throne of *Mīm*. The point of the *mīm* was removed; she obtained her sight from the eyes of Adum and ascended from the sides of the Kaaba, entering the Kaaba itself—that is, she joined the Settled Ones. Arriving there and running toward ⟪ar:عین عظیمۃ⟫ the Great Eye, in her summons she progressed with such intensity of gaze that she surpassed all the Imams and drew so close to ⟪ar:عین عظیمۃ⟫ the Great Eye that only three ranks remained between them, which were the stations of the Imams ⟪ar:جد، فتح اور خیال⟫—Grandfather, Opening, and Imagination. This is the *mi'rāj* in truth, and for this reason Allah says (interpretation of the meaning):

> ⟪quran 53:8-9⟫
> ⟪ar:‏ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّىٰ ‎ ‏فَكَانَ قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَىٰ ‎⟫
> *Then he [Jibrael (Gabriel)] approached and came closer, And was at a distance of two bows' length or (even) nearer.*
> — **Quran 53:8-9**

"Two bows' length" refers to the rank of ⟪ar:مولانا عامر⟫ Mawlānā ʿĀmir and ⟪ar:مولانا عمران⟫ Mawlānā ʿImrān, while "even nearer" indicates the rank of ⟪ar:مولانا عبد اﷲ⟫ Mawlānā ʿAbd Allāh. For this reason, when ⟪ar:میم اور عین⟫ the *mīm* and the Eye came into this world—veiled as ⟪ar:محمد مصطفی⟫ Muhammad the Chosen and ⟪ar:علی ابن ابی طالب⟫ Ali son of Abī Ṭālib—the veil was even more profound than the veil of the veil, because this form had been created in the World of Life. If ⟪ar:عین⟫ the Eye had not gone to the sight of ⟪ar:حجاب علی⟫ the Veil of Ali, and if ⟪ar:میم⟫ the *mīm* had not reached the sight of ⟪ar:حجاب محمد (ﷺ)⟫ the Veil of Muhammad (peace be upon him), I would never have read the Kalima![^cite-10]

Thus when he came into this world, the followers of Ali were few, while the followers of the Messenger of Allah were numerous.

## The Veiled and the Veil

All the Imams and the Pure Ones (al-Asfiyāʾ) are established in the stations ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ of the *Kalmam*. Since they had accepted the summons before they became material, the justice of Allah does not permit them to be sent into this world, which is the abode of Allah's wrath. Yet all of these ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ *Kalmam* make an impression in this material world. This effect is based upon the blessed *nasut* (the material form) which is prepared by ⟪ar:ریحیات⟫ the believers—which is called ⟪ar:حجاب⟫ the Veil. The true beings live in the World of Life and are called ⟪ar:محتجب⟫ the Veiled—hidden behind the veil.[^cite-11]

All the Imams who have come into this world are from ⟪ar:محتجبین⟫ the veiled ones of the World of Life who have appeared in this world through *hijāb* (the veil). In other words, they are also called ⟪ar:نواسیت⟫—the Descendants—and ⟪ar:حجابات⟫ Veils (plural). Those ⟪ar:محتجب⟫ who are veiled in me ⟪ar:کلمم⟫ are named ⟪ar:عین عظیمۃ⟫—the Great Eye. He, ⟪ar:محتجب⟫ the Veiled, established many veils in this world; the lowest of these was called the ⟪ar:علی ابن ابی طالب علیہ السلام⟫ veil of Ali son of Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him. The veil always acts according to the will of its veiled one.

Each higher veil becomes a lower ⟪ar:محتجب⟫ veiled one, and in this arrangement ⟪ar:حجاب و محتجب⟫ both veil and veiled can exist in this world simultaneously. The veil is always a ransom for its veiled. An apt example: if we sense a stone falling upon our head, we place our hand to shield it, saving the head. The hand becomes a veil for the head, protecting it from harm. Both head and hand are present in the body at once. In the same way, those who became veils for the sake of the Prophet also existed in the time of the Prophet and became veils to save the self of the Prophet, bearing pain themselves to protect their master.[^cite-12] An Imam can establish more than a thousand ⟪ar:حجابات⟫ veils at one time, but he does not. ⟪ar:مولا تنا فاطمۃ⟫ Our Mistress Fāṭima, peace be upon her, undertook four hundred and ten veils, as is indicated in the *tasbīh* (the devotional counting) or *fāṭira* (the chapter).

The Imam has the right to appoint anyone as a veil whom he chooses. An example: if a person approaches a mango tree and sees many ripe mangoes upon it, he might pluck one. If asked why he chose this particular mango when others were equally ripe, he would answer, "It is my choice to do so." In the same manner, the Imam too has the right to choose whomever he wishes as his veil. Thus did ⟪ar:فراط ابن احنق⟫ he choose—as the tradition relates concerning ⟪ar:امام جعفر الصادق⟫ Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq and his choice of ⟪ar:مولانا اسماعیل⟫ our Mawlānā Ismāʿīl.

His teeth were martyred in battle and a rib bone was broken. The tradition tells that he used to labor there—⟪ar:عبد اللہ ابن رواحا⟫ as did ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa. That is, they were in accordance with the station of the places ⟪ar:عبد اللہ ابن رواحا⟫ of the tooth and the limb, or they came to these places in your nostrils as ⟪ar:ریحیات⟫ fragrances. The Imams possess power over their bodies in the same way that we possess power over our garments.

## The Pillar of Light

⟪ar:عمود نور،⟫ In truth, the Pillar of Light ⟪ar:نور کلمہ⟫—the Light of the Word—is another name for ⟪ar:علم جاری و ساری⟫ the Flowing and Pervading Knowledge that has been passed from the Creator to the First Intellect. Whoever came into contact with this light truly succeeded. Then from the First Intellect this light connected with the Second Intellect, and then descended from the seven intellects and their circles to Asher, who has been entrusted with the command of the material world and who stands in the position of the First Intellect in the world of nature. All of them are called ⟪ar:عقول ابدائیۃ المجردۃ⟫—the Primordial Abstracted Intellects (physicality). Then it connects with the light of Ashir to every place that emanates from the world of nature, which are ⟪ar:ناطق، اساس اور امام علیہم السلام⟫—the Speaker (al-Nāṭiq), the Foundation (al-Asās), and the Imam, peace be upon them. And then it continues to his Gate (Bāb al-Imam). The Imam's Gate stands in the place of the Imam in this world because it is established there as ⟪ar:نفس کلیۃ⟫ a Universal Soul and ⟪ar:ھیکل⟫ a Temple. And then this Pillar of Light is transmitted from the Gate to the Proof (Ḥujjat), from the Proof to the Summoner (al-Daʿī), from the Summoner to the Permission-Giver (al-Mazūn), from the Permission-Giver to the Believers, and from the Believers to the Respondents while they take the Noble Covenant.[^cite-13]

It is said of the Pillar of Light that it is all-encompassing and knowledge is continuous through it; it is the soul—the Word, the Light of the Kalima *Lā ilāha illā Allāh* ("There is no god but Allah"). All spiritual and material boundaries are connected to this Pillar of Light, extending from the First Intellect to the believer, and are held by it. An example: a long wooden pole with honey upon it, and when the fly alights upon it, it never leaves. In the same way, the forms (with which souls are bound) never depart from this Pillar of Light. It is a honeycomb from which all the bees (believers) draw sustenance and adhere. Everyone comes and connects to it. This is ⟪ar:حبل اللہ المتین⟫ the Strong Rope of Allah, which can never be severed. That is why Allah says (interpretation of the meaning):

> ⟪quran 2:256⟫
> ⟪ar:‏لَآ إِكْرَاهَ فِى ٱلدِّينِ ۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشْدُ مِنَ ٱلْغَىِّ ۚ فَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِٱلطَّغُوتِ وَيُؤْمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱسْتَمْسَكَ بِٱلْعُرْوَةِ ٱلْوُثْقَىٰ لَا ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَا ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ ‎⟫
> *There is no compulsion in religion. Verily, the Right Path has become distinct from the wrong path. Whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in Allah, then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold that will never break. And Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower.*
> — **Quran 2:256**

Whoever comes into contact with this Pillar of Light succeeds and becomes among the people of mercy. It is far greater and more exalted than the light of the sun. ⟪ar:شمس⟫ The light of the sun, despite its intensity and heat, is dense and enveloped in materiality. The Pillar of Light contains no density; for this reason it could enter into contact with the First Intellect. We know the Creator because of this light. This light does not fall upon our bodies, but upon our ⟪ar:نفس ناطقہ⟫—our Rational Soul. ⟪ar:عنایت الہیۃ⟫ This is also called by another name: ⟪ar:قدرت الہیۃ⟫ the Divine Power.[^cite-14]

The Intellect—the tenth of the circle—moves this Pillar of Light. This movement is connected to the Imam of that age, and from it he understands that the Imam is attempting to bring a believer to spiritual death. That is, the Imam indicates that the believer's connection has been purified and he is now absorbed into the Pillar of Light. Then the Imam moves the Pillar of Light, through which the form ⟪ar:(نفس ناطقۃ + نفس حسیۃ)⟫—the Rational Soul and the Sensible Soul—of the believer is separated from his body and absorbed into the Pillar of Light.

**Statement:** Malik al-Mut (the Angel of Death) is in truth the Pillar of Light.

### The Development of the Believers' Soul

Thus the Pillar of Light absorbs the forms and transmits them onward to their selves as ⟪ar:مستفیدین⟫ beneficiaries—those who receive. The forms themselves become ⟪ar:مفیدین⟫ those who give. It is a magnet that holds the form and the self together. That is, when the form ascends, it develops together with ⟪ar:نفس حسیہ⟫ the Sensible Soul, and it also advances to a higher rank. The Pillar of Light unites this form and soul. The part of the body that has evolved into a form can no longer be corrupted, because the Rational Soul has attached it to itself. If that form reaches an upper limit and that upper limit is destroyed, then as the form of that upper limit is purified, the Pillar of Light draws it away, and the form is separated from it. The ⟪ar:نفس حسیہ⟫ remainder of it decays.

When Dāʾūd al-Quṭb's intentions failed, ⟪ar:سیدنا ھمام⟫ our master Hammām drew his current form with the aid of the Pillar of Light and gave it to ⟪ar:سیدنا محمد بن فہد⟫ our master Muhammad ibn Fahd for refinement. After this, Dāʾūd al-Quṭb deteriorated. Similarly, when ⟪ar:ابو بکر⟫ Abū Bakr deteriorated, Mawlānā Ali drew his form with the aid of the Pillar of Light and gave it to his son ⟪ar:محمد بن ابی بکر⟫ Muhammad ibn Abī Bakr for training.

### The Deliverer of Provision to the Believers

It is also the work of the Pillar of Light to deliver physical sustenance to man. The Pillar of Light draws man's sustenance and delivers it to him, protecting every part of that sustenance (for the one who consumes it). It ensures that no one else consumes the goods of a believer—that the believer alone receives what he has been brought into this world to have. When a goat is slaughtered, it has several parts, and multiple people may eat from it together. Yet the Pillar of Light conveys every part and piece of that goat to the person whose body it enters.

### The One Who Bestows the Water of Ablution

In the same manner, the water of ablution that reaches a person (when it touches his body during ablution) is also delivered by the Pillar of Light. ⟪ar:بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم⟫ As soon as one says "In the Name of Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful," a person's bond with the Pillar of Light is established. Otherwise, though it is our own matter, the connection takes time to form. Therefore, it is most important to pronounce the ⟪ar:بسم اللہ⟫ *Basmala* at the beginning, and without it, ablution is not valid. ⟪ar:بسم اللہ⟫ At the very moment the *Basmala* is recited, the connection with the Pillar of Light is established and its effect begins to work.

### The Guardian of the Believers' Virtues

The Pillar of Light is the protector of the virtues of the saints of Allah—those devoted to Allah's Guardianship (the leaven of *wilāya*)—and the one who conveys them to their appointed stations. In the same way, when a person is buried after death and his components scatter into fire, air, water, and earth, yet after countless years the Pillar of Light reconnects these components from the *umma* (the community). This is what is called ⟪ar:مقدرات الٰہیۃ⟫—the Divine Measures. The Pillar of Light labors on behalf of all things—⟪ar:(صورات، فضلات، ریحیات)⟫ forms, graces, and fragrances.

**Statement:** The *riwāya* (tradition) says: ⟪ar:اَلمَرْعُ یَحْشَرُ مَعَ مَن اَحَبَّہ⟫ "The soul is gathered with those whom it loves." As soon as we fall in love with someone, our bond becomes attached to theirs. Therefore, we must be most careful about whom we establish our connection with.

### The Leaven of Remorse of the Believers

All believers ⟪ar:خمیرۃ ندامت⟫ are preserved as the Leaven of Remorse in this Pillar of Light. When a believer takes the covenant with the Imam of the Age, he is stirred within ⟪ar:خمیرۃ ندامت⟫ the Leaven and comes into connection with the believer's soul. This union is called the ⟪ar:نفس ناطقہ⟫ Rational Soul.

### When the Bond with the Pillar of Light is Broken

When any of the boundaries or limits becomes defiled through intimacy, the Pillar of Light reverses from it and separates. It is said in the supplication that when a person engages in intercourse, the angels of Allah turn away from him until he returns to a state of purity. Intimacy breaks the connection with the sacred, which also severs the bond with the Pillar of Light. As soon as a person performs ritual washing, he is ⟪ar:نفس ناطقہ⟫ reconnected to the Pillar of Light.

As soon as a woman's private parts become exposed, her connection with the Pillar of Light is broken, and the angels turn away. The hair upon a woman's head is included among her private parts, so it is permissible for her to cover her hair while praying. ⟪ar:جنگ سفین⟫ When the Battle of Siffīn proceeded and ⟪ar:علی علیہ السلام⟫ Ali, peace be upon him, moved to strike ⟪ar:عمروبن عاس⟫ ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, the latter exposed his private parts to save his life. At that moment ⟪ar:علی علیہ السلام⟫ Ali, peace be upon him, turned his gaze away.

### The Accounting of Limits and Degrees

The Pillar of Light is fashioned like a *tasbīḥ* (a counting-cord of prayer beads) in which all the degrees are connected to one another. The Preacher is connected to the Proof, the Proof is connected to the Gate, and the Gate is connected to the Imam. When a believer dies, the Pillar of Light draws his form and places it in the proper place within the *tasbīḥ*, and this is called Paradise. The Paradise of the Preacher is distinct; the Paradise of the Proof is distinct; and the Paradise of the Gate is distinct. When the number in one Paradise becomes complete, a renaissance occurs in another. That is, when the number is fulfilled in the Paradise of the Proof—when the tenth rank is attained—⟪ar:تلک عشرۃٌ کاملۃ⟫ *"That is a complete ten"*—then one enters the Paradise of ⟪ar:باب الابواب⟫ the Gate of Gates. And the Pillar of Light, which keeps watch over all these degrees and developments, is the Light itself.

**Statement:** When the Prophet's revelation first descended upon him in the Cave of Ḥirā, he was in truth in contact with the Pillar of Light.

# Formation of the world of universe and corruption

*Source: KASHKOLE, Binder 1 (Science of Origin and Resurrection), Chapter 80. 20 topics. Language: ur.*



## The Three Intentions of al-ʿĀshir

In shaping the physical world, al-ʿĀshir al-Mudabbir al-Ḥakīm held three principal intentions:

| 1 | Creating Man in a Thousand Ways |
| --- | --- |
| 2 | To imprison the disobedient faction within the constraints of length, width, and depth |
| 3 | To establish the physical universe through cosmic motion |

Although the creation of man constituted the supreme purpose and first thought of al-ʿĀshir, in the order of execution he brought man into being last. This accords with the principle: ⟪ar-quote:اَوَّلُ الفِکَر وَ آخِرُ العَمَل⟫ (the first in thought, the last in action).[^cite-1] When a person conceives of achieving a goal, he first arranges and prepares all prerequisites that must precede the goal's fulfillment, and only then performs the final act that brings it to completion. Thus, although man's creation was al-ʿĀshir's supreme aim, he first brought the world of physicality and corporeality into being so that time and space might be arranged for humanity. Thereafter he established ⟪ar:موالید ثلاثۃ⟫ (the three kingdoms of birth) so that man's sustenance might be secured. Only when all necessities for man's existence were fulfilled did he bring man forth.

Similarly, when an imām or dāʿī (Summoner) assumes his station, his first concern is to prepare his successor for the caliphate; yet in practice, he accomplishes this final task at the end.

## The Creation of the Universe in Six Motions

Al-ʿĀshir executed a total of six motions (ḥarakat) in the formation of the physical world, composed of six ⟪ar:مُحَرِّک⟫ (movers). The Qurʾān testifies to this:

> ⟪quran 50:38⟫
> ⟪ar:‏وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍۢ وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍۢ ‎⟫
> *And indeed We created the heavens and the earth and all between them in six Days, and nothing of fatigue touched Us.*
> — **Qurʾān 50:38**

The six motions may be enumerated as follows:

| First Motion | Removal of luminosity from the disobedient faction and creation within them of the three dimensions—length, width, and depth—of illusion |
| --- | --- |
| Second Motion | Tajādhub al-Qutbayn (Attraction of the Two Poles): stabilization through four celestial forces |
| Third Motion | The eruption of the cosmic vessel; transformation of spirituality into physicality |
| Fourth Motion | Generation of the celestial spheres (kawākib) and the terrestrial realm (saqrāʾ) |
| Fifth Motion | Formation of the celestial spheres through emanating rays; establishment of the four lower elemental kingdoms |
| Sixth Motion | Initiation of astronomical cycles beginning from Saturn |

Following these six motions, the physical world acquired the capacity to sustain itself perpetually. Al-ʿĀshir did not execute a seventh motion; rather, after completing the six, he established himself upon his ⟪ar:عرش⟫ (throne) as the ⟪ar:مُدبر⟫ (Divine Administrator), and the appointed celestial beings beneath him set the machinery of creation in motion.[^cite-2] This is why Allāh says:

> ⟪quran 25:59⟫
> ⟪ar:‏ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍۢ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ۚ ٱلرَّحْمَنُ فَسْـَٔلْ بِهِۦ خَبِيرًۭا ‎⟫
> *He who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six Days, then established Himself upon the Throne. The Most Merciful—ask Him! He is the All-Knowing.*
> — **Qurʾān 25:59**

The duration of each cosmic "day" (yawm) is not to be measured by terrestrial reckoning. Allāh has declared:

> ⟪quran 22:47⟫
> ⟪ar:‏وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِٱلْعَذَابِ وَلَن يُخْلِفَ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُۥ ۚ وَإِنَّ يَوْمًا عِندَ رَبِّكَ كَأَلْفِ سَنَةٍۢ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ ‎⟫
> *And a Day with your Lord is as a thousand years of what you reckon.*
> — **Qurʾān 22:47**

Thus, across the span of six thousand terrestrial years, the planets—from Saturn to Mercury—completed the entire configuration of the universe.

### The Distinction Between Command and Creation

The Creator pronounced it (⟪ar:أمر⟫) and al-ʿĀshir brought it into being (⟪ar:خلق⟫). The Divine Command operates in an instant—⟪ar:کن فیکون⟫ (Be! and it is)—whereas the Creator of the physical universe labored across ⟪ar:فی ستۃ ایام⟫ (six days), demonstrating the immense creative effort required to establish material existence.[^cite-3]

---

**Reflection:** It is worthy of profound contemplation that al-ʿĀshir, who brought this vast universe into being, was once a human being like ourselves. This fact illuminates what extraordinary capacities we have lost through our forgetfulness.

## The Malefic Stars: Saturn and Mars

Saturn and Mars, though composed of the elements that constitute the Repentant, are designated ⟪ar:نحسین⟫ (the Two Malefic Stars). Their malefic character arises from the fact that some among their order initially accepted the call of Iblīs and embraced rebellion, only to repent subsequently. This circumstance attached misfortune to them. Yet because their repentance was timely—occurring at ⟪ar:انجماد مآء⟫ (the freezing of waters)—they attained the celestial realm. This fortune did not extend to the other factions. The divine plan commenced with the heaven of Saturn, whose function is demolition (hadm). By nature Saturn contains lust, evil, and malefic influence; its function is to freeze or congeal. Yet Saturn itself is among ⟪ar:نادمین وتائبین⟫ (the Repentant and Penitent). To construct any edifice, one must first dismantle the old structure and level the ground. Since Saturn's assignment is to break down and freeze, it was placed foremost in the celestial order. Its role is analogous to the royal executioner: the executioner is not evil in essence, yet by his function he has been entrusted with painful and destructive tasks.[^cite-11]

⟪ar:نحسین (زحل اور مریخ)⟫ The two Malefic Stars serve as magnets for all vicious tendencies. They capture ⟪ar:عقدتین⟫ the harmful essences they generate from their ⟪ar:مزاج وممتزج⟫ (temperament and blended nature) and confine them.

## The Fifth Movement: Creation of the Asdāf and the Mothers

When the Kawākib (celestial bodies) and Saqqara were brought into readiness, a subtle smoke, ⟪ar:دُخَّانِ لَطِیف⟫, which had belonged to the faction of Nadmin (the rebellious ones), remained about Saqqara in accordance with the Divine Will. Since these elements were part of Nadmin, they could neither unite with Saqqara nor join the Umma (the cosmic principles). These were the essences which, though they had turned in remorse, were compelled to descend to the earthly realm because of Divine retribution.

Asher (the Originator) then set the heavens in motion again—a fifth movement—which caused all celestial spheres and the planetary bodies, ⟪ar:کواکب سیارۃ⟫, to move in concert. For the first time, all the stars cast their rays toward Saqqara by the force of their movements. Yet Saqqara, which was composed of bone-like substance, ⟪ar:خود مصرین⟫, could not receive the rays of any constellation, for those rays were components of Nadmin. When these rays struck Saqqara and rebounded to their source, they united once more with the rays of their own celestial sphere—their constituent parts. The subtle smoke, ⟪ar:دُخَّانِ لَطِیف⟫, from the solar and lunar portions was absorbed into the lunar rays, and similarly from all the spheres: the rays gathered their constituent elements from the sides of Saqqara, returned to their source, and from this smoke there became formed the asdāf (celestial bodies' dense shells), which are also termed ⟪ar:أجرام الکواکب⟫.[^cite-8]

> Facts:
> 
> The asdāf fall on the Day of Judgment and are replaced by other asdāf. Both asdāf and latāʾif (subtle forms) fall at the lesser resurrection of the veil (*doomsday of the cover*). At the resurrection of the Peacock-Master, all three—asdāf, latāʾif, and spiritualities—fall together.

Since Saturn and Mars, ⟪ar:نحس⟫ (the malefic stars), cast their rays upon Sagittarius, they drew other essences alongside the Nadminite elements—those of hesitancy and perplexity, ⟪ar:شاک و متحیرین⟫, and those of rebellion and arrogance, ⟪ar:مصر و مستکبرین⟫. From the parts of the Nadminite ones emerged the asdāf; from the remainder came forth the malefic natures, ⟪ar:نحس طبعیتیں⟫.[^cite-9]

When we regard these planets with our sight, we perceive only their shadows; all the planets in their true reality possess forms immense beyond naked perception. The Wise One (al-Mubdiʿ Taʿālā, the Originator, Most High) has made all these heavens and stars as a lamp for the peoples of the earth, so that the greatness of the Creator might be investigated—who alone is the fashioner of all things.

## Creation of the Four Mothers (*Ummahat*)

Countless millions of years elapsed as these heavens and principles formed themselves. The various acts set in motion by Asher occurred at intervals stretching across different epochs. Some of these intervals were brief; others immeasurably long. After the Originator granted the heavens a total of six movements, the earth acquired the capacity to move of its own accord.

### The Lithosphere

When all the planets were set in motion by Asher's fifth movement, the atmosphere beneath the sky became exceedingly hot and arid owing to the movement of the moon—which bears the nature of fire. At that moment, extreme dryness united with intense heat, ⟪ar:کرۃ النار⟫⟪ar:کرۃ أسیر⟫, and thus the first of the four Mothers was produced: the sphere of fire at the cosmos's center. This is fire of such a nature that the eye cannot perceive it. The scholars teach that had the Originator granted light to this heat, we should never have been able to look upon the heavens—thus revealing one of the Divine wisdoms.

### The Atmosphere

When the effect of the moon's motion reached downward and its rays diffused below, the temperature began to diminish. As heat decreased, condensation ceased, and moisture appeared in its place. When temperature and humidity reached equilibrium, ⟪ar:کرۃ الهوا⟫ (the Sphere of Air) was produced.[^cite-10]

> Statement:
> 
> The decreasing motion of this heat resembles a person floating in water. The water closest to the swimmer moves with far greater agitation than water at a distance; the water far removed experiences no movement at all.

### The Hydrosphere

When the effect of the moon's motion withdrew entirely, the components relaxed and the heat dispersed. There was formed, by the union of cold with moisture, ⟪ar:کرۃ المآء⟫⟪ar:کرۃ زمحریر⟫ (the Sphere of Water), which enveloped the entire earth. All this occurred in essence—that is, the water was not yet manifest in sensible form, but its essential nature had come into being.

### The Geosphere

As the sky's motion descended further, the distance from the celestial source produced extreme cold and extreme dryness: ⟪ar:کرۃ الأرض⟫ (the Sphere of Earth). Here too, outward dust had not yet appeared, but only its essence. When this intense cold and rigidity united with Saqqara, the combination of Saqqara's heat with this cold produced a heavy substance that enveloped Saqqara entirely—as though the sphere of clay had spread like a garment upon its surface.

These four spheres float within their respective orbits without mingling with one another; the celestial bodies' components are not found within the earthly spheres, and the earthly components do not ascend into the heavens.

### The Geosphere: Second Phase

When the Mother-spheres were established, Asher undertook the creation of the threefold life-forms, ⟪ar:موالید ثلاثۃ⟫. By his governance, the Kawākib cast their rays upon Saqqara a second time—yet these rays differed from the first. First, they were weaker than their predecessors. Second, when the heavens first emitted rays, the Mothers had not yet come forth, and those rays reached straight to Saqqara without obstruction, struck it, and returned to their source. Now, however, with four spheres interposed between the heavens and Saqqara, the rays' velocity weakened. Unable to penetrate Saqqara by virtue of their diminished force, unable to return to their source, these rays refracted upon striking Saqqara.

When these rays engaged the earth—which in its primordial state was extremely cold and dry—they began to warm it. As the earth warmed, so too the water above it warmed, and the natures of these two spheres moved toward equilibrium, as we observe them today. Before these second rays, both spheres existed in such cold as to preclude all life. Despite this moderation, a hierarchy persists in these natures: as we descend into the earth's depths, temperature climbs until we approach Saqqara itself, which remains in extreme heat. Similarly in the waters: as one descends deeper, or rises higher into the air, conditions become increasingly hostile to life.[^cite-11]

These rays passed upward through the spheres of earth and water, entering the sphere of air. The rays' weakened power prevented them from traversing the entire atmosphere; they reached only a portion and dispersed within it. The region they penetrated, by the spreading of their influence, produced a moderate cold and moisture, giving rise to ⟪ar:کرۃ النسیم⟫ (the Sphere of Breeze), from which we breathe our life. The higher one ascends within this sphere, the more temperature increases. The upper portion of the atmosphere, untouched by these rays, retained its original nature—extreme heat and dryness; the lower portion, into which the rays diffused, became cool and moist.

> Statement:
> 
> When we travel by aircraft, the temperature outside becomes extremely low. All who travel by plane pass through ⟪ar:کرۃ النسیم⟫.

This Sphere of Breeze, ⟪ar:کرۃ النسیم⟫, is truly the center and source of the water-sphere. It originated from the water's essence and spread like a layer over the water's crust. For this reason, the properties of the water-sphere and the Sphere of Breeze are one and the same.

## The Jauhar, the Two Knots, the Head, and the Tail

Beneath the moon are two wandering stars, ⟪ar:جوزہر⟫, which possess neither shell nor dense body; they are named after their positions: ⟪ar:'راس'⟫ (the Head) and ⟪ar:'زنب'⟫ (the Tail). These are both malefic stars in which the Tail exhibits wickedness more intense than the Head. Both are called ⟪ar:عقدتین⟫ (the Two Knots).[^cite-12] These two are prisons wherein the evil essences, ⟪ar:صورات خبیثۃ⟫, are held and chastened. The asdāf (dense shells) of the Two Knots do not exist—for the components that ascended through the rays of the Kawākib and became asdāf were Nadminite elements, which have no connection to these two stars.

Although these two stars possess malefic components and are of the faction of those who rebelled and grew arrogant, ⟪ar:مصر ومستکبرین⟫, the Originator did not place them within Saqqara but rather above the heavens. The reason is this: these two stars were formed from essences of those who were among the first to turn in remorse to Asher, who then accepted his invitation and became fiercest and most desperate in opposing it. Though they began by following the remorseful, they ended in defiant arrogance, ⟪ar:اصرار واستکبار⟫. For this reason, the Originator placed them above the remorseful, yet not below ⟪ar:فلک قمر⟫ (the lunar sphere).

These two use their governance to bring forth all evils, diseases, killings, earthquakes, floods, and storms in the world. They reveal all these defects, ⟪ar:صورات خبیثۃ⟫, through their influence and by means of their agency. They are neither with the heavens nor with the Mothers, but belong to the third faction—those of rebellion and arrogance, ⟪ar:فرقہ الثالثہ (مصر و مستکبر)⟫. Though they are beings of Saqqara, they are stationed according to Divine justice above the lower limit. ⟪ar:عقدتین⟫ The world of dense bodies and the cosmos of the heavens, especially ⟪ar:نیرین  (شمس و قمر)⟫ (the two luminaries: the Sun and the Moon), endure obstruction at the time of their eclipse. The Tail is more vehement in this rivalry than the Head. Just as the Sun and Moon point toward the Speaker-Prophet (Nātiq) and his Foundation (Asās), or toward the Imam and his Proof (Ḥujja), so too do they point toward the Two Knots—to Iblis, ⟪ar:ابلیس روحانی⟫, and to Satan.

## The Gates of Paradise and Hell

Paradise and Hell are one and the same in essence, yet they are reached through different portals—a difference of form. The gates form a series of levels surrounding the centers. The gates ascending toward Paradise grow ever more subtle and refined; the gates descending toward Hell grow ever more dense and heavy. Paradise possesses eight gates; Hell possesses seven.

### Hell

There are three threefold life-forms, ⟪ar:موالید ثلاثۃ⟫: the first is the mineral, which dwells beneath the earth; the second is vegetation, which covers the earth's surface; the third is the animal, which lives upon the earth. Corresponding to these are the four Mothers—the spheres of earth, water, air, and fire. These three life-forms and four Mothers together constitute the seven gates of Hell, and Hell itself is Saqqara. When an unbeliever departs this life, he must traverse these seven gates to enter Saqqara; he cannot ascend to the heavens above. The seven doors, which serve as gateways to Saqqara, stand in direct relation to the Mothers and the life-forms. In other words, the gates of Hell commence from beneath the lunar sphere.

### Paradise

The sky of the moon stands first; above it rise seven heavens. Beyond them is the eighth constellation, which encompasses all the stars. These eight heavens are in fact the eight gates of Paradise, and Paradise itself, ⟪ar:فلک محیط⟫, is the world above them—the place called ⟪ar:تامور⟫, the abode of ⟪ar:عالم حیات⟫ (the World of Life), or ⟪ar:کعبۃ الروحانی⟫ (the Spiritual Kaʿba). The nearest gate to Paradise bears the name ⟪ar:'دار السلام'⟫ (the Abode of Peace). No gate exists beyond this one. This name was borne by the house of our Master ʿAlī, and ⟪ar:رسول اللہ (ﷺ)⟫ (the Messenger of God, peace be upon him) called his own house ⟪ar:'بیت الشرف'⟫ (the House of Honour). Just as one enters a house through its door, so too can one enter the Paradise-house only ⟪ar:بیت الشرف⟫ through the gate ⟪ar:دار السلام⟫.

## The Greater Sensibility and the Greater Generative Power

The cosmos is divided into two principal realms: ⟪ar:عالم جرمانی⟫ (the world of dense bodies—from ⟪ar:فلک محیط⟫ to ⟪ar:تحت فلک قمر⟫) and ⟪ar:عالم جسمانی⟫ (the world of subtle bodies—from ⟪ar:تحت فلک قمر⟫ to ⟪ar:سقرا⟫), called ⟪ar:' جسم مطلق'⟫ (the Absolute Body), where the physical universe begins. ⟪ar:فلک محیط⟫ is also termed ⟪ar:ھیولیٰ اور صورت⟫ (hyle and form).

### The Hyle (*Hayūlā*): The Greater Generative Power

The Hyle is that ⟪ar:عالم امہات، ھیولی⟫ which is constituted of ⟪ar:نفس النامیۃ⟫ (the Soul of Generation). This is termed ⟪ar:نامیۃ الکبریٰ⟫ (the Greater Generative Power). Its boundaries extend from the moon to the center of Saqqara. It is the dwelling-place and source of all things; its center and origin is ⟪ar:نفس النامیۃ⟫ the moon. The ⟪ar:فلک قمر⟫ fetus is determined by the moon's governance.

### The Form (*Ṣūra*): The Greater Sensibility

That ⟪ar:عالم افلاک، صورت⟫ which is composed of ⟪ar:نفس الحسیۃ⟫ (the Soul of Sensation) is termed ⟪ar:حسیۃ الکبری⟫ (the Greater Sensibility). Its span extends from the firmament to the moon. It is the dwelling of all that possesses ⟪ar:حسیۃ⟫ (sensation), and its center and source is ⟪ar:شمس⟫ (the Sun). When a child is born into this world, it receives ⟪ar:فلک شمس⟫ its sensory nature, ⟪ar:نفس حسیۃ⟫.

That is, in the World of Life, the intellect standing in the position of al-ʿAql al-Awwal (the First Intellect) focused upon ⟪ar:فلک محیط⟫ (the Encompassing Heaven), the second intellect upon the constellational sphere, the third intellect upon the heaven of Saturn, and so forth. | Heat and Dryness | Heat and Moisture |

The collision and friction between ⟪ar:حرارت ویبوست⟫ produced lightning, which caused the clouds to compress and torrential rains to fall in all directions. When this rainwater struck the earth, it again produced vapours which ascended to the heavens. These vapours then turned into clouds and rained down once more upon the earth. Through this process, ⟪ar:بحر⟫ (the sea) was formed. This cycle of ascending and descending together as cloud is called ⟪ar:مزاج اور ممتزج⟫.

These seas formed from Saqqara's rocky matter, from which ⟪ar:جبال⟫ (mountains) and ⟪ar:حجار⟫ (rocks) were produced. These mountains eroded and broke apart, yielding sand (silicon), lime, and pebbles. Thus a sheet of earth climbed over Saqqara. On account of this earthen layer, though we walk upon Saqqara itself, we remain separated from it. For a prolonged period, rain fell upon Saqqara, creating depressions in some regions and levelling others. Through this process, twelve islands were brought forth—islands compatible with ⟪ar:قصد الٰہی⟫ (the Divine Purpose). ⟪ar:عنایت الٰہیۃ (عاشر)⟫ The Originator arranged each constellation and each heaven in its proper station, positioned every member of the membered creation in its rightful place, and established the seven heavens as rulers over ⟪ar:عالم امھات⟫ (the World of Mothers) and ⟪ar:موالید ثلاثہ⟫ (the Threefold Life-Forms). ⟪ar:عالم امھات⟫ This cosmos is called ⟪ar:عالم کون و فساد⟫ (the World of Generation and Corruption). In accordance with the order of precedence in turning to repentance, the sequence of heavens, Mothers, and living beings was established. This sequence was determined on the basis of earlier preparation and warmth of origin.

| Fathers (Āb) | Mothers (Umm) | Children (Walad) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Seven Heavens | Four Mothers | Three Life-Forms (Mineral, Plant, Animal) |

## The Sixth Movement: The Governance of the Heavens

When all the hyle, ⟪ar:ھیولی⟫, had been expended in creating the physical world, and the heavens were divided into their proper ranks—the heavens themselves, the Mothers, and Saqqara—Asher gave the heavens their sixth and final movement, which inaugurated the schemes of celestial governance, ⟪ar:تدبیرات الافلاک⟫. Each heaven devised and perfected its plan over a span of 1,000 years, and through its scheme shaped the world and brought forth the threefold life-forms, ⟪ar:موالید ثلاثۃ⟫, within ⟪ar:کرۃ الارض⟫ (the Sphere of Earth).

### The Minor Cycle

In the first thousand years, one constellation became sage and king, devising its plan in solitude. Thereafter, each of the remaining constellations, in its appointed order, deliberated and assisted the reigning king in executing his design for a thousand years. Thus seven thousand years passed—the span that marks the conclusion of the seventh heaven's cycle. This is called ⟪ar:دور صغیر⟫ (the Minor Cycle).

Saturn was the first to rule, governing alone for the initial thousand years. The six remaining planets then, one by one, joined Saturn's plan, each supporting him in his dominion for a thousand years. Thus Saturn's ⟪ar:دور صغیر⟫ lasted seven thousand years.

| Saturn | Jupiter | Mars | Sun | Venus | Mercury | Moon | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1000 (alone) | 1000 | 1000 | 1000 | 1000 | 1000 | 1000 | 7000 |

### The Great Cycle

When the first heaven's minor cycle of seven thousand years was completed, the next heaven began its reign, also completing its own seven-thousand-year minor cycle. When all seven heavens had finished their ⟪ar:دور صغیر⟫ (minor cycles), a total of fifty-one thousand years had elapsed (7,000 × 7 = 49,000 + 2,000 intervals). The entire era, beginning from when the first heaven commenced its governance, is attributed to that heaven and is termed ⟪ar:دور کبیر⟫ (the Great Cycle).[^cite-13]

For example: after Saturn had completed its seven thousand years, Jupiter began to reign. It ruled alone for a thousand years; then the six remaining heavens meditated upon it and supported its governance, each for a thousand years. Thus the seven heavens completed their ⟪ar:دور صغیر⟫, totalling fifty-one thousand years (7,000 × 7 = 49,000 + 2,000 intervals). Since Saturn was the heaven that inaugurated this period, the entire cycle—including all seven minor periods—is reckoned as ⟪ar:دور کبیر⟫ (Saturn's Great Cycle). Thus each planet's great cycle lasts fifty-one thousand years.

| Saturn | Jupiter | Mars | Sun | Venus | Mercury | Moon | Intervals | Great Cycle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7000 | 7000 | 7000 | 7000 | 7000 | 7000 | 7000 | 2000 | 51,000 |

What follows thereafter: ⟪ar:مشتری⟫ (Jupiter's) ⟪ar:دور کبیر⟫ (Great Cycle) begins. First it completes its minor cycle as sole governor; when the six remaining planets complete their minor cycles and their governance-periods, Jupiter completes its ⟪ar:دور کبیر⟫ of fifty-one thousand years.

| Minor Cycle | Great Cycle |
| --- | --- |
| 7,000 years | 51,000 years |

### An Age of Development

Every thousand years brings forth a new generation of human beings—termed one ⟪ar:کَرَۃ⟫ (rotation or generation). Thus humans are born during the governance of each planet. When fifty-one thousand years have passed, the cycle of one celestial-governance era concludes, and the distinctive qualities of that person develop fully. When three hundred sixty thousand years have been completed—encompassing all seven heavens' ⟪ar:دور کبیر⟫ (great cycles)—a believer dedicated to the Faith, ⟪ar:مستقیم السِّیر⟫, shall have advanced so greatly in terms of spiritual purity that:

| Progression |  |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | His hand reaches to touch the dwelling-place of the heart. |
| 2 | His soul rises from the rank of the Mustajīb (the Responder) to the station of the Nātiq (the Speaker-Prophet). |

## The Durations: Dūr, Kūr, Tūr, and Mūr

### The Dūr (Cycle)

These seven heavens were entrusted with the task of influencing the world through their own governance schemes and bringing down the clear essences, ⟪ar:قامت الفیۃ⟫, into Saqqara. Then, through the Imam's infidelity and godhood, they grant them death and raise them again—transforming them from the ⟪ar:ھیکل (کثافت)⟫ (temple of density) into the ⟪ar:صورت (لطافت)⟫ (form of subtlety). Then they extract them from one Imam's temple and elevate them through successive temples (from Qaʾim to Imam, from Imam to Jaʿfar, from Jaʿfar to the Peacock-Master) from which they may then ascend to the World of Light.

Each heaven scheme-making and perfected itself over the span of ⟪ar:دور کبیر⟫ (the Great Cycle) of fifty-one thousand years. That is, the seven heavens persisted for three hundred fifty-seven thousand years. Add to this three thousand years, and we arrive at three hundred sixty thousand years—the reckoning in solar terms. ⟪ar:قمری⟫ In lunar reckoning it reaches four hundred thousand years. In this manner, an entire epoch or cycle completes in three hundred sixty thousand years. There occur seven ⟪ar:کشف و ستر⟫ (unveilings and concealments) within one period of time. The span of each circle is eternally three hundred sixty degrees, just as there are roughly three hundred sixty days in a year, each indicating the completion of a circle.

### The Kūr (Core)

Multiplying the duration of a cycle by itself yields the duration of one ⟪ar:کور⟫ (core). That is, multiplying four hundred thousand years by four hundred thousand years yields a duration of one core of **16,000 crore years** (16 billion years). Each core contains four hundred thousand cycles.

| Great Cycle (Dūr) | Great Cycle (Core) | Mother's Core | Solar Reckoning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 360,000 Years | 1 Core = 360,000 Cycles | 129,600,000,000 years | 1 Mūr = 360,000 Cycles |
| Lunar Reckoning | 400,000 Years | 1 Core = 400,000 Cycles | 160,000,000,000 years |

### The Tūr (Form)

Beyond the core's duration lies that ⟪ar:طور⟫ which forms a component of the ⟪ar:مور⟫ (Mūr). One ⟪ar:طور⟫ comprises forty thousand ⟪ar:اکوار⟫ (cores). Within each Mūr are ten ⟪ar:طوریۃ⟫ (forms), which are called ⟪ar:عقل کلیۃ⟫ (universal intellects). Within the context of these ten, there exist many ⟪ar:صورات عقلیۃ⟫ (intellectual forms), the lowest of which is constituted of three hundred sixty ⟪ar:قوائم⟫ (principles).

### The Mūr (Mauress)

Multiplying the duration of a core by itself yields the duration of one ⟪ar:مورأعظم⟫ (the Greater Mauress). Within one ⟪ar:مور اعظم⟫, there are four hundred thousand ⟪ar:کور⟫ (cores), and within each core are four hundred thousand ⟪ar:ادوار⟫ (cycles), ⟪ar:اکوار⟫.

At the end of each ⟪ar:دور، کور، مور⟫ (cycle, core, mauress) there appears precisely what appeared at the beginning. Their appearances are in the form of the noon-point. ⟪ar:صاحب مور⟫ In truth, he is the Sultan.
