## The Conditions of the Cycles of Unveiling and Concealment

Just as an ordinary day comprises twenty-four hours and is divided into three periods—morning, afternoon, and night—so too does the Divine Day possess a religious duration of fifty-seven thousand years, ⟪ar:دور کشف، فترت اور ستر⟫. The daytime extends for fifty thousand years, with the first portion being forty-seven thousand years, which is ⟪ar:دور کشف⟫ (the Cycle of Unveiling—the morning), and the final portion being three thousand years, which is ⟪ar:دور فترت⟫ (the Cycle of Interruption—the afternoon). The night lasts seven thousand years, termed ⟪ar:دور ستر⟫ (the Cycle of Concealment):

| Morning | Afternoon | Night |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unveiling Cycle | Interruption Cycle | Concealment Cycle |
| 47,000 years | 3,000 years | 7,000 years |

### Conditions of the Unveiling Cycle

During ⟪ar:دور کشف⟫ (the Unveiling), the inner truths and realities, ⟪ar:علوم باطن حقیقیۃ⟫, shall be revealed. Although the ordinances of the revealed Law shall not be binding in the period of unveiling, the people of that era shall attain such spiritual heights that their obligatory practices shall exceed the practices of the concealment-era believers. Just so: though fasting is not binding upon them, they shall fast more ardently than those ⟪ar:اہل دور ستر⟫ of the concealment cycle, and though zakāt (the obligatory alms) is not binding, their voluntary charity shall surpass sevenfold that of the concealment-era faithful. ⟪ar:دور کشف⟫ The practice of circumcision shall continue, but in ⟪ar:ہَشْفَۃ⟫ some individuals (the circumcised) it shall not become apparent.

The bodies of the unveiling cycle shall resemble those of the concealment cycle, yet with this difference: they shall be exceedingly delicate and pure. During this period there shall be no disease, for there exist no germs therein. Germs are in fact manifestations of our own transgressions and iniquities, which arise together with corporeality. In the era of unveiling, only halāl (permissible) crops and halāl animals shall exist. All the malevolence of harmful creatures—mosquitoes, fleas, and the like—shall be prevented from the people of unveiling.

In the unveiling cycle, believers shall alone exist, yet alongside them shall also be brought forth the pure Shiʿa of ʿAlī; all of them, however, shall be subordinate to the believers and shall serve as their servants. Very lofty realities and exalted worlds, ⟪ar:عولم حقائق عالیۃ⟫, shall be revealed upon the pulpit. In this era, there shall be no enmity, and thus no hostility anywhere. Should it occur anywhere, it shall be exceedingly slight, remaining only at the level of the heart and never expressed outwardly; and all this shall also occur at the end of the world, in the ⟪ar:(دور فترت)⟫ (Interruption Cycle).

Beyond this, all the burdensome ordinances of the revealed Law shall be lifted. Only ⟪ar:شریعت عقلیۃ⟫ (the Intellectual Law)—matters of marriage, slavery, purity, inheritance, and the like—shall remain. ⟪ar:حسیۃ⟫ The sensory experiences shall diminish, thereby removing anger, hardness of heart, physical exhaustion, and lust. People shall be inclined toward piety and reverence to the utmost degree, and the conjugal bond between husband and wife shall occur but once yearly, solely to fulfil the Sunna (exemplary practice). When he enters ⟪ar:برج حمل⟫ (the House of the Ram), ⟪ar:بیت الشرف⟫ only then shall the husband cohabit with his wife so that she might conceive and fulfill the Divine command. Beyond this, there shall be no marriage. Death too shall come without sickness. People shall intend their own death and impose it upon themselves.

### Conditions of the Concealment Cycle

There are two types of summons (daʿwa, the invitation) in the concealment cycle: the inward summons and the outward summons. The inward summons comprises the inward invitation of the Divine Stations (the Imāms), ⟪ar:مقامات الٰہیۃ (ائمہ)⟫, their ⟪ar:ابواب⟫ (gates), ⟪ar:حجتوں⟫ (proofs), the ⟪ar:دعات⟫ (summoners), and the ⟪ar:ماذونین⟫ (authorized ones)—all dwelling in ⟪ar:ھیاکل نورانیۃ⟫ (luminous temples). When the cycle began with Adam (peace be upon him), these people concealed themselves for fear of their enemies. The outward summons comprises the supplications of the Imāms. These supplications arise from the outward summons and receive their command from the Imām hidden behind the veil, summoning people to him. Those who respond to the outward summons are drawn from it and guided toward the inward summons of their ⟪ar:امام⟫ (Imām), their ⟪ar:دعوت باطنۃ⟫ (inward invitation). For this reason, our Master ʿAlī al-Jamālī (the Graceful) said: ⟪ar:سیدنا علی الجمالی⟫ "I am ⟪ar:امام⟫ like a pen in the hand of a scribe—the ⟪ar:امام⟫ Imām."

## The First Motion: Length, Width, and Depth

Al-ʿĀshir resolved to fashion the physical world from the disobedient faction and to confine them within it. Yet in their spiritual state, their imprisonment was impossible; he was therefore obliged to transmute them into corporeality first. The analogy is of a candle burning upon a tablet: one cannot remove the candle without its tablet.[^cite-4] In executing this transmutation, his first intention was to generate within these beings the three dimensions of illusion—length, width, and depth—which are the hallmarks of physicality. The Qurʾān illuminates this decree:

> ⟪quran 77:30⟫
> ⟪ar:‏ٱنطَلِقُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ ظِلٍّۢ ذِى ثَلْثِ شُعَبٍۢ ‎⟫
> *Depart you to a shadow of three columns.*
> — **Qurʾān 77:30**

In implementing al-ʿĀshir's command (⟪ar:اھبطو⟫, "descend"), he first began to diminish the luminosity of the disobedient faction, whereupon they grew dense and terror-stricken.

### First Movement: The Generation of Length

As the brightness of these beings faded, panic seized them and they began to affect one another—colliding and rubbing together as clouds chafe against one another. To escape this state of dread and confusion, each being moved away from itself toward the self of another, and this movement created length. This length was not yet physical, but rather existed in the "wild" or potential state (⟪ar:طول بالقوۃ⟫) from which physical length would eventually be born. This constituted the first motion. From this longitudinal motion, heat was generated, and two celestial constellations—Aries and the second Aries—were formed. As heat declined toward its contrary extreme, coldness emerged, and two further constellations—Pisces and Libra—came into being with this coldness. All these creations unfolded in the potential realm:

| Heat (ḥarāra) | Cold (burūda) |
| --- | --- |
| Pregnancy and gestation | Fixity and solidity |

### Second Movement: The Generation of Width

After the first motion, terror intensified among them. To escape this condition, they executed a second motion in which they fled from one another, generating a whirling motion. Alongside this, moisture (ruṭūba) and dryness (yubūsa) were produced. Two celestial authorities—Capricorn and Aquarius—were formed with the moisture, while with dryness came Sagittarius and Cancer.

| Moisture (Ruṭūba) | Dryness (Yubūsa) |
| --- | --- |
| Capricorn and Aquarius | Sagittarius and Cancer |

### Third Movement: The Generation of Depth

When length and width had been created, the beings perceived that they had grown increasingly imprisoned within matter. To escape the horror of these two dimensions, they enacted a third motion, generating the third dimension—depth (ʿumq). This motion produced no new constellation or temperament (mizāj).

Before the advent of length, width, and depth, all beings existed as distinct individuals, each maintaining its own reality. Yet when overwhelmed by the ⟪ar:ثلاثہ ابعاد⟫ (three dimensions), they lost their individuality entirely. The analogy is instructive: if three distinct colors are placed separately, each remains clearly visible; but when mixed and blended, their individual natures dissolve and they fuse into a single different hue. So too did these beings, upon being seized by length, width, and depth, commingle with one another until their individuality vanished and they coalesced into a unified condition—the ⟪ar:ھیولی⟫ (hylē, primordial matter) in its most potential state.

A yellow arrow from the central intersection points downward to the label 'مجمع کیفیت' (Composite Quality).]

After these three motions, the beings did not execute a fourth; this was precisely what they desired. They lament that had they possessed patience and refrained from motion, they would not have descended into the physical world. Their impatience precipitated their division into hylē and form (ṣūra).

## Primordial Matter and Secondary Matter: Hylē I and Hylē II

When the three motions were completed, all beings took on the nature of ⟪ar:ھیولی⟫ (hylē, primordial matter) and ⟪ar:صورت⟫ (ṣūra, form), and owing to the ⟪ar:ثقل⟫ (weight) of the hylē they began to densify. This is why all things in the present age are encompassed within these three dimensions.

Within this collective mass, those individuals who had responded receptively to al-ʿĀshir's daʿwa (the summons / the invitation) rose to the higher ranks and became ⟪ar:صورت⟫ (form)—the actuating principle. Those less receptive became the ⟪ar:ھیولی⟫ (hylē)—the receptive principle. Form is always more potent and luminous and more active; hylē is more transparent and passive. Through Divine solicitude (⟪ar:عنایت الٰہیہ⟫), al-ʿĀshir determined to fashion objects from hylē and form. Those superior in capacity and endowed with the status of masculine (the influencers) were made into the celestial spheres (⟪ar:افلاک⟫, aflāk); those of feminine status (the effect-receivers) were made into the elemental kingdoms (⟪ar:امہات⟫, ummahāt).

| Masculine (Influencers) | Feminine (Effect-Receivers) |
| --- | --- |
| Seven Planets and the Zodiacal Sphere | The Four Elemental Kingdoms |

The term ⟪ar:ھیولی⟫ (hylē) is composed of two words: ⟪ar:ھیاوا + اولی⟫ (hiyāwāʾ + ūlā), meaning "the first preparation" or "primal receptivity." Preparation denotes capacity and readiness to receive influence. Hylē, then, is a substance capable of accepting impressions and effects. In the condition of Hylē, all beings—whether masculine or feminine—possessed the capacity to receive influence and thereby came to consciousness of causality, so that they might be extracted from the spiritual world.

### Hylē I (Primordial Matter)

When light was stripped from these beings, they fell into panic and enacted three motions that generated the three delusory dimensions of length, width, and depth. All beings commingled with one another, their individuality vanishing; they coalesced into one undifferentiated mass. This condition is termed ⟪ar:ھیولی أولی⟫ (Hylē I).

### Hylē II (Secondary Matter)

Even in the state of Hylē I, these beings received invitations—both toward mercy and toward rebellion. Both invitations were being transmitted; all beings were hearing them and responding to their effects. Because of their responsiveness, they became divided into different factions according to their stance toward al-ʿĀshir. Some remained adamant in disobedience and arrogant; others repented of their error and stood ready to obey al-ʿĀshir; yet others wavered in doubt, uncertain whether to repent or persist in defiance.[^cite-5] Thus they became mentally divided into three sects.

The greater the density of intention crystallizing within them, the more profoundly length, width, and depth ⟪ar:تجسم⟫ (took material form) upon them, leading to the emergence of another form of ⟪ar:ھیولی⟫ and ⟪ar:صورت⟫. In the terminology of the daʿwa, the hylē is called ⟪ar:نامیۃ⟫ (the receptive principle, lit. "the naming"), and the form is called ⟪ar:حسیۃ⟫ (the sensible principle). The hylē that then ⟪ar:صورت⟫ assumed dominion was designated ⟪ar:ھیولی ثانی⟫ (Hylē II), and it received the command ⟪ar:اھبطو⟫ (descend).

By this point three sects had been established in their intentions: the repentant (⟪ar:نادمین⟫), the vacillating (⟪ar:شاکین⟫), and the obdurate (⟪ar:مصرین⟫). Some individuals were shifting between sects by accepting the influence of both the merciful call (⟪ar:رحمانی دعوت⟫) and the call of rebellion. Some who initially insisted on disobedience came to accept the merciful invitation and joined the ⟪ar:نادمین⟫ (repentant). Others who first showed signs of repentance succumbed to the call of rebellion (⟪ar:ابلیسی دعوت⟫) and became ⟪ar:مصرین⟫ (obdurate). This fluidity was occurring in the spiritual realm. Yet as soon as the command ⟪ar:اھبطو⟫ (descend) was executed, al-ʿĀshir effected a freezing of all intentions. Never again could any being shift from one sect to another. This phenomenon is called ⟪ar:انجماد مآء⟫ (the freezing of waters). When the command of descent was issued, beings fell downward from the subtle realm due to their density, for every dense thing falls downward by the law of gravity, while every subtle thing rises upward by its own nature.[^cite-6]

| Hylē I | The state of length, width, and depth in which all beings became confused and lost their individuality |
| --- | --- |
| Hylē II | The post-descent state in which all intentions were frozen, in which the repentant, the vacillating, and the obdurate were separated from one another according to their respective intentions |

> — *Correlative observations*

The first faction, realizing their error, repented and sought forgiveness, acknowledging the preeminence of the First Intellect (al-ʿAql al-Awwal). Through this repentance, they became distinguished from the other two sects. Though they could not be prevented from descending, they were halted at the level corresponding to their repentance. Yet because this repentance occurred after the freezing had taken effect, they were obliged to join the physical world. This sect is known as ⟪ar:نادمین ومستغفرین⟫ (the Repentant and the Seeking Forgiveness).

The second faction, remaining in ⟪ar:شاک و متحیر⟫ (vacillation and bewilderment), could not determine whether to repent or persist in error. They are called ⟪ar:شاک و متحیر⟫ (the Vacillating and Bewildered).

The third faction, insisting on denial and rebellion against the Creator, are termed ⟪ar:مصرین و مستکبرین⟫ (the Obdurate and the Arrogant).

| Repentant and Seeking Forgiveness | Belief in the Creator; acknowledgment of the Precedence of the First Intellect |
| --- | --- |
| Vacillating and Bewildered | Belief in the Creator but considering all beings equal in primacy |
| Obdurate and Arrogant | Deniers of the Creator and opponents of all revealed truth |

When the ⟪ar:ثلاثہ ابعاد(طول، عرض، عمق)⟫ (three dimensions: length, width, depth) converged and ⟪ar:حیت ہبوت⟫ (the descent took effect), the physical world was formed according to the intentions and natures of each faction and their hylē. The purest portion—drawn from the first sect—was exalted into the heavens, a luminous realm whose radiance reflects the beauty and righteousness of these beings. The celestial sphere possesses minimal density relative to lower realms and was therefore stationed at the apex. ⟪ar:بروج⟫ The zodiacal sphere, being denser, occupies a lower position; below it ⟪ar:فلک زحل، فلک مشتری،⟫ the seven heavens descended in descending order of subtlety. The degrees of density in these celestial spheres mirror the varying density-grades of bodily organs, each organ having been formed according to the intention (and density-level) of those beings from which it arose. ⟪ar:شاک و متحر⟫ From the second sect—the Vacillating—the four elemental kingdoms (fire, air, water, earth) were fashioned, whose essential nature is restlessness and movement. The instability of the elements springs from the uncertainty of those who comprise them. ⟪ar:مصر و مستکبرین⟫ Due to the rigidity and obstinacy of the third sect, they were constituted as the frozen crust (saqrāʾ) ⟪ar:(crust)⟫ and the terrestrial realm.

### Establishment of Intentions in the Subtle World (ʿĀlam al-Niyyāt)

Because all these beings—possessing different intentions and natures—were intermixed, they began to develop relationships and intentions with one another, and through these interactions they created circumstances. All relationships, friendships, enmities, bonds, forms, garments, and neighborhoods were established in this realm through three mechanisms:

| Istiḥsān | Regarding an evil thing as good |
| --- | --- |
| Milān | Inclining toward and assisting in evil |
| Qiṣāṣ | Enacting the evil deed oneself |

Beyond merely creating relationships and enmities, the intentions themselves gave rise to our outward forms, stature, complexion, and all other characteristics within ⟪ar:عالم نیات⟫ (the World of Intentions). Whatever one desires in the eternal realm, one receives in this world. To offer clarification by example: those whom we regarded in eternity with love alone became our brothers or sisters in this world. One we observed with mingled love and hatred became our spouse. Those seen through eyes of plague became our parents. Thus some faces inspire love in our hearts, and others hatred, even though we have never met them—their appearance resonates with intentions formed long before.

## The Prayer of the Descending Repentant

When ⟪ar:أنجماد مآء⟫ the freezing of waters occurred and Hylē was commanded to descend, al-ʿĀshir and ⟪ar:اہل کلمم⟫ those of his word (the celestial ministers) gazed upon the repentant faction with a look of longing and mercy, consoling them. The Qurʾān preserves the divine pledge:

> ⟪quran 2:38⟫
> ⟪ar:‏قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۭا ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًۭى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ ‎⟫
> *We said: "Descend, all of you from here. Yet if there comes to you guidance from Me, those who follow My guidance shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve."*
> — **Qurʾān 2:38**

> ⟪quran 19:72⟫
> ⟪ar:‏ثُمَّ نُنَجِّى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوا۟ وَّنَذَرُ ٱلظَّلِمِينَ فِيهَا جِثِيًّۭا ‎⟫
> *Then We shall deliver those who feared, leaving the evildoers therein on their knees.*
> — **Qurʾān 19:72**

Al-ʿĀshir assured them: "Though you must descend into this physicality as consequence of your error, take solace! Since you have held fast to us, we shall come into this world as Muḥammad and ʿAlī and shall guide you from this physical world toward peace and salvation." As they descended, the repentant faction offered praise to Allāh, which the Qurʾān has preserved in immortal words:

> ⟪quran 10:10⟫
> ⟪ar:‏دَعْوَىٰهُمْ فِيهَا سُبْحَنَكَ ٱللَّهُمَّ وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيهَا سَلَمٌۭ ۚ وَآخِرُ دَعْوَىٰهُمْ أَنِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَلَمِينَ ‎⟫
> *Their invocation therein is "Glory be to You, O Allāh!" and their greeting therein is "Peace!" and the close of their invocation is "All praise belongs to Allāh, Lord of the Worlds."*
> — **Qurʾān 10:10**

In their descent, the repentant sect praised al-ʿĀshir, offering no complaint that he had corrupted them or that without his action they would not have fallen. Instead they praised him—and it was precisely because of this praise that al-ʿĀshir undertook to be the first to draw them back from the physical world. For this reason this prayer is recited at the conclusion of every gathering, just as it was recited when al-ʿĀshir departed the assembly.

The tradition records that when the disobedient faction transgressed against al-ʿĀshir and subsequently confessed their error and sought his forgiveness, both moments were marked by the letter *lā* (negation). When they disobeyed, they declared: ⟪ar-quote:لاَ نُسمِعُ وَلاَ نُطِیعُ⟫ ("We do not listen to you, nor do we obey you"). When they acknowledged their error, they proclaimed: ⟪ar-quote:لا الہ الا اللہ⟫ ("There is no god save al-ʿĀshir"). Thus the entire spiritual map has been established upon the foundation of the Word of Sincerity (Kalimah).

In the second motion, the most repentant essence rose upward—this is called ⟪ar:اول النوادم⟫ (the First of the Repentant). This occurred because subtle substance always ascends. Al-ʿĀshir then set this leaven—the First of the Repentant—into circulation, and through this action four celestial powers came into being:

| Tenth (ʿāshir) | West (ghārib) | Fourth (rābiʿ) | East (ṭāliʿ) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

These are like four spiritual anchors that held the entire cosmic mass in place and prevented further descent. It is due to these four forces that the whole world remains fixed in its position. All four dwell within the ⟪ar:فلک محیط⟫ (the Encompassing Sphere) and upon the border of the zodiac. The first, the ⟪ar:طالع⟫ (Ascendant), stands above, at the eastern horizon of the zodiac. The second, the ⟪ar:رابع⟫ (Fourth), lies below the earth—which is why the earth only rotates in place and cannot orbit. Since the entire universe is held stationary by these four forces, its center—the earth—remains motionless. All other planets ⟪ar:(سیارات السابتۃ)⟫ except earth orbit their spheres. The third force, the ⟪ar:عاشر⟫ (Tenth), stands in the east. The fourth, the ⟪ar:غارب⟫ (West), stands in the west. Two further dimensions complete the scheme: the ⟪ar:قطب شمالی⟫ (North Pole) and ⟪ar:قطب جنوبی⟫ (South Pole), representing the vertical axis of up and down. Thus these four forces complete the six dimensional axes: up, down, right, left, forward, back.[^cite-7] For this reason, the entire physical world and all within it is encompassed in six dimensions.

## The Governors of the Spheres and the Zodiac

These four forces became magnets of subtlety, drawing subtle essence upward from the hylē. Through their attraction, the most refined beings—the ⟪ar:نادمین و مستغفرین⟫ (Repentant and Seeking Forgiveness)—gathered at the periphery; the ⟪ar:شاک و متحیر⟫ (Vacillating and Bewildered) assembled at the middle; and the ⟪ar:مصر و مستکبرین⟫ (Obdurate and Arrogant) crystallized at the interior. The highest among the Repentant gathered at the circumference of the zodiacal sphere. These twelve beings are termed the Governors of the Zodiac (⟪ar:مدبری البروج⟫). They are also called ⟪ar:عقول عالم طبعیت⟫ (the Intellects of the Physical World).

---

**Learned Observation:** The celestial sphere of environment is the most subtle of all heavens and contains no visible stars or planets. The celestial constellations and zodiacal signs are in truth the governors of the heavens, constantly working to extract subtle essences and raise densities. Among the wise ones whom al-ʿĀshir commissioned as counselors, two bear special names: one is called ⟪ar:عین⟫ (ʿayn, the Supreme), and his deputy is called ⟪ar:میم⟫ (mīm, the Completing).

---

The terrestrial realm ⟪ar:سقرأ⟫ (saqrāʾ), through the four forces of the hylē, crystallized into the form of a stone, and the monstrous density of length and width overwhelmed it physically.[^cite-8]

Al-ʿĀshir then imparted a third motion to the hylē. This motion, acting at the point where ⟪ar:حَیتِ السَّلِیب⟫ (the condition of cross-compression) obtained, gave rise to ⟪ar:عمق اول⟫ (the First Depth). At this juncture—where the forces of length and width and their four temperaments converged—a center was established. This center is called the First Depth. Yet the universe itself constitutes the fifth temperament, for these four are derived from it and exist as aspects of it; their aggregate is itself this fifth nature. ## The Generation of Time and Space

With the eruption of the cosmic vessel, physicality came into being, and with physicality came time and space. The ⟪ar:کواکب سابتۃ⟫ (fixed stars) and ⟪ar:کواکب سیارۃ⟫ (wandering planets) undergo no corruption or alteration; neither do they diminish nor increase in magnitude. Their motion is purely circular, a form that signifies the perfection of celestial movement. The circle is the most perfect form in geometry!

---

**Learned Observation:** The author of the *Epistles of the Brethren of Purity* (⟪ar:صاحب رسائل اخوان الصفا⟫) explains that time is intrinsically connected to space, and the two are mutually dependent. The existence of one is impossible without the other.

---

These seven heavens exert their influence upon the four elemental kingdoms through ⟪ar:موالید ثلاثۃ⟫ (the Three Kingdoms of Coming-to-be), combining them with the ⟪ar:نفوس (حسیۃ، نامیۃ)⟫ (souls—both sensible and receptive) for the purpose of their manifestation, that they might be born into this world. The elemental kingdoms cannot accomplish this independently; they depend upon the heavens, just as a woman depends upon a man to conceive a child.

### Time (al-Zamān)

The author of the *Epistles* teaches that time is a pure and formal power whose effects manifest in the soul through the unceasing passage of day and night. An analogy illuminates this: imagine numbering that commences with one and progresses through continuous addition: one plus one yields two; then one plus two yields three; and so forth. Time's origin is bound to this physical world—as soon as the world was brought forth and physicality descended upon it, time commenced from that very moment. Thus time is not the designation of a fixed span, but the mark of the termination of time itself (⟪ar:یوم القیامۃ⟫, the Day of Resurrection).

### Space (al-Makān)

The author of the *Epistles* further teaches that space does not exist outside this world; rather, it is a condition intrinsic to physicality. Where physical bodies exist, space exists. Thus to debate whether a vacuum or a plenum exists beyond the limits of the universe is an idle inquiry. For there is no space outside this world, and where space is absent, neither void nor plenum can obtain. The boundary of any physical object is its space. The Brotherhood of Purity denies the existence of vacuum beyond this world. Empty space is a space containing nothing and left void. Space is an attribute of physical things—it can be encountered only where physical objects exist. Therefore, where physical objects do not exist, space itself cannot exist; and where space does not exist, neither emptiness nor fullness can be found. To the contrary, the Brotherhood affirms that though space may appear empty, it is never truly devoid. Within this world there is no place wherein spirits do not dwell. Elucidating this truth, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allāh be upon him) declared: ⟪ar-quote:لاَ خَلاَ وَلاَ مَلاَ فِی الھَوَا⟫ ("The air is neither empty nor full").

### The Transition from Spirituality to Physicality

Spirituality is subtle; physicality is dense. All subtle things ascend toward spirituality, and all dense things descend toward physicality—for all things return to their origin. Since all beings of Hylē II belonged to the disobedient faction, their intention was coarse and unrefined. This density was mitigated in the Repentant faction by their remorse. The Vacillating faction was denser than the Repentant ⟪ar:شاک و متحیرین⟫, for their intention was more cumbersome. The Obdurate ⟪ar:مصر و مستکبرین⟫ possessed the greatest density. The density of these three factions was transformed into physicality by the weight of their conditions. Thus in this present physical world, the heavens are the subtlest of all realms, the elemental kingdoms occupy a middle density, and the terrestrial sphere (saqrāʾ) is the most dense.

An instructive example is water vapor, which is subtle; yet when cooling generates weight within it, the vapor becomes liquid water—a denser form. When this water is cooled further, density increases until it freezes into ice, the densest form of the same substance. Coldness, being contrary to oppression, inclines toward tranquility; the more coarse the intention, the more sluggish the descent (⟪ar:ھبوط⟫) and the more scarce good deeds become, and consequently the greater the density. Heat, by contrast, dwells in the realm of subtle intention and inclines toward motion, generating movement toward righteous deeds and creating the subtlety that is the cause of every ascent!

## The Fourth Motion: The Generation of the Stars and the Terrestrial Sphere

Al-ʿĀshir circulated the hylē a fourth time through the sphere of the heavens, an action that caused the heavy elements within the heavens to gather and crystallize.

### The Fixed Stars (Kawākib Thābita) and the Wandering Planets (Kawākib Sāyyāra)

Like the human form, the heavens were gradually differentiated and arranged. From this hylē the seven stars of the seven heavens and the stars of the eighth constellation came forth, and they began to revolve in their respective spheres. The portion of hylē possessing the lowest density (greatest subtlety) formed the ⟪ar:فلک محیط⟫ (Encompassing Sphere)—the most subtle of all heavens.

From the outer surface of the universe to the center of the earth lies the circumference sphere in which the Encompassing Sphere operates. The zodiacal constellation extends from the lower boundary of the circumference to the earth's center. Similarly, the sphere of each heaven extends from its outermost limit to the earth's center. For this reason, on the Day of Judgment, when the heavens are rolled up, they shall descend upon the earth—not ascend. Though the paths and expanse of these heavens are immeasurably vast, they float in the upper regions.

In a single day (twenty-four hours), the Encompassing Sphere completes a full revolution of the entire world through ⟪ar:حرکۃ کلیۃ الہیۃ⟫ (the All-Encompassing Divine Motion) of the wise one. This motion proceeds from east to west. Since the earth is the center of this motion, it completes one rotation in twenty-four hours—for the faster the periphery rotates, the faster its center must turn.

### The Zodiac (al-Burūj)

Allāh has divided the zodiacal constellation into twelve parts. Each part contains thirty lesser constellations, yielding a total of (12 × 30 =) 360 smaller divisions. All stars are distributed within these constellations. The Prophet Idrīs (peace be upon him), who transmitted knowledge of stellar science (⟪ar:علم الفلکیات⟫), devoted thirty years of his life to its attainment. One may observe that six constellations are visible at any given time, and at different seasons, the next six constellations appear; the stars within them form varied patterns to which you have assigned different names.

| Aries | Pisces | Aquarius | Capricorn | Sagittarius | Scorpio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Taurus | Gemini | Cancer | Leo | Virgo | Libra |

### The Sphere of the Sun (Falak al-Shams)

The Sun was the first to embrace the effect in the physical world and to become ⟪ar:مُنفَعِل⟫ (receptive to influence), manifesting the first perfection (kamāl awwal / الكمال الأول), which stands in the station of the First Intellect (al-ʿAql al-Awwal). Though the Sun was the first to be activated, it is the fourth in the celestial order. In the microcosm of man, the heart's primal point fulfills this role, occupying a position opposite to ⟪ar:شمس⟫ the celestial Sun in the heavens. Just as the heart is the center of the human body's ⟪ar:حرارت غریزیۃ⟫ (innate heat), the Sun is the center of the universe's ⟪ar:حرارت غریزیۃ⟫ (cosmic heat). Though the ⟪ar:شمس⟫ Sun appears as a sphere of light, it possesses density. As the heart in the human body is the center from which all bodily function derives, so ⟪ar:شمس⟫ the Sun is the focal point of all celestial spheres. The essential purpose of all these rotations is to draw dense elements downward through the ⟪ar:شمس⟫ Sun and cause components to manifest in the ⟪ar:قامت الفیۃ⟫ (physical realm), whence they progress upward through the celestial spheres. Not only do the heavens descend into the encompassing world—the Sun lifts what rises from below.

Above the Sun there are ⟪ar:زحل، مشتری، مریخ⟫ (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars)—three heavens—and below it there are ⟪ar:زہرہ، عطارد، قمر⟫ (Venus, Mercury, Moon)—three heavens. The elemental kingdoms lie below the Sun as well, and all receive its influence. The Sun's origin in al-ʿĀshir's motions remains the same as the three dimensions ⟪ar:طول، عرض، عمق⟫ (length, width, depth). Among the heavens, after the Encompassing Sphere, the Sun ranks foremost in nobility and virtue. It holds this preeminence because when all beings ⟪ar:حالت انحدار⟫ (were in a state of descent) in their disobedience, the Sun was among the first to repent and repent, to glorify the First Intellect and to sanctify and worship Allāh. Because of its monotheistic devotion and wisdom, it was filled with light as a reward. ⟪ar:شمس⟫ The Sun is subject to the Encompassing Sphere, and the light of every star, constellation, and zodiacal sign reflects the glory of what it accomplished when it fell and repented.

---

**Learned Observation:** The lights of the five daily prayers are sent down through the heavens from the realm of life, and the heavens surrounding the earth transmit them downward through the rays of ⟪ar:شمس⟫ the Sun. For this reason, the times appointed for all five prayers are established according to the course of the Sun.

---

### The Remaining Celestial Bodies

Following the Sun, the Moon came into being, dwelling in the station of the head (intellect) of the physical world, serving as the center of fluidity and radiation. Saturn and Mars were then formed as a dual force, centers of coldness and dryness. Subsequently, the remaining heavens were fashioned, and all the spheres gathered into one absolute body.

### The Encompassing Sphere (Falak al-Muḥīṭ)

In comparison to the other heavens, the Encompassing Sphere stands in the position of the soul. It is the ⟪ar:مُحَرِّک⟫ (mover) that animates the absolute body, and through day and night it rotates the heavens in their cavities. It is their house and foundation—the sphere from which they began.

| Encompassing Sphere | Sphere of the Sun | Lunar Sphere | Saturn's Sphere |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spirit | Heart | Brain | The Two Feet |
| Activating Force | Heat + Dryness | Cold + Moisture | Cold + Dryness |

The true purpose of all these celestial bodies is the creation of man. All forms in this world manifest through the lights of these heavens. ### The Terrestrial Sphere (Saqrāʾ)

Contemporaneously with the generation of these celestial bodies, the Saqrāʾ—the dense terrestrial crust—was also developed, formed in the shape of an inverted vessel. Its inner composition, which science designates as the Mantle and Core, is in reality the infernal realm (Jahannam). It is vast and immense, filled with an explosive and turbulent atmosphere. According to scientific investigation, the greatest flame emerging from the Sun extends two hundred miles in length; yet the heat and intensity of the Solar fire pale in comparison to the heat and ferocity of the infernal realm. The infernal heat is countless times more severe and terrible. It contains seventy valleys, each bearing distinct names, and within it flow rivers and rise mountains. Different pathways lead to entry and exit. Four gates provide entrance to this realm—three upon the earth and one in water. Only the most obstinate transgressors are brought down into the Saqrāʾ.

---

**Learned Observation:** Though the Sacred House (the Kaaba) stands upon this Saqrāʾ, it is not positioned at the apex of Hell but rather to the left. The same pattern obtains in the human body: the ⟪ar:سبیلین⟫ (two channels of impurity) stand in the station of Hell, while the heart occupies the station of the Kaaba—and in the human body, the heart is indeed displaced toward the left.

---

Saqrāʾ does not denote the common soil upon which we dwell. Saqrāʾ is the densest realm and is constituted of ⟪ar:فرقۃ ثالثۃ⟫ (the Third Faction—those who denied the Creator). All water, earth, fire, and air within it belong to the Third Faction. Above the crust of Saqrāʾ lies a stratum of clay, which forms the fourth sphere of the elemental kingdoms and is composed of ⟪ar:شاک و متحیرین (فرقۃ ثانیۃ)⟫ (the Second Faction—the Vacillating and Bewildered). By al-ʿĀshir's design, it was necessary that a human being emerge upon the Saqrāʾ and thereafter progress upward. Since the entire universe is circular in form, the earth is positioned at the center of this cosmos. All the heavens and celestial spheres exert their influence upon it, bringing about transformations in this world.

# People and their Types

## What Are Souls and How Do They Emerge?

There is a life force that exists in a hidden state throughout the world. When the darkness of the spiritual realm descended, it fell into the form of substance and shape. Therefore, whatever exists in this universe today manifests in the form of *hyle* (ḥūlī, matter) and form; whatever bears the character of *namiyyah* (نامیۃ, the vegetative principle) remains in a hidden state.[^cite-1]

It exists in concealment within minerals, accompanied by other forces. ⟪ar:قوت نامیۃ،⟫ When droplets of seawater rise from the earth as vapor and encounter the spheres of air and fire, they receive their portion from those spheres, then descend as clouds. When this water falls repeatedly upon minerals, it appears in the form of vegetation—the hidden ⟪ar:قوت نامیۃ⟫ within them—and is called ⟪ar:نفس نامیۃ⟫ by scholars. Plants possess the power to rise and increase in mass, a capacity absent in minerals. In minerals, this force remains potential; in plants, it has become actual. On account of ⟪ar:قوت نامیۃ⟫, plants now absorb nourishment from the earth and grow in length, width, and depth.

When an animal or human being—which is a branch of the animal kingdom—consumes this plant, it ⟪ar:نفس نامیۃ⟫ becomes ⟪ar:نطفہ⟫ within the body. When sperm passes from the male to the female and their fluids unite, pregnancy is established. So long as the child remains in the mother's womb, ⟪ar:نفس حسیۃ⟫ functions in a potential state, while the vegetative principle ⟪ar:نفس نامیۃ⟫ remains active.

When the newborn emerges from the mother's womb, the sun's rays awaken the inner ⟪ar:نفس حسیۃ⟫. The child gradually advances, and the inner ⟪ar:ناطقۃ مجازی⟫ self—the faculty of metaphorical speech—begins to actualize, until, through learning, he reaches the station of a beneficiary (*mustafīd*, the receiver of knowledge). Then, when he places his hand in the hand of his Ruler and takes the covenant of Imam al-Zaman with sincerity, he receives what is called the ⟪ar:'نفس ناطقۃ الحقیقی'⟫ true rational soul, and ⟪ar:تامور⟫ the divine spark attaches to what lies within him—⟪ar:خمیرۃ الندامت⟫ the essence of contrition. ⟪ar:نفس ناطقۃ⟫ This is its designation. Throughout his life, he strives to make ⟪ar:نفس حسیۃ⟫ the sensible soul luminous, for it stands ⟪ar:نفس ناطقۃ⟫ in shadow to the rational soul.

When the beneficiary progresses to mature understanding in the summons (*daʿwa*, the spiritual invitation) and attains the rank of benefactor (*munʿim*, the giver of benefit), he acquires ⟪ar:نفس ناطقۃ⟫⟪ar:نفس کلیۃ⟫ the universal soul, by means of which he becomes capable of instructing others. The individual soul (*nafs juzʾīyya*) forms its component; in contrast, the universal (*nafs kullīyya*) constitutes its perfection. When ⟪ar:نفس کلیۃ⟫ is attained, he enters the category of ⟪ar:'مطلق'⟫ the absolute, able to teach others; the confirmations of the upper limit then begin to manifest upon him. He himself becomes ⟪ar:'نفس'⟫ soul; the one above him becomes ⟪ar:'عقل'⟫ intellect; and the one below becomes ⟪ar:'جسم'⟫ body. If there is an Imam, then ⟪ar:نفس⟫ he possesses intellect ⟪ar:قائم⟫ standing firm. If the soul ⟪ar:نفس⟫ stands, then the intellect ⟪ar:عقل⟫ is a luxury—a superfluous gift.

## Types of Souls

The self is singular in essence, yet its forces emerge at different times and stations. The rise of these forces has received distinct names. When the fetus in the mother's womb possesses only the power to grow, it is named ⟪ar:نفس نامیۃ⟫ the vegetative soul. When the five senses activate outside the womb, it receives the name ⟪ar:نفس حسیۃ⟫ the sensible soul. When the powers of thought, remembrance, debate, and comprehension of the reality of objects become operational, it is named ⟪ar:نفس ناطقۃ⟫ the rational soul. And when it attains the capacity to harness the power of knowledge fully, it is named ⟪ar:نفس کلیۃ⟫ the universal soul.[^cite-2]

*Nafs* is the union of true knowledge and action. If knowledge and action are not correct, it remains merely *nafs*. It is commanded to water the animal before slaughter—that is, before taking the noble covenant, it is vital to deliver the sermon of the covenant that dwells in the palace of water. From this, the respondent's form begins to acquire knowledge, upon which the soul rests. Since the soul itself is infinitely subtle, it also requires a most subtle center, which is the form of the believer.

# Births

## The Heavens' Creations

The principal purpose governing all the celestial spheres was to generate minerals, plants, animals, and human seed ⟪ar:(سلالۃ)⟫. In their appointed succession, each sphere exerted its influence upon this terrestrial realm according to its nature, extracting and constituting diverse elements, and bringing them forth upon the earth. These four categories of being are constituted from the residue of the three principles, and the heavens continually draw this residue from the elemental realm—called the Ummahat, or Mothers—and generate it upon the earth. After their natural dissolution, their bodily forms decompose into the four elements, each returning to its proper center. Within the dominion of these heavens, minerals, plants, and animals were produced in their complete forms; yet the seed of humanity alone remained suspended, its essences gathered in the earthly realm.

| * | Saturn was commanded to produce minerals alone.
| --- | --- |
| * | Jupiter was commanded to produce both minerals and vegetation.
| * | Mars and all subsequent planets were commanded to produce minerals, vegetation, and animals.
| * | All the heavens were instructed to prepare human seed.

All offspring brought forth by these heavens were generated from the treasures of the celestial spheres. Thus in each category of creation, three types arose. For example, among minerals, there appeared the excellent minerals—components of those ⟪ar:نادمین، شاک و متحیر اور مصر و مستکبر⟫ who deny—the intermediate minerals ⟪ar:شاک و متحیرین⟫ (the doubters and perplexed), and the base minerals ⟪ar:مصر و مستکبرین⟫ (the arrogant and disdainful).

### Government of Saturn:

Before the generation of humanity, it was necessary first to create their sustenance: minerals, plants, and animals. For this ⟪ar:مدبر حکیم⟫ wise governor, Saturn was given the first dominion, initiating its solitary rule. Its method combined four phenomena that produced vapor—a form distinct from those four elements. As when water poured upon fire generates steam, a substance differing from both fire and water, so too did vapors accumulate into clouds, bringing forth torrential rains upon the earth. These rains, ⟪ar:غیر النفع⟫ harmful in their excess, inundated the entire terrestrial sphere. Everywhere lay frozen snow, and bitter cold prevailed. During Saturn's reign, mountains and trees were born. The sun's rays withdrew behind dark clouds, and the atmosphere grew murky. Since Saturn possesses a malevolent nature ⟪ar:نحس⟫—its function to bring ruin and to freeze—during this first millennium all things harsh and base were produced: iron, copper, lime, and stone. Filthy and saline waters covered the land, causing all manner of corruption.

## The Birth of Humanity from the Pits

When the Moon came to aid Saturn, the process of human generation commenced. This is because the Moon is the seventh heaven, holding a particular station in the ⟪ar:'خلق آخر'⟫ ultimate creation of humanity. At the beginning of each age, the same pits are born from ⟪ar:جثہ ابدائیۃ⟫ primordial bodies.

Over six thousand years, all lawful minerals, plants, and animals that had been generated died their lawful deaths. Besides these, from the essences of diverse fragrances and all other subtle things—and from the most rarefied, moderate, and pure fraction of fresh river water—water rose as vapor, and preparations commenced for the first manifestation of the highest elements of the deniers' category. From these vapors, clouds formed which, of their own accord, rained upon the exceedingly pure earth without external compulsion. The force of these rains carved potholes into the ground—craters neither very deep nor shallow.

*Flowers must go elsewhere; much fruit remains in the orchard still.*

## Two Types of Creation

The Divine has created two types of creation in this world. One emerges as vegetation from the earth, occurring at the beginning of each age; the other occurs through birth ⟪ar:'رحم مادر '⟫ from the maternal womb.

⟪ar:اشباح صوریۃ⟫ When these luminous forms appeared in dense state within the three gates, ⟪ar:تدبیر الٰہی⟫ divine governance required them to be scattered and dispersed throughout the heavens, the Ummahat, and the Saqqara, that they might be purified through examinations and trials—as gold is purified by fire, base matter removed through ordeal. After ⟪ar:مدبر حکیم⟫ this wise governor dispersed them, He created humanity by ⟪ar:قامت الفیۃ⟫ combining these scattered components. He employed two methods to bring them forth ⟪ar:قامت الفیۃ⟫ in their form.

### Birth from Pits:

The first method of birth is from the pit at the beginning of each age—the most excellent birth. The Divine says (interpretation of the meaning):

> ⟪quran 71:17⟫
> ⟪ar:‏وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًۭا ‎⟫
> *And Allah has brought you forth from the (dust of) earth. [Tafsir At-Tabarî, Vol.29, Page 97].*

It is stated in the facts that the Divine created ⟪ar:اشباح نورانی⟫ radiant forms in the ⟪ar:(قامت الفیۃ)⟫ form of humanity. Beings were born first, humanity afterward. The purpose of its description is that all the multitude gathered until the end shall evolve into human form. The rank of this ⟪ar:ھیکل⟫ human vessel shall accord with the order of appearances in this world. Those who climb last shall occupy the place of the sole of the foot. The Almighty created humanity from a state of being; now humanity must return to the ultimate state of selfhood. And it is then that liberation becomes possible.

### Birth from the Womb:

When the first creation was completed, He then ordained a second birth, resembling the first creation. The ingredients destined to be revealed in the world—scattered throughout minerals, plants, and animals—became ⟪ar:جثہ ابدائیۃ⟫ sustenance. This is why the Divine says (interpretation of the meaning):

> ⟪quran 23:12⟫
> ⟪ar:‏وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَنَ مِن سُلَلَةٍۢ مِّن طِينٍۢ ‎⟫
> *And indeed We created man (Adam) out of an extract of clay (water and earth).*

⟪ar:جثہ ابدائیۃ⟫ He gathered all subtle nutrients divided into flesh, blood, and the four natures—purity, melancholy, phlegm, and sanguinity—according to all their kinds. These foods were ⟪ar:جثہ ابدائیۃ⟫ the purest and most noble. He took the subtle from them and removed the base. This continued until the appointed time came for him and his wife's bodies to reunite. At that moment, the most subtle part of both emerged from their bodies and rose toward the brain, that the brain might sort and prepare it. The brain transformed it into thick white blood, drawn from all the body's organs—small and large, high and low. This white blood flowed to its source: the uterus in woman and the backbone in man. Through the act of marriage, the two were united by white blood, combining the four natures. Within all these natures lay a hidden, mysterious life ⟪ar:نفس نامیۃ⟫ known as ⟪ar:خمیرۃ ابدائیہ⟫ the primordial leaven, possessing ⟪ar:صورت نامیۃ⟫ the form of growth. ⟪ar:نفس نامیۃ⟫ This was concealed within the four natures as fire lies hidden in wood struck by lightning. That is, in the eternal realm, the essence of ⟪ar:(ناطقۃ، حسیۃ، نامیۃ)⟫ the rational, sensate, and vegetative soul is called in ⟪ar:خمیرۃ ابدائیہ⟫ this world the primordial leaven and is established by the ⟪ar:نطفہ⟫ sperm-drop.

When this sentence—this nature—had been moderated in temperament and permitted to appear, it proceeded to the clear, pure, and balanced place of its mother's womb. Four forces ⟪ar:(طالع، غارب، عاشر، رابع)⟫ worked to establish it—the ascendant, descendant, culmination, and foundation. It arrived in such a state as to be receptive, passive, and capable of accepting the influences soon to manifest within the womb. It came in the form of ⟪ar:ھیولی⟫ prime matter, so that ⟪ar:صورت⟫ form might be imprinted upon it by the Creator's influence. It proceeded through the ranks of creation as yogurt curdles into yogurt, and yogurt transforms into cheese.

*Life is the appearance of elements in order.*

*Death is the disturbance of these elements.*

Upon this, all the celestial spheres began to shine and exerted their influences, making it subtle until it became the essence of the radiance of the Kawakab—like the essence of milk. It became permeated by all four temperaments, and diverse natures began to form within this single nature. The first ⟪ar:'قلب '⟫ heart of this sperm was passive, just as it was the first to be active in ⟪ar:شمس⟫ the heavenly world. It conformed to the heart's ⟪ar:شمس⟫ nature—heat and moisture. The heart began to absorb this nature and became the center for the entire body. Then, one by one, all remaining organs began to become passive in turn.

The Kawakab, stationed in the palace of fathers, began to influence the body from the heavens, while the Ummahat, stationed in the palace of mothers, began to influence the mother's womb. Each organ had one ⟪ar:مُتَوَلِّی⟫ overseer among the Kawakab, from which it received influence. Whatever the mother consumed during pregnancy was dispersed as nourishment to her infant's organs. Each part of the child received its share by joining with its corresponding maternal organ. The child's hands received from the mother's hands; the child's heart from the mother's heart, and so forth. The heart supported the three organs above it and the three below, just as ⟪ar:شمس⟫ the Sun supports the three spheres ⟪ar:(زحل، مشتری، مریخ)⟫ above it and the three ⟪ar:(زہرہ، عطارد، قمر)⟫ below. ## The Heavens' Governance in the Formation of the Foetus

### Saturn: (First Month)

In the first month, the human sperm receives the influence of Saturn, for it is first among the heavens. The nature of this sphere is to coagulate. In the generation from pits, Saturn solidified the pit's boiling water and froze it, allowing the water to cease its boiling and emerge from the pit. Similarly, in the womb, it acts upon the sperm to coagulate it.

### Jupiter: (Second Month)

Then in the second month, Jupiter's governance commences. Since it is a beneficent sphere, it creates growth and increase of this ⟪ar:قوت نُمُو⟫ power of growth through its heat and moisture. All parts of the sperm gather together in the form of a blood clot. The power of growth awakened during Jupiter's month.

### Mars: (Third Month)

In the third month, Mars's governance begins—⟪ar:نحس⟫ a malevolent sphere. Through its warmth, it transforms it ⟪ar:علقۃ⟫ into clot-form and then into ⟪ar:مضغۃ⟫ lump-form. The heat of this sphere increases the power of growth and opens pathways in the form of pores for nutrition. In this month, the essential vital parts begin to appear. [^cite-7]

### The Sun: (Fourth Month)

In the ⟪ar:شمس⟫ fourth month, the Sun's governance begins. Since it is the king of the heavens, its attention focuses especially on the heart, the king of the human body. Under its influence, all ⟪ar:اعضاء رئیسۃ⟫ vital organs—especially the heart and brain that lay present in the lump-form ⟪ar:مضغۃ⟫—emerge and become active. The ⟪ar:نفس حسیۃ⟫ sensate soul emerges.

### Venus: (Fifth Month)

In the fifth month, Venus's governance commences—⟪ar:شمس⟫ a supremely delicate sphere. This sphere distinguishes male from female within the embryo. It reveals the features of eye and nose; the head protrudes between the two ears. In this month, all the fetus's bones become prepared.

### Mercury: (Sixth Month)

In the sixth month, Mercury's governance begins. In this month, flesh climbs upon the bones, and the hands and feet become quite prominent and fully separated. The fetus begins to perceive its location. It is able to open its mouth and move its lips, commencing to feel them with its tongue. In this month, the sense of sleep and wakefulness arises.

### The Moon: (Seventh Month)

In the seventh month, the Moon's governance begins, imparting the power of perception. In this month it ⟪ar:قامت الفیۃ⟫ achieves complete human form, and its ⟪ar:اعضاء رئیسۃ⟫ vital joints grow ever stronger. It begins to move constantly, sensing the narrowness of the womb and the desire to emerge from it.

### Saturn: (Eighth Month)

If there is no time for its emergence, the sperm remains in the mother's womb, and Saturn's governance reverses its effect upon it, which is ⟪ar:نحس الفلکی⟫ celestial malevolence. Its nature is coldness and dryness, the natures of death. In this month, the effect of gravity ⟪ar:کشش سقل⟫ upon the embryo becomes very strong. If the embryo is born in this month, Saturn freezes it through its misfortune, and the child dies.

### Jupiter: (Ninth Month)

If the child remains in the mother's womb until the ninth month, then Jupiter's governance begins—⟪ar:سعد اکبر⟫ the greater beneficence. Its function is heat and softness, the natures of life. In this month, the fetus's movement increases greatly. This movement becomes voluntary, triggering contractions in the womb. In the ninth month, Jupiter enters the Pisces constellation, which assures the embryo's birth.

---

The existence of these voluntary movements of the soul depends upon the conditions surrounding it. When conditions become corrupted, that soul separates. When the newborn emerges from its mother's narrow womb and becomes one ⟪ar:شخص کامل⟫ complete human being in the vastness of the earth, the ⟪ar:شعاء الشمس⟫ rays of the Sun become even more ⟪ar:قوت حسیۃ⟫ awakened as sensate power, emerging ⟪ar:بالفعل⟫ in actuality. ⟪ar:شمس⟫ The Sun, heart of the heavens, is the center of the other ⟪ar:نفوس حسیہ⟫ sensate souls, just as the Moon is the center of the ⟪ar:نفوس نامیۃ⟫ vegetative souls of the heavens. Its ⟪ar:قوت حسیۃ⟫ sensate power spreads through the newborn's body and creates movement within it. Then ⟪ar:قوت حسیۃ⟫ sensate power and ⟪ar:قوت نامیۃ⟫ vegetative power combine to form a new integrated power. From this union, the newborn begins to breathe ⟪ar:کرہ نسیم⟫ the sphere of air-breath, which becomes sustenance for his ⟪ar:قوت حسیۃ⟫ sensate power and his ⟪ar:قوت نامیۃ⟫ vegetative power.

## The Stages of Foetal Formation

The Qur'an describes the seven stages of foetal birth:

> ⟪quran 23:12-14⟫
> ⟪ar:‏وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَنَ مِن سُلَلَةٍۢ مِّن طِينٍۢ ‎ ‏ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَهُ نُطْفَةًۭ فِى قَرَارٍۢ مَّكِينٍۢ ‎ ‏ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا ٱلنُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةًۭ فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةًۭ فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْمُضْغَةَ عِظَمًۭا فَكَسَوْنَا ٱلْعِظَمَ لَحْمًۭا ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ ۚ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ ٱلْخَلِقِينَ ‎⟫
> *And indeed We created man (Adam) out of an extract of clay (water and earth). Thereafter We made him (the offspring of Adam) as a Nutfah (mixed drops of the male and female sexual discharge) (and lodged it) in a safe lodging (womb of the woman). Then We made the Nutfah into a clot (a piece of thick coagulated blood), then We made the clot into a little lump of flesh, then We made out of that little lump of flesh bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh, and then We brought it forth as another creation. So blessed be Allah, the Best of creators.*

| Salalah (سلالہ) | The substance that dwells in the father's loins and the mother's womb before fertilization takes place. The components of manifestation are scattered throughout the world; the subtle essence is fixed upon the father's backbone and in the mother's womb, which is called Salalah.
| --- | --- |
| Sperm-drop (نطفہ) | When these two substances unite and the two fluids mingle in the mother's womb, fertilization occurs and the sperm-drop is formed.
| Lump (مضغۃ) | This sperm-drop receives nourishment and takes the form of a lump, called a mudghah.
| Clot (علقۃ) | The structure of this lump before the bones are formed is called the clot. ⟪ar:'علاَّقۃ '⟫ In Arabic, it is named 'adhering one' or 'hanging one.'
| Bones (عظام) | Within this structure lies a shell of bones, called bones.
| Flesh (لحم) | The flesh that climbs upon these bones is called meat.
| Another Creation (خلق آخر) | When the child emerges from the mother's womb, the soul is breathed into it. A six-month-old fetus can be born because the soul is breathed at the end of the sixth month—at the beginning of the seventh—when it is able to receive sensation. The remaining two months are devoted to the infant's growth. If it even slightly sneezes at the time of birth, it receives sensation; if it does not sneeze, it receives none, and the child is born lifeless.

⟪ar:نفس نامیۃ⟫ The vegetative soul is divided into four elements (fire, air, water, earth) which are placed under the sphere of the Moon. In the fourth month, the heart moves—that is, three chambers form in the heart and it commences its beating. When the eighth month begins, Saturn exerts its effect again; Saturn renders the child dead, so the child born in the eighth month is born dead. But the ninth month is Jupiter's, and the infant is born healthy. Here only the soul's status remains, and therefore its virtue is greater. [^cite-8]

In this way, the seven Spheres and their influences come one after another, and the Mahdi, the successor of the Qaim, stands opposite the soul. Though the infant is ready in seven months, it yet takes another two months to be born. These two months represent the equivalent of the heavenly world and the constellation sphere—the universe of the boundaries and limits.

### Regarding This Embryo, Sayyidina al-Muʾayyad Says:

If only you knew why you were drawn forth from the powers of the heavens and bodies, and why you were placed in a narrow and confined space, and then brought out of the narrowness of the world.

This points to the sperm-drop that adjoins it—the ⟪ar:نفس نامیۃ⟫ vegetative soul—which has been extracted from ⟪ar:نفس نامیۃ موالید ثلاثۃ (معدن، نبات، حیوان)⟫ the three births: minerals, plants, and animals. These ⟪ar:موالید ثلاثۃ⟫ three births were drawn from the four Ummahat—fire, air, water, and earth—which are the forces of the heavens. Then He created within you an inner reality, whose signs are hidden in the heavens and the earth. This refers to your ⟪ar:قوت حسیۃ⟫ sensate power, which connects to the newborn at the moment of birth. When an infant emerges from its mother's womb, its life and death, its joy and sorrow, its wealth and poverty, its fame and ignominy, all lie beneath the influence of the stars and the heavens. Yet the command of the Creator—the Originator and Master of all the heavens and stars in His majesty and glory—transcends all celestial influences! All these heavens, stars, and planets are subject to His command and obey His every decree.

## The Senses and the Powers of the Brain

Those parts of the body that are firm and solid are called ⟪ar:'اعضا '⟫ organs; those that are in the form of vaporous essences—very subtle, pure, and transparent—arising from these four qualities and pervading the body are ⟪ar:'مزاجات '⟫ temperaments; and the subtle substance itself is ⟪ar:'روح حیوانی '⟫ the animal soul.

| Solid | Intermediate | Subtle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Organs | Temperaments | Animal Soul |

This soul originates at the animal place—the heart—and spreads through the passages of the mind. Then it passes through the eye-sockets, ear-canals, tongue-cavities, and extends to all ⟪ar:رئیس و اسفل⟫ superior and inferior organs, finally reaching the toes. This soul invests the entire body as hands invest themselves in gloves.

The human body possesses five external powers: ⟪ar:لمس، ذائقۃ، بو، سماعت اور بصر⟫ touch, taste, smell, hearing, and sight. Of these, ⟪ar:لمس، ذائقۃ، بو⟫ the three—touch, taste, and smell—develop within the womb. The remaining two ⟪ar:سماعت وبصر⟫ hearing and sight—are created when the infant emerges from the womb. Corresponding to these five external senses are ⟪ar:حواس مشترکۃ، مصورۃ، مفکرۃ، وہمیۃ اور حافظۃ⟫ five internal senses: the common sense, the imaginative power, the thinking power, the estimative power, and the faculty of retention. All these senses exist in the fetus ⟪ar:بالقوۃ⟫ in potentiality before its birth and begin to manifest ⟪ar:بالفعل⟫ in actuality at their appointed times after birth, culminating in ⟪ar:نفس ناطقۃ مجازی⟫ the metaphorical rational soul.

| Order | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | Sense |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| External | Touch | Smell | Taste | Hearing | Sight | Power of Sensation |
| Internal | Common | Imaginative | Reflective | Estimative | Retentive | Power of Intellection |

The common sense dwells in the foremost part of the brain. It is called 'common' because every corporeal power flows through it, and every faculty resembles this intellect in some way. All that the eye sees, the ear hears, the hand touches, the tongue tastes, the nose smells—all these sensations originate in the mind. This part of the brain is therefore called ⟪ar:'مخزن صور محسوسات '⟫ the repository of sensible forms.

⟪ar:قوت تخیل⟫ The imaginative power dwells in another part of the brain. When this power serves and aids the intellect, it is called ⟪ar:قوت مفکرۃ⟫ the reflective power. When its attention turns toward bodily desires and gives rise to supposition and conjecture, it is called ⟪ar:قوت متخیلۃ⟫ the imaginative power. When ⟪ar:متخیلۃ⟫ the imaginative power is activated, the intellect stores this thought in the third part of the brain, which is ⟪ar:قوت حافظۃ⟫ called the retentive power. ⟪ar:تخمینۃ⟫ The estimative power resides in the fourth part of the brain, in the middle of the head. ⟪ar:قوت حافظۃ⟫ Retention is positioned in the back of the brain, storing every ⟪ar:شبیح⟫ form-impression that ⟪ar:متخیلۃ⟫ the imagination transmits to it. ⟪ar:قوت متذکرۃ⟫ The recollective power retrieves ⟪ar:شبیح⟫ such impressions when required. ⟪ar:حافظۃ⟫ Retention preserves all bodily impressions and sensations. This power exists in humans and animals and continues to function as long as the four temperaments maintain equilibrium in the body. Yet by reason of the eternal nature of the soul, ⟪ar:متخیلۃ⟫ a portion of the imagination always remains intact and never perishes.

⟪ar:'عقل '⟫ The intellect is like a postmaster to whom messengers bring news and letters concerning various events, which he then arranges and organizes. ⟪ar:'متخیلۃ '⟫ The imagination is like his secretary, to whom he gives letters to place in the bag. ⟪ar:'متذکرۃ '⟫ Recollection is like the king, to whom ⟪ar:متخیلۃ⟫ imagination delivers all letters so that he might read them and derive benefit or harm from them. The king then hands these letters—these thoughts—to his treasurer, ⟪ar:حافظۃ⟫ retention, to be safely stored in the treasury. ⟪ar:مفکرۃ⟫ Reflection is the king's official, who can retrieve those letters—those memories—from the treasury whenever he wishes, at the king's command.

## Humanity as the Quintessence of the Universe

⟪ar:صاحب رسائل اخوان الصفا⟫ The author of the Epistles of the Brethren of Purity explains that ⟪ar:'عالم'⟫ the world refers to the seven heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them. They also call it ⟪ar:'انسان الکبیر '⟫ the Macrocosm or Great Human. This is because, like humanity, the world itself possesses a body with distinct organs. This world also possesses a soul whose powers flow through its organs. A human soul produces effects upon its body; the manifestations of this single effect appear in diverse forms. The tongue speaks, the eyes see, the ears hear, the feet walk—each organ displays its particular function.

From the circumference of the heavens to the center of the Saqqara, this world is itself a body—or a human being—which is called ⟪ar:'عالم الکبیر'⟫ the Universal World or Macrocosm. There dwells within it a ⟪ar:نفس کل⟫ Universal Soul which exerts its influence upon this vast body. Different parts of the ⟪ar:عالم الکبیر⟫ Universal World receive this ⟪ar:نفس کل⟫ influence in accordance with their receptivity and capacity, and from this their various natures emerge. For example, the soul's effect is manifested as motion in the heavens, but as rest in the earth. This ⟪ar:نفس کل⟫ Universal Soul creates mingling in the Ummahat (the elemental mothers) and stasis in minerals. It manifests as growth in plants and sensation in animals. In humanity, it manifests as reason and discernment. For this reason, the Almighty is described as "Creator of the Heavens, Dweller upon the Earth, Stillness of Minerals, Growth of Plants, and Life-Giver to Animals." [^cite-9]

The hierarchy illustrates the order of creation descending from the Mover (muḥarrik), through the concentric heavens, down through the elemental mothers and the four categories of being—mineral, plant, animal, and human—to the Universal Body.

The heavens and the moon-sphere above it are perfect in their essence and goodness; their perfection flows forth as ⟪ar:تشبیح⟫ glorification. ⟪ar:'انسان کلی'⟫ The Universal or Perfect Human represents this celestial perfection. In contrast, in the lower realm beneath the moon's sphere, where good and evil mingle, there appears ⟪ar:'انسان جزوی'⟫ the Particular or Imperfect Human. Humanity is created between these two and thus receives influence from both. ⟪ar:انسان کلی وانسان جزوی⟫ The Particular Human is created from the lower celestial realm, ⟪ar:انسان کلی، انسان جزوی⟫ just as those lower realms are created from the heavens. These lower domains remain perpetually subject to the heavens and receive their influences continuously.

⟪ar:صاحب رسائل⟫ It is said by the authors of the Epistles that the Ummahat (elemental mothers) appeared after the heavens; minerals came after the Ummahat; plants came after minerals; animals came after plants; and humanity came after animals. This series is not confined to any single epoch; rather, these emanations continue to occur in the same order perpetually. Minerals continue to become plants; plants continue to become animals; and animals continue to manifest in human form. Yet after becoming human, there is no further progress into any other form. The reason is that humanity is the essence and quintessence of these three—minerals, plants, and animals. Once returned to the original state of perfection, there is no further necessity to transform into any other form.

A perfect human being who has attained the original purpose of his birth and whose development is complete—this is the reason the Divine did not create any creature after humanity, for humanity is the perfect embodiment of the mineral, plant, and animal realms, and the true and ultimate purpose of their generation. The principal purpose of minerals, plants, and animals is to evolve and manifest in human form. Once humanity is achieved, there is no need to advance into any other form. This is why humanity is the link and the bond. ⟪ar:موالید ثلاثۃ⟫ These three births—minerals, plants, and animals—depend upon humanity's existence, and humanity makes use of all three for its sustenance and continued life.
